author: Jesse Staniforth
title: PQ’s Sonia Caron to take power in Quebec’s largest riding
content:
After 12 years, the Parti Québécois’s Sonia Caron succeeded in turning the northern Quebec electoral riding of Ungava back to the PQ’s bright blue in the Oct. 5 election.


Caron was born and still lives in Chibougamau — eight hours north of Montreal, near the Cree Nation of Mistissini — and told APTN News in a French interview that she hopes to become an advocate for all those living in the North.


“I represent the Parti Québécois, of course, because it reflects my values,” she told APTN, “but my primary interest is in advocating for the North in Quebec City and being the best possible advocate for the people I work with. It’s important to convey our needs to the government, so that both sides can understand how we can move forward together to be more effective and determine which needs to address first.”


At a towering 855,164 square kilometres, the Quebec electoral riding of Ungava is one of the largest electoral ridings in Canada, eclipsed only by the federal ridings of Nunavut and the Northwest Territories, each of which consists of a whole territory.


Ungava is larger than the entirety of France, but according to Elections Quebec, its population is only 45,740, of whom 30,773 are eligible to vote. These residents are spread widely across the riding, which contains all 14 communities of the Inuit region of Nunavik (roughly 13,000 people) and all nine communities of the Cree Nation of Eeyou Istchee (roughly 20,000 members). The riding also includes non-Indigenous population centres like Chibougaumau, Lebel-sur-Quévillon, Matagami and Chapais, which add up to roughly 14,000 more.


Only 8,516 people voted in Ungava on Oct. 5 — a voter turnout of 27.61 per cent — and Caron won a plurality with 3,272 votes.


A teacher and principal who began her career in Inukjuak before returning to Chibougaumau to start a family, Caron said she’s interested in determining which issues in the North are poorly understood in Quebec City and need greater advocacy, while working with Cree and Inuit leaders to address their needs as well.


“I’m very aware that I represent three different entities within the same territory,” she said. “Whether it’s services for seniors, mental health, access to quality education, for me, it’s simply a matter of bringing everyone together around the same table.”


Experience and intentions


Caron has worked in elementary and high schools, but over the last ten years she’s been the principal of a vocational school. Over that same time, she said, she has been on several boards of directors, including those of Quebec National Mining Institute, the Assembly of Partners of the Société du Plan Nord and the Regional Council of Labor Market Partners, where she sat with Cree and Inuit representatives.


“I’ve been deeply involved in labor issues, health, education and the mining and forestry sectors, thanks to the training programs we offer at our center,” she said. “So I thought to myself, why not go out and help people understand and become aware of the real issues facing the North?”


After decades in school administration while also working with government agencies and state-owned corporations, Caron said she feels she’s developed a clear picture of how government works and how to make it operate more effectively.


“My background in education and leadership also leads me to always analyze the root causes of an issue,” she said, “or dig deeper to address the problem at its source. Sure, sometimes it takes longer, but when you focus on the right drivers of change, it can lead to a lot of positive outcomes.”


That experience also gave her the opportunity, she said, to figure out how to work efficiently across the enormity of Ungava’s geography.


“Often, we’re cut off by air travel, waterways, or roads that can be treacherous in winter,” she said. “But we’ve always worked remotely—even here at the James Bay School Service Center. Having a physical office is important, but I’ll be a grassroots representative whom people can reach out to regularly to keep me informed about the issues and how they’re evolving.”


Caron said she bristles at the idea that “there are few of us spread across a vast territory,” arguing instead that people who live in the region know it best.


“My vision will be shaped in collaboration with First Nations and Inuit communities, as well as with the people of James Bay,” she said. “Quebec cannot function without the North. So I want to give the North the importance it deserves — …

author: Nahuel Lag
title: Mucha tierra en muy pocas manos: un plan para favorecer a las grandes empresas globales
content:
Por Nahuel Lag 


La decisión del gobierno de Javier Milei de buscar estrategias jurídicas —DNU 70/2023, Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada— para derogar la Ley de Tierras y la decisión de la Corte Suprema de validar la derogación sin revisar su constitucionalidad, no son un fenómeno aislado. Carlos Duarte, relator por América Latina del Grupo de Trabajo de la Declaración de las Naciones Unidas sobre los Derechos de los Campesinos (Undrop, por sus siglas en inglés), lo identifica dentro de una “arquitectura jurídica transnacional que se difunde por mimetismo legislativo y presión multilateral” en el informe

“Contrarreformas agrarias: anatomía de un despojo en progreso”

. 


El trabajo da un a

nálisis minucioso, con particular foco en América Latina, en el que establece cuatro lógicas contemporáneas de despojo

 que se repiten en todos los continentes: ingeniería legal,

financiarización, acaparamiento verde y el rol del Estado como promotor corporativo

. El objetivo: avanzar sobre las tierras campesinas, indígenas y de pequeños productores para trastocar el derecho de acceso a la tierra y ponerla al servicio de los intereses corporativos.  


El informe, publicado este año, continúa actualizándose de manera vertiginosa en los últimos meses ante cada nuevo paso de los sectores políticas de la derecha regional: el

debate del capítulo de tierras en la Argentina

, el

decreto de “fortalecimiento del agronegocio” en la Honduras

 del presidente Nasry Asfura y

la Colombia del flamante mandatario Abelardo de la Espriella

, cuya primera acción fue prohibir la palabra “campesino” en documentos oficiales.    


“

Con la llegada de gobiernos de ultra derecha hay un proceso muy agresivo

 de intentar romper todas las salvaguardas sobre la propiedad de la tierra y reinterpretar los marcos regulatorios para generar procesos de concentración”, sentencia Duarte en diálogo con Tierra Viva y contrapone que el problema tampoco logró pasar de

tímidos reformismos durante los gobiernos progresistas

 por la imposibilidad de romper con las élites terratenientes.  


Foto: Luciana Fernández


Seguir concentrando lo ya concentrado


América Latina, advierte Duarte, es el laboratorio primordial de estas estrategias que tienen como objetivo pasar de “la tierra como base material de proyectos de vida” a “su consolidación definitiva como un simple activo financiero líquido” y como consecuencia la

“concentración acelerada, desplazamiento de los sujetos vulnerables y ruptura del relevo generacional campesino”

.


Al contextualizar esta arquitectura jurídica global, el profesor e investigador del Instituto de Estudios Interculturales Javeriana de Cali (Colombia) contrapone llamamientos a la redistribución de la tierra como la

Declaración de Derechos Campesinos

, en 2018, y los acuerdos alcanzados en la última

Conferencia Internacional sobre Reforma Agraria y Desarrollo Rural

 (Ciradr+20) con un mundo en regresión normativa y en proceso de concentración. El dato más reciente del informe “La situación de la tenencia de la tierra y la gobernanza” —publicado por la FAO, la Coalición Internacional por la Tierra y el Cirad— ubicó la distribución de la tierra entre países en un 0,95 en el coeficiente de Gini, siendo 1 el mayor nivel de concentración. 


Tres datos permiten realizar un repaso rápido de cómo esa situación se refleja en la Argentina. Según el informe

"Los señores de la tierra"

 —FIAN Internacional y Focus on the Global South, 2025—,

diez terratenientes transnacionales controlan 40 millones de hectáreas y tres de ellos operan en Argentina: Arauco, Benetton y Cresud

. Según datos del Registro de Tierras —creado por la Ley en disputa—, el

Observatorio de Tierras

 señaló que Argentina el cinco por ciento de la tierra está en manos extranjeros y en 36 municipios con recursos estratégicos superan hasta el 50 por ciento. Según el

Censo Nacional Agropecuario 2018

,

el 55 por ciento de las chacras solo tiene el dos por ciento de la tierra y el uno por ciento de las grandes explotaciones agropecuarias controla el 36 por ciento de la tierra

. 


La ingeniería legal para los negocios corporativos con la tierra 


El trabajo de “Contrarreformas agrarias” del relator de la Undrop toma dimensión para entender qué lugar ocupa la Argentina en un proceso de orden mundial. De las cuatro lógicas de despojo descritas en su trabajo, el Decreto 70/2023 es uno de los mayores ejemplos de la primera de ellas: la “ingeniería …

author: CMI Argentina
title: La oposición en Diputados convocó a excombatientes para darles voz por el proyecto del gobierno sobre Malvinas
content:
Después de que el gobierno enviara a la secretaria legal y técnica a defender el proyecto de Ley de Defensa de Soberanía Nacional, el peronismo convocó a organizaciones de ex combatientes. La sesión del 15 de octubre por la Ley de Tierras y las maniobras oficialistas.


Por Verónica Benaim @VeBenaim


 


La agenda Malvinas copó toda la semana legislativa en la Cámara de Diputados de la Nación. El día

después de la presentación de María Ibarzabal Murphy

, funcionaria clave del gobierno de Javier Milei, el peronismo abrió este jueves la Comisión de Asuntos Cooperativos, Mutuales y ONG para darle voz a representantes de organizaciones de excombatientes de Malvinas en el marco del debate sobre el proyecto de ley de Defensa de la Soberanía Nacional.


Mientras el oficialismo prepara una estrategia para desactivar la sesión convocada por la oposición para la semana que viene, que tiene como fin principal voltear el DNU 70/23 que deroga la ley de venta de tierras rurales a extranjeros, el diputado de Unión por la Patria, Aldo Leiva, convocó a un batallón de representantes de asociaciones civiles nucleadas en la Mesa de Coincidencia Malvinas (MECOMA). Y es que, tras el fallo de la Corte Suprema, el peronismo buscar sumar rechazos a la decisión judicial por facilitar la extranjerización de tierras nacionales.


Del encuentro, que tuvo una fuerte presencia de dirigentes y expertos de Malvinas de la provincia de Buenos Aires -sobre todo de la ciudad de La Plata- participó el diputado Máximo Kirchner que no forma parte de la comisión y que suele participar de las actividades cotidianas del parlamento.


Los que estuvieron ausentes fueron los diputados del bloque de La Libertad Avanza que, según pudo saber Tiempo, tomaron la reunión como una forma de “oportunismo político” por parte de los opositores. Es más, enviaron una carta, en donde expresaron su rechazo al encuentro bajo el argumento de que “se propuso un temario que no se condice con la comisión. Se desvirtúa el objeto de una comisión permanente de esta Cámara”.


Durante el encuentro,

Tiempo

 dialogó con Leiva quien explicó los motivos de la convocatoria. “En mi doble rol como diputado y veterano de Malvinas, creemos que estamos viendo una situación muy compleja donde la Corte dice que el planteo de una de nuestras organizaciones es ilegitima, y por otra parte en lo que se viene debatiendo del proyecto enviado por el gobierno ha habido muchas limitaciones para escuchar nuestras voces por lo que creemos oportuno hacer esta convocatoria para escucharnos y generar propuestas”.


El diputado y veterano de Malvinas, Aldo Leiva.


Ante la consulta sobre qué le dejo la defensa que hizo Ibarzabal, la secretaria de Legal y Técnica de la Casa Rosada, respondió que fue “insulsa”. “Ha sido pésimo, nos faltan el respeto al no venir responsables como el canciller (Pablo Quirno), pero este gobierno rehúye al debate y pretende llevarnos de las narices a votar algo que nada tiene que ver con Malvinas, sólo un tercio se refiere a la cuestión Malvinas y el resto se nos quiere meter por la ventana”.


De todas formas, detalló que para Unión por la Patria se debe dar el debate, aunque fragmentando el tratamiento del proyecto de ley con el fin de desvincular el endurecimiento de las penas relativas a Malvinas de los artículos referidos a la seguridad interior y modificaciones en los servicios de inteligencia.


El excombatiente, escritor y periodista, Edgardo Esteban.


La sesión del 15 y las maniobras oficialistas


En paralelo al desarrollo de la reunión de la comisión convocada por el mayor bloque opositor al Gobierno, circuló que la Libertad Avanza prepara una convocatoria de comisiones para el miércoles a las 16 con el fin de revivir el proyecto de ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada que aprobó el Senado. Es el día anterior de la sesión convocada por los opositores. La estrategia del bloque violeta es incluir en ese proyecto un apartado de Ley de Tierras y convencer a los legisladores provinciales que están en duda de no dar quorum al día siguiente.


Frente a este escenario, la diputada camporista Paula Penacca manifestó: “Nos van a querer engañar y confundir. Desde hoy hasta el jueves 15, ellos van a intentar confundir. El miércoles que viene van a querer poner en tratamiento la sanción del proyecto de inviolabilidad privada que viene del Senado y que fue el que logramos hacer pelota el 6 de agosto porque era en contra de la soberanía y a favor de los grandes intereses …

author: Gustavo Faleiros
title: Com Flávio, o Brasil pode virar um grande garimpo
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a newsletter Ligando os pontos, enviada toda quinta-feira. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui

.


O amor da família Bolsonaro pelo garimpo não é novidade.

 Ficou famosa a frase de Jair Bolsonaro de que ele mesmo gostava de “faiscar”, de pegar uma bateia e sair em busca de pepitas de ouro. Porém, essa visão romântica de como funciona a mineração não ajudou a esconder os enormes danos causados pela ilegalidade garimpeira nos quatro anos de sua gestão.


Dados da plataforma independente

Amazon Mining Watch revelam que, durante o governo Bolsonaro

, a velocidade de crescimento dos garimpos foi exorbitante.

No início de 2019, quando se tornou presidente, o monitoramento por imagens de satélite mostrava que existiam 201,5 mil hectares de áreas de mineração de ouro na Amazônia. Quatro anos depois, já eram 401,5 mil hectares, uma área igual a 3,3 vezes a cidade do Rio de Janeiro e 92% maior que no início do governo.


Para fins de comparação, a mesma ferramenta, que utiliza inteligência artificial para analisar imagens Sentinel-2 com resolução de 10 metros, indica que,

durante o governo de Lula 3, a taxa de crescimento foi bem menor – 24,3%

, elevando o total de áreas de garimpo na Amazônia a 499 mil hectares até a metade desde ano.

Este resultado coincide com o aumento de ações de fiscalização durante a gestão petista.

 A repressão ocorreu principalmente em áreas de mineração nas terras indígenas e pela apreensão de máquinas usadas pelos criminosos ambientais.


Durante o governo de Bolsonaro, foram muitas as evidências de que os garimpeiros ilegais tinham portas abertas nos gabinetes de Brasília.

 Uma investigação do The Intercept

revelou gravações nas quais Eduardo Bim, então presidente do Ibama

, órgão que deve zelar pela proteção ao meio ambiente, pedia para fiscais aliviarem a barra de uma empresa investigada por falsificar lavras de extração de ouro. 


Essas evidências, de que os interesses escusos estão intimamente conectados ao clã Bolsonaro, foram reforçadas na semana passada com uma

reportagem da Agência Pública


mostrando que um dos chefões dos garimpos na Terra Indígena Yanomami, em Roraima, foi um dos articuladores da fuga para os Estados Unidos de Alexandre Ramagem, o diretor da Agência Brasileira de Inteligência (Abin) durante a gestão Bolsonaro. Foragido da justiça

, Ramagem está condenado a 16 anos de prisão por participação na trama golpista. 


Já faz mais de uma década que os arautos da extrema direita gostam de “lacrar” dizendo que o Brasil governado pelos candidatos de esquerda, como Lula e Dilma, estava a um passo de se tornar a Venezuela. Uma grande fake news: nada do que ocorreu aqui nas últimas duas décadas se compara com os sofrimentos causados pelos erros do chavismo no país vizinho. Aqui não houve mudança na Constituição para acabar com o limite de mandatos presidenciais. As eleições foram respeitadas e sempre aferidas por observadores transparentes. A autonomia entre os poderes segue preservada.


Mas é no tema da soberania sobre seus recursos naturais onde, infelizmente, Brasil e Venezuela estão se aproximando cada vez mais.

 A invasão promovida na Venezuela por Trump para impor um governo subserviente aos interesses dos Estados Unidos gerou uma nova corrida pelo ouro e minérios daquele país.

A atual presidente, Delcy Rodríguez, tem se mostrado pródiga em deixar a exploração de petróleo e ouro nas mãos do governo norte-americano

 – em 18 de setembro, por exemplo,

o Financial Times noticiou que  31 toneladas em barras de ouro

 estavam sendo negociadas para serem transferidas da Venezuela para o Banco Central dos EUA.


Isso ocorre exatamente no momento em que operações do exército venezuelano, com ajuda militar norte-americana, tentam dominar a atuação de grupos ilegais no

Arco Mineral do Orinoco,

 uma grande zona mineira criada em 2016 por Nicolás Maduro com o objetivo de gerar novas receitas para seu regime autoritário. Nunca deu certo, pois as minas de ouro foram sempre controladas pelos chamados “sindicatos”, organizações infra-legais atuando em conluio com militares corruptos.


Até o momento, as ações de repressão também não estão funcionando. Como mostrou o site de notícias Armando.info,

os grupos criminais continuam hackeando o sistema

 e contrabandeando ouro ilegal para dentro do mercado norte-americano. Na verdade, mais do que isso:

a Venezuela se tornou um hub de …

author: anred
title: Río Negro: la Cámara de Bariloche confirmó el desalojo de la Lof Inalef y la comunidad anuncia que seguirá resistiendo
content:
La Cámara de Apelaciones en lo Civil de Bariloche confirmó la sentencia que ordena el desalojo de la Lof Inalef, en la Rinconada de Inalef, paraje Mallín Ahogado, Río Negro. «Informamos que la Cámara de Apelaciones en lo Civil de Bariloche ha dictado un fallo desfavorable para nuestro Lof. Se confirmó la sentencia anterior y sigue en pie el pedido de desalojo sobre nuestro territorio», informó la comunidad este miércoles 7 de octubre. La comunidad denunció, además, falencias en su primera defensa técnica y anunció que continuarán apelando y sosteniendo la permanencia territorial: «esto no termina acá. Seguiremos con los recursos y acciones que correspondan, defendiendo nuestra permanencia en el territorio». El nuevo fallo se produce en un escenario de creciente conflictividad territorial en la Patagonia y días después de que la Corte Suprema reactivara la derogación de la Ley de Tierras Rurales impulsada por el gobierno de Javier Milei.

Por ANRed.


La

Lof Inalef vuelve a quedar frente a una orden de desalojo

 sobre un territorio que reivindica como ancestral, luego de que la

Cámara de Apelaciones en lo Civil de Bariloche confirmó la sentencia que ordena el desalojo del territorio mapuche ubicado


en la Rinconada de Inalef, paraje Mallín Ahogado, El Bolsón, Río Negro.


La comunidad informó este miércoles 7 de octubre que recibió un nuevo revés judicial y cuestionó tanto la decisión como el desempeño de la primera defensa técnica: «informamos que la Cámara de Apelaciones en lo Civil de Bariloche ha dictado un fallo desfavorable para nuestro Lof.

Se confirmó la sentencia anterior y sigue en pie el pedido de desalojo sobre nuestro territorio»

, comunicaron desde la Lof Inalef, que anticipó que continuará recurriendo la resolución: «esto no termina acá.

Seguiremos con los recursos y acciones que correspondan, defendiendo nuestra permanencia en el territorio

«.


El conflicto tiene antecedentes de larga data. En mayo de este año, la jueza

Paola Bernardini

 había dictado una

sentencia de desalojo en favor de Juan Lux Auroux

, mientras en otra causa

el exintendente de El Bolsón Félix Argentino Merino había obtenido una resolución similar sobre tierras de la familia Inalef

. La comunidad sostiene que se trata de un territorio ancestral y que distintos procesos judiciales desconocen esa historia.


Foto del aniversario de el Bolsón del 28 de enero del 2026. Se lo ve al gobernador Alberto Weretilneck, al intendente Bruno Pogliano y el hijo de Félix Argentino Merino, el abanderado.


La propia documentación judicial incorpora antecedentes sobre esa ocupación: en la causa vinculada a Auroux consta que

el Consejo de Desarrollo de Comunidades Indígenas (CODECI) reconoció en 2018 la conformación de la Lof Inalef y tuvo por acreditada “la posesión ancestral, tradicional, actual y pública” sobre tierras de sus abuelos José Antonio Inalef y María Antonia Leviu, registradas por el Estado desde 1907

. El expediente también señala que la tramitación del relevamiento territorial de la Comunidad Newenche, de la que forma parte la Lof Inalef, se inició en 2012.


El comunicado de este miércoles cuestiona además la actuación de quienes ejercieron inicialmente la representación legal de la comunidad: «sabemos cómo está jugando la política hoy en día. Además,

la primera defensa técnica presentó graves falencias no incluyó nuestros testigos ni nuestras pruebas y no ejerció la defensa en etapas clave

«, denunciaron. En este marco,

la Lof anunció que continuará utilizando las herramientas judiciales disponibles y convocó a las comunidades y organizaciones que históricamente acompañaron su lucha

.


El antecedente reciente muestra que esa red de solidaridad ya tuvo una expresión concreta en junio de este año, cuando la Lof Inalef convocó a un trawn frente a la amenaza de desalojo y recibió el

acompañamiento de comunidades mapuche, organizaciones de derechos humanos, sindicatos, movimientos sociales y organizaciones ambientales de la Comarca Andina

. Entre otras, acompañaron Lof Coronado-Inalef, Lof Pu Huayteka, Lof Che Buenuleo, Lof Quemquemtrew, la APDH, la CTA, organizaciones docentes y asambleas ambientales.


La disputa territorial se encuentra además atravesada por una historia de violencia:

en agosto de 2024, Juan Carlos Villa fue asesinado a tiros por un efectivo de la Policía de Río Negro durante un operativo en la zona de Rinconada de Inalef y su hijo Emanuel resultó gravemente herido

. La Coordinadora del …

author: Esperanza
title: Comunidad Temulemu vuelve a la Corte Interamericana de Derechos Humanos por el caso de su werken Rafael Pichun Collonao
content:
La comunidad Temulemu interpondrá una demanda ante la Comisión Interamericana de Derechos Humanos, por el caso de su werken Rafael Pichun Collonao, privado de libertad en la cárcel de Angol desde abril del 2024, condenado a 7 y 8 años de cárcel por su supuesta “participación organizativa” en el llamado caso Quilleco.


Según el Lonco Juan Pichun, el estado de Chile vulnera su propia legislación y lo que hoy vive su hermano Rafael repite lo que vivió su padre en la CIDH por el caso lonkos, en el año 2013:


“Hoy en día no sólo se vulneran los derechos Mapuches, el mismo estado a través de los poderes judiciales, a través de los persecutores, están vulnerando los mismos derechos que el estado ha impulsado y legislado, y en ese marco creemos que es importante llevar el caso de Rafael como un caso donde se vulneran varios derechos, como por ejemplo los derechos a la defensa, con el uso de testigos secretos, sin rostro.


Es una discriminación por parte del estado, dentro de sus mismos contextos jurídicos, ellos mismos han vulnerado su propia legislación.


Esta es la segunda vez que llevaremos un caso de la familia a un contexto internacional. Ya el estado de Chile fue condenado, y Rafael es parte de ese fallo de la CIDH, en el llamado caso lonkos, donde mi padre pudo lograr su inocencia a través de este tribunal internacional y eso mismo queremos acreditar, que en la acusación que le hacen a Rafael se vulneran también los derechos a una defensa”.


El werken rafael Pichun fue condenado en el denominado caso Quilleco, proceso judicial donde se presentó como única prueba un mensaje de whatsapp que el Werkén recibe, lo que la comunidad y los abogados defensores consideran insuficiente para mantenerlo hoy en la cárcel.


“Si hoy día ponemos a un Mapuche y a un no Mapuche en las mismas condiciones, en un mismo juicio, el que no es mapuche va a salir libre y nuestra gente va a ser condenada a una alta condena”.


Esta información se publicó en

Radio Kurruf

.

author: Administrador
title: Transmisión en vivo, 18:00 horas y palabras del Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés en la reunión del 3 de octubre del 2026 a las 1100 hrs.
content:
TRANSMISIÓN EN VIVO 18:00 HORAS | SÁBADO 3 DE OCTUBRE

Sesión Informativa sobre el Viaje-Abrazo a Buscador@s, diciembre 2026-Enero 2027 CIDECI de San Cristóbal de Las Casas, Chiapas, México

Sesión Informativa sobre el Viaje-Abrazo a Buscador@s, diciembre 2026-Enero 2027 CIDECI de San Cristóbal de Las Casas, Chiapas, México Sesión 13:00 HORAS | SÁBADO 3 DE OCTUBRE

Palabras del Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés en la reunión del 3 de octubre del 2026 a las 1100 hrs.

.- El principal objetivo: el encuentro-abrazo con buscadoras. Es importante que esto se entienda bien y quede bien claro. Porque no vamos a cancelar una reunión o actividad con Buscadoras por cualquier otra cosa.

Llevamos muchos años esperando el momento de encontrarnos con ellas.

Entonces, la prioridad o lo más importante en nuestra agenda o programación son las reuniones, encuentros y actividades con las Buscadoras, el día y la hora que ellas establezcan.

Cualquiera otra propuesta de actividad o reunión, deberá ser cuando no haya encuentro o actividad con buscadoras.

Incluso la celebración del aniversario del alzamiento será dependiendo de nuestro abrazo con las Buscadoras.

.- Ya está la paga para los buses de la delegación. Se consiguió gracias al apoyo de la Europa Insumisa, que donó lo que se había juntado para el Capítulo Europa de la Gira por la Vida, y que no se usó completamente. Estas compañeras, compañeros y compañeroas nos dijeron, desde hace tiempo, que esa paga es de los zapatistas, pero, hay que decirlo, es producto de su trabajo, su esfuerzo y su dedicación, y hay que reconocerles esa solidaridad incondicional. Esperamos que ese ejemplo sea luego replicado en capítulos siguientes de la Gira por la Vida, de modo que cada capítulo apoye la realización del siguiente.

Mientras tanto, aquí reconocemos el trabajo desinteresado de todas las personas, grupo, colectivos, organizaciones y movimientos de la Europa de abajo y a la izquierda.

También ha sido fundamental el trabajo de apoyo del colectivo de la Sexta México. “Mujeres y la Sexta”, para conseguir los autobuses.

Gracias compañeras, compañeros y compañeroas. A las Buscadoras les haremos saber de su apoyo.

.- Por lo tanto, toda la campaña económica será ahora para apoyar el traslado de todos los grupos, colectivas y organizaciones posibles a la Ciudad de México, en las fechas que les parezcan más adecuadas a ellas, dentro del mes de diciembre del 2026 y la primera semana de enero del 2027.

En el caso de amenazas y peligros, se tratará de que su traslado ida y vuelta sea por vía aérea, de modo que no corran riesgos al transportarse por tierra.

.- Les vamos a quedar mal porque no vamos a ir 1,111, sino que hasta ahora van 1,509. Más los que se suben de última hora. Pero hay lugar para el Frayba por si quieren acompañarnos.

.- el segundo objetivo es reunirnos con algunos grupos, colectivos, movimientos y organizaciones de la Sexta para planear juntos, en común, lo que sea posible para la segunda etapa de la Gira por la Vida-Capítulo México.

Esto es, cuando vamos a ir a escucharles de lo que son y están haciendo, y hablarles de lo que somos y estamos haciendo, o sea del común.

.- Si hay tiempo y modo, podemos movernos a lugares cercanos geográficamente a la Ciudad de México.

Pero sólo si hay condiciones y somos invitados. Hasta ahora hemos recibido invitación a Oaxaca, Oaxaca; a Querétaro, Querétaro, y se está viendo si a Puebla, Puebla. Si es posible en otros lugares, hay que organizarse y proponer.

Las compañeras de Oaxaca empezaron a organizarse desde que se anunció la salida a la Ciudad de México. Tienen ya resuelto el hospedaje y la alimentación para un parte de la delegación zapatista.

.- Estamos organizados por equipos y podemos cubrir bien lo que se haga en el Valle de México y hacer presencia en geografías cercanas. Así, dislocados, podríamos cubrir al mismo tiempo varios lugares, y varios temas.

.- Van más de 300 teatristas con 3 obras de teatro: Bichos, Agüitas y El Común en el día después. Por si alguien quiere presentar las obras o alguna de ellas en los lugares convenientes, resolviendo lo del traslado, que en la Ciudad de México suele ser un problema.

author: La Zarzamora
title: Comunicado público ppm Caso Grollmus
content:
Frente a las exuberantes condenas y tras un viciado proceso declaramos:

Mari mari pu machi, pu lonko, pu werken, kom pu che. El día de hoy nos dirigimos a la sociedad en general, a todos y todas quienes nos han brindado su apoyo y respaldo en este proceso denominado “Caso Grollmus”.

Actualmente a nosotros como comuneros mapuche se nos ha condenado a penas que marcarán un precedente como obscenamente políticas, se nos condena por decisión política, por ser mapuche que vivimos y recuperamos nuestro territorio.

Tras el gigantesco despliegue comunicacional, y tras el espectáculo montado por el Ministerio Público y la PDI, la familia Grollmus demanda al estado en busca de indemnizaciones y reparaciones.

La fiscalía con el aval del tribunal logró su objetivo: condenar a una pena que ponderada resulta en 1055 años de prisión contra nosotros. La prensa vociferó la sentencia y el poder político respaldo, claridad absoluta.

Les decimos, su ocupación contra nuestro pueblo y su territorio apenas tiene 143 años. Nuestro pueblo resistió al imperio español casi 300 años.

Hoy Chile soberbio y republicano nos condena a más de 1000 años. Por el único motivo de luchar por nuestra soberanía, por nuestro buen vivir y dignidad. Lo anterior tendrá la más necesaria respuesta: continuar con el legado de nuestro pueblo, luchar por nuestra dignidad y libertad.

Los Grupos de Tarea y la BIPE de la PDI recorren los penales de forma morbosa buscando testigos a quienes poner corbata de protegido y sin rostro. Sólo por cuatro relatos de estos “testigos” se dictó sentencia y veredicto. Nuestro territorio se militariza y vuelven a saquear nuestros recursos naturales, vuelven las concesiones mineras, CMPC y Mininco cual mecenas entregan dinero y donaciones a Postas y Escuelas.

Queremos manifestar nuestro agradecimiento por todo el respaldo de nuestros hermanos y hermanas en otros territorios y ciudades. No renunciaremos jamás a la lucha por un debido y objetivo proceso.

Nos movilizaremos por nuestra libertad y juicio justo.

Finalmente los invitamos a sumarse a la próxima movilización articulada en distintos territorios para este 12 de octubre, Día de la resistencia de nuestros pueblos.

¡NULIDAD Y LIBERTAD! ¡NO MÁS TESTIGOS PROTEGIDOS! ¡UNIDAD EN EL WEYCHAN! ¡LIBERTAD A TODOS LOS PRESOS POLÍTICOS MAPUCHE!

Presos Políticos Mapuche del Caso Grollmus de la Franja Lavkenche, CP Biobio, CERECO Coronel, Cárcel Llancahue de Valdivia.

title: Revista Crítica Anticapitalista 6 – La Comuna, la clase y la lucha de clases
content:
PRESENTACION


¿Qué relación existe entre la Comuna como forma política de la emancipación social y la clase, entendida ésta no como categoría positivizada y sociológica, sino en su carácter dual y contradictorio? ¿Es la Comuna una manera de entender la clase y la lucha de clases en clave no identitaria, no positivizada? ¿La oposición entre Comuna y clase es algo derivado de una concepción anti-dialéctica de la lucha de clases? En ese campo ¿a qué dialéctica nos referimos? ¿A la dialéctica hegeliana orientada a la síntesis estatal como forma política de la identidad? ¿A la dialéctica negativa que la cuestiona? ¿La lucha de clases, entendida en clave dialéctica no-identitaria, permite entender la Comuna como proceso contradictorio de disolución de la clase? ¿Implica esto un desafío a nuestro concepto de proletariado y a la idea de revolución calcada en el canon leninista?

author: Darío Aranda
title: Marcos Pastrana y la sabiduría diaguita para pensar la época
content:
Por Agustín Brun


Desde Tucumán


En Tafí del Valle, Tucumán, reside Marcos Pastrana, referente diaguita e histórico defensor de la naturaleza. Sus ideas, expresadas con las palabras justas y necesarias, invierten muchas veces el sentido común, convocan a ver la realidad desde otra perspectiva. Una mirada indígena, que con una sabiduría que emana de la ancestralidad de la cosmovisión andina busca sacar el velo de tanta modernidad y tanta ciudadanía, para así poder ver lo que llama la “realidad profunda” de las cosas.


Visitar su territorio, su hogar y concretar

una entrevista filmada de 67 minutos

 como registro de memoria, ideas y propuestas.


Recordar y transmitir


Había una larga lista de preguntas, pensadas durante días, buscando la mejor forma de aprovechar la ocasión. Pero alcanzó con apretar el botón "grabar" y pedirle que se presente para que comience una alocución libre, sin apurar las palabras, pero sin detener el curso de su pensamiento. No importaron las preguntas, ya que aconteció algo más interesante: un testimonio extenso, donde Pastrana reflexiona a partir de años caminando los territorios en defensa de la vida.


Sus palabras transcurren entre sentires autobiográficos, análisis de un presente que le preocupa fuertemente, reflexiones sobre el cosmos y la estética natural, pero también sobre el robo de los recursos genéticos, el saqueo de las tierras raras a través de mineraloductos, de las guerras y de la historia de la humanidad y cómo nos la cuentan. Reivindica los derechos de los pueblos indígenas, que deben ser reconocidos por las instituciones, pero poniendo una alerta a cuando los Estados, gobiernos y demás entidades globales no lo hacen: el derecho natural fluye, no es algo que dependa de un acta.


Pastrana describe a la Pacha no como una “figura de adoración”, sino como el “espacio que debemos ocupar en el tiempo que nos toca vivir”. Y es esa, su Pacha, la que le ha dado la obligación, la responsabilidad histórica, de “recordar y transmitir” el concepto del "Buen Vivir" comunitario.


Foto: María Teresa Cañas


Los cuatro elementos


“No hay que temerle al caos, porque del caos venimos”, afirmó Pastrana en el

Congreso de Salud Socioambiental en 2023

, en un momento ciertamente caótico, a meses de las elecciones presidenciales donde finalmente ganaría Javier Milei.


¿A qué se refiere con caos?”. Para el pensamiento de Pastrana es fundamental la diversidad. Lo que el sistema extractivista llama “orden”, no es más que una homogeneización, una clausura de la diversidad, en pos de la estética artificial. Esto anula lo que realmente es el orden cósmico, al que el sistema llamaría “caos”, y que es energía, vida en expansión, y que es fundamental entenderla como el verdadero orden cósmico para así poder abrazar la estética natural.


“La estética precede a la ética”, define Pastrana. Y recuerda un debate con académicos y amautas (palabra quechua que refiere a las sabias indígenas), donde Leonardo Boff —filósofo y ecologista brasilero— describe a la ética como uno de los cuatro elementos para el Buen Vivir. Un amauta de Cusco (Perú) le responde que se está olvidando de la estética. Porque justamente el apego y respeto por la estética natural, por sobre la estética artificial, es la que luego no permite hacer daño “a nadie ni a nada”.


De este modo, el abuelo diaguita reivindica el entorno y los cuatro elementos de la cosmovisión andina que lo conforman: el agua, el aire, la tierra y el fuego (la energía). Son esos cuatro elementos, es decir la naturaleza, los que hay que defender, como base de toda lucha. “Quien no defiende ni valora los cuatro elementos, no defiende a nadie. Ni a las personas, ni al ambiente, ni a los pueblos, ni a la democracia”, arremete.


Y define que ésa es la esencia del ser indígena. Si se abandona la lucha y la defensa de los cuatro elementos, del entorno y la estética natural, la persona deja de ser indígena en toda su dimensión, y pasa a ser otra cosa, independientemente de su color de piel, origen étnico o nombre. Esa es, entonces, la base de una vida en armonía con el entorno y el resto de los seres humanos. Afirma que quienes buscan instaurar un “orden” a través de la estética artificial no hacen más que crear daño, por más que ello se “adorne con todas las leyes, convenios, constituciones”.


Pastrana advierte sobre la

patrimonialización de los territorio, las creaciones de reservas

 por y para las élites financieras del mundo, mientras el resto del planeta …

author: Unknown
title: KON-MED calls for demonstrations in five German cities against the international conspiracy
content:
The Confederation of Kurdish Communities in Germany (KON-MED) has called for demonstrations and rallies in Düsseldorf, Berlin, Hamburg, Frankfurt and Bremen on Saturday, October 10. The occasion is the 28th anniversary of the beginning of the international conspiracy against Abdullah Öcalan on October 9, 1998. The umbrella organization is demanding freedom for the Kurdish leader imprisoned in Turkey and a democratic solution to the Kurdish question.


In a statement on Thursday, KON-MED described October 9, 1998, as the beginning of a new and decisive phase in the international conspiracy against the leader of the Kurdish freedom movement. On that date, Öcalan was forced to leave Syria. After a months-long odyssey through various countries, he was arrested in Kenya on February 15, 1999, and forcibly transferred to Turkey.


“These events made it clear that the Kurdish question does not concern Turkey alone, but that international powers are also directly involved,” the statement said. Even 28 years later, the developments of that period have lost none of their political significance, according to the Kurdish umbrella organization.


Referring to the current peace and democratic society process, KON-MED emphasized that peace must not be reduced to the silencing of weapons. “Peace means that the Kurdish people can freely participate in determining their own future. This requires genuine dialogue and serious negotiations. Öcalan’s freedom is key to a democratic solution.”


“The Kurdish people’s demand for freedom and a democratic life cannot be postponed,” the umbrella organization stated. Through the actions on October 10, Kurdish communities and their supporters in Germany aim to commemorate the events of 1998 and bring the democratic resolution of the Kurdish question into public debate.


KON-MED calls on the Kurdish population, as well as everyone committed to democracy, human rights and peace, to take part in the events in the five cities.

author: groundxero
title: “80 Lakh Voters On the Line”: After Gyanesh, Opposition Turns the Heat on Delhi CEO Ashok Kumar Amid Mass Deletions in State
content:
Hundreds protested outside the Kashmere Gate office of the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer Ashok Kumar on Monday demanding immediate rollback of SIR in the state amid 47 lakh deletions and 33 lakh notices issued for alleged ‘discrepancies’, with the INDIA block taking the lead. A report by

 Mouli Sharma

.


 


New Delhi, 7 October 2026:

Hundreds of people took to the streets for a short notice protest call outside the Kashmere Gate office of Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Ashok Kumar on Lothiyan Road amidst ongoing SIR processes, which have seen massive voter deletion from the state’s draft rolls as well as the issuances of ‘notices’ to many more. 


 


Police barricaded the roads, causing hours long congestion and traffic diversions between the hours of 12 and 4PM, following which a delegation of INDIA block representatives was permitted to have a private audience with Kumar during which they submitted a joint memorandum addressed to the President of India, Droupadi Murmu, through CEO Kumar.


 


“47,56,722 (32.78%) of Delhi’s voters have been removed from the rolls under SIR and 33,12,919 (34%) (sic) individuals have been issued notices. Deletions of this drastic a scale raise grave questions about citizens’ voting rights as well as the transparency of the electoral process,” the representation by the INDI alliance said, whose signatories included the state representatives of the INC, RJD, CPI, CPI(M), CPI(ML), RSP, AIFB, and TMC (MAMTA). Press were denied entry and efforts to contact the CEO have so far yielded no response.


 


Besides the INDIA block, though, large numbers of protesters from student and workers’ organisations, including the AICCTU, RWPI, Disha Students’ Organisation, and even the Aam Aadmi Party joined the protest in solidarity with the demands for an immediate rollback of SIR. Dozens of locals also joined the protest, expressing that recent revelations about the ECI’s functioning as well as the accusations against CEC Gyanesh Kumar had led them to lose faith in the electoral machinery. 


 


“The student character of the protests in Jantar Mantar might lead people to believe that this is solely a youth issue,” said Shweta Raj of the CPI(ML). “The Kashmere Gate protest clearly shows that this is not the case. People as old as 60-70 years old were there on the ground, women had travelled in large numbers from Shastri Park, because at the end of the day this is a universal issue. Day in and day out we get calls from people all over the city who have been pushed to the point of desperation trying to fulfill the bureaucratese of SIR who are still falling short, whose names are still being deleted.”


 


She also highlighted that the process of SIR, which severely disadvantages those without

permanent residential

 addresses in their current states of residence, has followed a pattern of recurring displacement drives across the city, effectively earmarking those affected for immediate loss of their voting rights. 


 


“The largest number of people affected were from

bastis

 that had been demolished without any rehabilitation of the residents. There is no roadmap for a person like that to get back on the rolls; the whole thing is systematised,” she said. 


 


The demands: rollback, resign, and EVM ban


 


The delegation submitted three demands to the CEO in writing: first, the immediate rollback of SIR in Delhi, along with the readmittance of all the deleted voters (barring the dead) back into the rolls and an indefinite stay on ‘processes’ such as responding to issued notices of ‘logical discrepancies’ in voters’ identities; second, an immediate resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar; and third, perhaps most longstanding within India’s electoral debate: a ban on EVMs and conduct of future all elections through ballots, in an effort to regenerate people’s trust in the electoral machinery. 


 


In 2010, engineer Hari Prasad had demonstrated in an infamous live broadcast on national TV how India’s Electronic Voting Machines could be hacked to favour a preselected candidate. Prasad was arrested for his ‘demonstration’ at the time, under the then ruling UPA government. Ironically, it was the BJP led opposition at the time who was most vocal about the demand for a return to traditional ballot-paper voting. author: Brian Hioe
title: Indigenous Groups Protest Typhoon Ragasa Response Last Month
content:
INDIGENOUS COMMUNITY members protested last month outside of the Executive Yuan, marking the one-year anniversary of deadly flooding in Matai’an, also known as Guangfu Township. The deadly flooding occurred after Typhoon Ragasa in September 2025.

Such community members have called on the Executive Yuan to ensure that reconstruction is carried out in coordination with the wishes of the local community, while working with the local government to do so. On the other hand, community members have criticized when reconstruction takes place in such a manner that leads to mass land expropriation, depriving local residents of their land.

In this sense, Matai’an community members have criticized broken promises from the government, which has promised to fund reconstruction and provide resources. The protest also raises how Matai’an has become highly dependent on donations from the outside world after the deadly flooding.

As part of the demonstration, participants threw plastic bottles filled with sand and water from Matai’an at photos of KMT caucus leader Fu Kun-chi, Hualien county magistrate Hsu Cheng-wei, Ljaucu Zingrur, head of the Council of Indigenous Peoples, and minister without portfolio Chen Chin-te.

One notes that anger, then, is directed both at the central and local governments. In particular, Fu Kun-chi and his wife, Hsu Cheng-wei, are often understood as members of a political dynasty that rules over Hualien. Fu and Hsu have been criticized as not doing enough for Hualien in the aftermath of Typhoon Ragasa, as well as after successive earthquakes have damaged infrastructure there. At the same time, the central government and the Council of Indigenous Peoples have also been criticized for failing to take sufficient action in the aftermath of the disaster–as well as to avoid such disasters occurring in the future.

Indeed, one notes that in the aftermath of the deadly flooding, Fu attempted to put the blame for the disaster on the central government. Fu alleged that the central government did not warn local authorities in time, and suggested that the central government was mostly at fault for delays in reconstruction.

Either way, one notes that though there was a wave of volunteers who traveled to Hualien to assist in the aftermath of Typhoon Ragasa, attention has now shifted elsewhere. Likewise, if external aid in the wake of the disaster is simply followed by how the disaster is used as a pretext for land seizures, this continues colonialism directed at Indigenous communities. It proves deeply colonial, of course, if a disaster simply serves as a pretext to conduct land seizures and further displace Indigenous people from their land.

author: Kodao Productions
title: Leandro Leviste’s arrest order explained
content:
A local court ordered the arrest of one of the country’s youngest and richest legislators over alleged alleged failures to put up solar energy farms in accordance with a congressional franchise awarded in 2019.


Makati City Regional Trial Court Branch 235 issued a warrant of arrest against Batangas Rep. Leandro Leviste on Monday, October 5, for allegedly violating the country’s Public Service Act (PSA). The warrant set Leviste’s bail at P72,000.


Leviste, however, is in Europe in an extended and unexplained absence from his duties as a member of the House of Representatives .


What is Leviste accused of?


Leviste is the founder of the Solar Para sa Bayan (Solar for the People) Corporation, granted a 25-year franchise to construct, install, establish, operate, and maintain solar-powered generation facilities and mini-grid systems in the Philippines. His company promised to supply affordable, reliable, and sustainable electricity to underserved areas in the Philippines.


The company, however, failed to deliver, resulting in cancelled service contracts and billions of pesos in government penalties, the Department of Energy (DOE) reported.


Leviste however succeeded in raising more capital by going public with a derivative company, the Solar Philippines Nueva Ecija Corp. that was valued at P60.9 billion (Dh3.57 billion) at the time of its initial public offering in December 2021.


He subsequently divested large blocks of shares to Meralco PowerGen Corporation (MGen) and other investors, earning over P34 billion in the process.


Government regulators said Leviste violated his congressional franchise by not seeking permission before selling parts of his operations to other entities. Leviste’s firm was subsequently slapped with a P24 billion fine.


Who is Leviste?


The 33-year old first-term legislator is a son of incumbent senator Loren Legarda and former Batangas provincial governor Antonio Leviste.


The younger Leviste came into national political consciousness when he publicly criticized former allies of past Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte who jumped ship and allied themselves with the ruling Ferdinand Marcos Jr. clique after the Marcos-Duterte fallout in 2024.


His troubles escalated when Marcos’ Executive Secretary Ralph Recto publicly accused him of attempting to offer large-scale payoffs (allegedly ranging from P400 million to P1 billion) to influence political outcomes in Batangas. Recto, himself from Batangas Province, is a political rival of the Levistes.


Leviste left the Philippines in August, purportedly to accompany his mother Legarda in seeking medical treatment abroad. Legarda’s medical leave with the Philippine Senate had been extended six times.


Does Leviste deserve arrest?


Leviste’s lawyer Antonio La Viña said Leviste’s arrest warrant was based on “a complaint looking for a crime.”


La Viña said Leviste did not implement the franchise because the DOE did not issue the necessary rules and regulations. The agency did not identify the places where the franchise could be implemented.


“[Y]ou cannot invoke a general penal clause of a law without identifying specific provisions in the law which an accused has committed. In other words, ‘no harm, no foul,’ the lawyer added.


Leviste belittled the arrest order, saying it is “a small matter compared to the other things happening.”


“I am more concerned about you,” he added.


Center of the crisis


As two of the rapidly dwindling Duterte allies in the Philippine legislature, the mother-son’s legal troubles are only expected to worsen.


Last Sunday, Philippine Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla announced the impending filing of about 20 graft and corruption charges against Leviste and Legarda.


Legarda is a member of the Senate minority allied with Vice President Sara Duterte who is undergoing an impeachment trial. Two of her colleagues are in jail for plunder while another is in hiding from an International Criminal Court arrest order.


In a heated debate two weeks ago, the Senate decided that only those who are physically present during the trial promulgation may vote whether to absolve or to oust the Philippine vice president from office.


Duterte’s public threats to have Marcos assassinated and the ongoing trial to oust the vice president are described as one of the worst political crises in the Philippines in the century. #

(Raymund B. Villanueva)

author: rti_admin
title: Why do we Protest? A Moral and Philosophical Basis
content:
The protests that have sparked in most South Asian countries in the last few years have sparked hope for socio-political, economic, and cultural change. Bangladesh’s protest over the job crisis in 2024, Nepal’s Gen Z protest (2025), and Sri Lanka’s protest of 2022 shocked the nations and their corrupt political systems. The Gen Z protest forced ruling BJP minister Dharmendra Pradhan in India to resign and raised demands for educational reform and accountability in 2026. The growing unrest of youths and their protests demand an objective analysis. This article asks some fundamental questions on the moral, philosophical, existential, and political basis of protest. More than answering the question of why we protest, this article is about why we should protest. While the outward manifestation and result of protest are obvious, the inward changes that protest brings are pertinent in shaping the morale of individuals in particular and society in general.

Let us ask, therefore, why shall we protest? Do we protest because we are bad? Bad as citizens, bad as human beings, bad daughters, and sons? Why do our youth protest? Why does this act of protest arouse so much fear? Fear from society and the state. Aristotle writes that “young men (and women) have strong passions and tend to gratify them indiscriminately” (Aristotle 2012). The younger generation possesses tremendous energy, creative force, and potential. More importantly, they are full of life, and life, to thrive, needs proper conditions that the current regime has failed to provide. However, it is the nature of life to expand itself. Hence, the protest of the youths. The old society, religion, and state use force to serve their purpose, and they try to control the boundless possibilities of youths. When any social and political structure downplays human nature and the necessities of life, we can no longer contain ourselves and remain silent. There is a limit to the control of the inner nature of humanity. Family, society, religion, and political power have always been terrified of human nature. They are forever trying to control, subjugate, and overpower the true potential of humanity.

Gods came, religion came, and then came the state! But is it possible to contain our boundless humanity that runs in our veins? History has proven again and again that it has never been, and never will be, able to suppress the beauty of humanity. The way religion, society, and the state forever wish to control individuals, individuals, in return, have forever rebelled and protested in every way possible. No god, no religion, no society, or no state can contain our boundless humanity. Is it possible to contain a forever-flowing river? We might try to control and put a brake on its flow for a temporary period of time, or it may dry out in a particular season. But for how many days? For how many seasons and years? It will return in the next season; it will return next time; eventually, with more vigorous force, it will make its own course. Nothing can stop it from reaching its destination.

In the same way, human beings possess immense potentiality. Hence, their free actions, thinking, and will cannot be stopped. Protest and rebellion can manifest in different ways. It may not always be political in nature. Sometimes it is chaotic, enigmatic, mysterious, decadent, and even in the form of telling the truth. When politics reduces to a level of tyranny, we rebel not only in the political domain but also in art, literature, science, and even in philosophy. Rebellion is a part of human life and its very existence. Reducing everyone who reads, thinks, and creates to the level of ‘Dimagi Naxal’ by none other than Narendra Modi, PM of India, is absurd and brands basic human nature and constitutional rights as criminality. His comments came in the wake of the Gen Z protest that was led by highly educated minds of India. Hence, delegitimising them while branding them with various tags is an act unbecoming of a leader of the nation. It must have been an act of rebellion that attracted people in power. All of these are various forms of negotiation with the existing socio-political structure. When we refuse the dictates of family, society, religion, or the state, that act of refusal becomes a site of protest. The protest must be understood as an act of negation. Camus rightly asked, “What is a rebel? A man who says no” (Camus 2013). While saying ‘no’ to negative politics, organisations, and beliefs …

author: Manila Today Staff
title: The cost of US imperialism that we are fighting against
content:
with added reports from Jessica Obciana and Kline Vergara

“Homes are destroyed, livelihoods are lost, nations are lost by interests that are made far beyond our own borders. Even now, initiatives like Pax Silica, supply chains for critical minerals and semiconductors are being reordered around the needs of the US war machine, and countries like us [the Philippines] are being asked to serve as suppliers and now become their targets, rather than being allowed to decide our own development,” said Dr. Giovanni Tapang, convener of the Stop the US-Israel War on Iran Network.

Various anti-imperialist groups gathered for the webinar Updates from the Resistance: The Current Situation in Iran, Palestine, Venezuela, and Cuba, co-organized by BAYAN, the International League of Peoples’ Struggle (ILPS) Philippines, the Philippines-Palestine Friendship Association (PPFA), and the Stop the US-Israel War on Iran Campaign Network, to express people’s solidarity in lambasting US imperialism following its sanctions, blockades, military aggression, and other forms of intervention and coercion against the people.

“This is the war machine that we are fighting against. And as we listen to those who are on the front lines, we learn of their resistance, deepen our understanding, and together strengthen solidarity to defeat this war machine,” Tapang added.

“We have seen the case of Venezuela: how this warfare has been attacking the Global South, attacking the country, and in many, many aspects, not only the political one, military, economic, and cultural, and in social consciousness. Venezuela is under siege now,” said Richard Lobo, Venezuela’s Chargé d’Affaires.

Venezuela possesses the world’s largest proven crude oil reserves, estimated at around 303 billion barrels as of 2023, according to the US Energy Information Administration.

Lobo noted that US intervention in Venezuela extends beyond economic sanctions to political, military, economic, and cultural intervention.

In January 2026, the US launched Operation Absolute Resolve as a large-scale military operation in Venezuela framed around drug trafficking and national security that led to the capture of President Nicolás Maduro and First Lady Cilia Flores and their transfer to the United States. Such an operation also targeted Venezuelan military infrastructure across Caracas and other locations.

Months after Maduro’s capture, the US laid out an agreement to gain access and control over an estimated 65 billion barrels of oil reserves, mineral wealth, and other resources.

Meanwhile, Lobo emphasized that the situation has only amplified the resistance among Venezuelans in defending their sovereignty and their right to determine the country’s political and economic direction.

“Even though we have been under attack […] the people there in Venezuela have been resisting and have been struggling. And one thing that I can say right now is that even with the kidnapping of our president, they believe the government is still in power,” Lobo stated.

More than 5,000 civilians have been killed in the US-Israel aggression against Iran, including 168 girls who were killed when a school was struck in March this year.

“Iran is experiencing aggression by the United States and Israel since the 1979 revolution against a very corrupt government, the Shah’s government. The United States has been trying to overthrow the revolutionary government in Iran, engaging in economic warfare for 46 years,” said Dr. Foad Izadi, associate professor at the University of Tehran.

The 1979 Iranian Revolution overthrew Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, whose government had maintained close relations with the US. The revolution fundamentally changed Iran’s relationship with the US, posing decades of diplomatic confrontation, economic sanctions, and political pressure.

“(The US) has also asked Iran to reduce its support for the Palestinian cause. As you know, Iran has been a strong supporter of Palestine. author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Fuel hikes squeeze jeepney drivers, commuters dry
content:
Jeepney with signage: "No to Oil Price Hike" (Photo by Roselle Ochobillo/Bulatlat)

By Wendyl Geronimo and Roselle Ochobillo

For commuters, the recent P1 increase in jeepney fares may seem small. But for workers who rely on public transportation every day, the additional peso can add to an already tightening budget.

For jeepney drivers, meanwhile, the bigger burden is not the fare increase itself but the fuel prices behind it.

After several rounds of oil price increases, diesel prices have continued to eat into drivers’ daily earnings, leaving some struggling to provide food, pay rent and keep their children in school.

The pressure was among the reasons transport groups, including the Pagkakaisa ng mga Samahang Tsuper at Opereytor Nationwide (PISTON), held a nationwide strike on Sept. 29 and 30, calling for lower petroleum prices and relief from fuel taxes.

For 52-year-old jeepney driver Teody Bermejo, National Capital Region and Alabang Pasay President said that the additional peso in fare does little to address what drivers actually spend to keep their vehicles running.

Bermejo, who has been driving for around 30 years, said he now spends much of his working day trying to recover the cost of diesel.

He drives from around 4:00 a.m. until 9:00 p.m., or as long as 16 hours a day. When diesel was around P50 to P55 ($0.80 to $0.88) per liter, he said he could take home around P1,000 ($15.98), sometimes reaching P1,500 ($23.97).

Now, he said, his take-home income has fallen to around P500 to P600 ($7.99 to $9.59), despite the long hours on the road.

“That is really not acceptable to us because diesel prices have increased by around P52 to P55 ($0.83 to 0.88), while they only added P1 to the fare. There is a huge difference. It really won’t be enough for us.”

For Bermejo, the impact of rising fuel prices has reached his household. He has four children in school, but his income can no longer cover their needs at the same time.

One of his children who was in college had to temporarily stop studying and find work to help the family.

“My child in college had to stop studying for now. In a way, they also had to find a job to help me because my income now is not enough to support all of them in school at the same time.”

He said the family is now trying to continue the education of his other children while making ends meet with his reduced income.

The same struggle is felt by 50-year-old Janet “Arja” Tumbaga Pocsidio, a member of Piston Women who helps operate a Cubao-Divisoria route.

Pocsidio is a mother of five and helps provide for her children and grandchildren. When diesel prices reached around P140 to P145 ($2.24 to $2.32) per liter, she said their earnings from driving became too small to sustain the family.

On some days, her husband would earn only P70 to P80 ($1.12 to $1.28).

The family eventually stopped operating their jeepney for periods because the cost of fuel outweighed what they could earn from passengers.

Pocsidio then worked as a barker, earning around P250 to P400 ($3.99 to $6.39) a day, which she used for food and her children’s school expenses.

The rising cost of basic necessities also changed what the family could afford to eat.

She said they often relied on dried fish and eggs, while even small increases in food prices became noticeable in their daily budget.

Housing became another burden. Pocsidio said their family was paying P6,000 ($95.88) in monthly rent, aside from electricity and water.

Eventually, they were forced to leave their rented home because they could no longer keep up with the payments.

“We were evicted, and we ended up sleeping in our jeep. Yes, we were evicted because we couldn’t afford to pay,” Pocsidio told Bulatlat.

The family later stayed at the Piston San Juan office for about four months, where they paid for electricity.

For her, depending on the organization for shelter was difficult.

“I feel ashamed. I’m extremely ashamed. I’m quite self-conscious, but I have no other choice. I just told myself that I would leave it in the Lord’s hands.”

While drivers struggle with operating costs, commuters are also adjusting their budgets.

Bench Cuabo, a government worker, said that the P1 ($0.02) fare increase may appear minimal but still affects his daily transportation expenses.

He said his usual P15 ($0.24) fare has increased to P17 (0.27), and when drivers cannot provide change, he sometimes ends up paying P20 ($0.32).

author: ALR Editors
title: Announcing Asian Labour School Oct-Nov 2026 Semester
content:
Dear friends,


We are back with an amazing list of new and returning courses for the Asian Labour School. If you are interested in

acquiring democratic facilitation skills, navigating conflicts and taking collective care, working cooperatively, strengthening a union core or leading your own radical walking tours

, please check out the course information below and study with Asian Labour School.


Building Movement Democracy through Democratic Facilitation (Course Starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Facilitator: Chie Matsumoto


We all have attended meetings where decisions were made by only a few members, most outspoken ones or someone at the top. We may have once thought, “Why am I even here?” and left without saying a word. Democracy starts in the smallest conversations, dialogues and meetings by raking in most diverse opinions and ideas, piecing them together to create something new and meaningful to all participants.


Building Movement Democracy through Democratic Facilitation (Course Starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Worker Cooperatives: Can Cooperating Transform How We Work Together? (Course Starts on Oct 10, 2026)


Facilitators: Emi Do and Matt Noyes


Worker cooperatives are enterprises that are owned and governed by workers. When all of our working experiences have been in profit-maximizing enterprises, or in workplaces that are structured hierarchically, it is no wonder that we can encounter challenges when attempting to work together cooperatively. In this course we will explore the challenges and tensions when there are no bosses to hate!


Worker Cooperatives: Can Cooperating Transform How We Work Together? (Course Starts on Oct 10, 2026)


Careful, We’re Organizing aka How to Fight without Falling Apart (Course Starts on Oct 21, 2026)


Facilitator: Nash Tysmans


Movements are built through relationships. Yet the pressures of organizing (urgency, conflict, exhaustion, political disagreement, and unequal power) can strain those relationships and undermine our collective capacity. How can we build movements that are both effective in challenging injustice and caring in how we work together?


Careful, We’re Organizing aka How to Fight without Falling Apart (Course Starts on Oct 21, 2026)


Building Strong Union Committee at Workplace (Course starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Facilitator: Sithar Chhim


In order to win any campaign at workplace, unions need to be strong enough to pressure the company. Building a strong and representative committee is the only way to win over the bosses who have well organized structure at workplace compare to workers.


Building Strong Union Committee at Workplace (Course starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Designing Radical Walking Tours (Course Starts on Oct 12, 2026)


Facilitator: Kevin Lin


Have you ever thought about leading your own radical walking tour to share with friends the significance of places and histories in your city? Leading and participating in a radical walking tour is not only educational but fun and always memorable. A walking tour provides a concrete sense of places, people, and histories. This course will walk you through the conceptualisation, research and logistics of a radical walking tour, and hear ideas and experiences from other participants across Asia.


Designing Radical Walking Tours (Course Starts on Oct 12, 2026)

title: Hüseyin Olan: AKP uses all state resources for its own interests in Bitlis
content:
A long-running road problem in Aladana village in the Hizan district of Bitlis (Bedlîs) has pushed residents to the point of revolt.


Road repair work carried out by teams from the Bitlis Special Provincial Administration on the Horozdere Group Road has raised many questions after Aladana, a village largely inhabited by Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) voters, was left without asphalt.


DEM Party MP for Bitlis Hüseyin Olan spoke to ANF about the extent of the Justice and Development Party’s (AKP) partisanship in Bitlis and across Kurdistan. Olan said, “The AKP has now become a party-state. It uses all the resources of the state for its own interests and discriminates in the provision of services between those who vote for it and those who do not.”


‘AKP invests in villages where it receives the most votes in Bitlis’


The failure to asphalt the road to Aladana village, where most residents are the DEM Party voters, has sparked strong reactions during repair work on the Horozdere Group Road launched by the Special Provincial Administration in the Hizan district of Bitlis. While teams from the Bitlis Special Provincial Administration laid asphalt on the Horozdere Group Road, the entrance road to nearby Aladana was left unpaved, raising questions over the decision.


Aladana residents are being deprived of services they should receive in return for the taxes they pay. After rainfall, vehicles are often unable to reach the village, forcing residents to walk four kilometres to get home.


Heavy snowfall in winter brings life virtually to a standstill. Children cannot attend school, people who fall ill wait for hours for help to reach hospital, and villagers are effectively confined to their homes.


DEM Party MP for Bitlis Hüseyin Olan, who has repeatedly brought the conditions faced by Aladana residents to the attention of parliament, said the situation was entirely politically motivated.


Olan said the road problem in Aladana falls under the responsibility of the Bitlis Special Provincial Administration and pointed to services being distributed according to political preferences.


Olan said the AKP holds the majority in the Special Provincial Administration. He said, “The AKP administration in the Special Provincial Administration acts as it pleases, directing these investments to villages that are close to it and where it receives the most votes. We have raised this issue many times, but they continue their partisan approach.”


‘They arrested one of our council members and secured the majority’


Olan said the political balance resulting from the Provincial General Council elections also affects the distribution of services. He said the 12-12 balance between the DEM Party and the AKP in the Provincial General Council was disrupted ahead of the council presidency and commission elections on 1 April when a DEM Party member was arrested on the pretext of “Rojava protests.”


Olan said this enabled the AKP to take control of both the presidency and all commissions. He continued: “In the Provincial General Council elections, we as the DEM Party had 12 members, while the AKP had 11. The AKP brought in a member from the New Welfare Party (YRP), creating a 12-12 balance. But in January, using the Rojava protests as a pretext, they detained and arrested one of our council members. In the renewed elections in April, the AKP had 12 members while we were left with 11, and as a result they took both the presidency and the commissions. After the AKP achieved this result, our council member was released. We see the same partisanship in the KÖYDES elections. author: groundxero
title: ‘We can’t report anything against AP govt’: National media silent on Tirumala Tirupati controversy after ED and CBI probes debunk false claims of ‘beef tallow’ use
content:
In a press release on 17 September 2026, eight months after the Supreme Court-appointed CBI Special Investigation Team (SIT) explicitly ruled out the presence of animal fats in the ghee used for manufacturing the Tirumala Tirupati temple’s prasadam, the Enforcement Directorate has arrested a promoter of a private food company allegedly involved in contamination after lab forensic analysis revealed the presence of seven adulterants. Notably, none of them are animal fats, specifically ‘beef tallow’, the allegation of whose presence triggered outrage and investigation in the first place, and cemented a political upset in the state by amplifying communal tensions.


 


by

 Mouli Sharma


 


On 19 September 2024, Andhra Pradesh’s Tirumala Tirupati temple had taken over national and regional news by storm for an unsavoury reason: an allegation of the presence of animal fats in the temple’s

prasadam

 (consumable offerings to Hindu deities given as blessed alms to devotees), specifically the accusation that ‘beef tallow’ was used in the rendering of adulterated ghee used to make the temple’s laddus. Unverified accounts of ‘lab reports confirming the allegations’, which were amplified by TDP’s CM Chandrababu Naidu himself, eventually led to an FIR about the same being registered on 25 September 2024, followed by a PIL being filed in the Supreme Court by one Dr. Subramanian Swamy.


Over a year later, the allegations were debunked by a Special Investigative Team constituted by the CBI to investigate the case, whose forensic examination categorically ruled out the use of animal fats, though the presence of synthetic adulterants was confirmed.


On 17 September 2026, almost exactly two years later, the enforcement directorate reproduced the same findings. Seven adulterants were listed in an ED press release announcing the arrest of a food promoter allegedly involved in multi-crore transactions behind the procurement of the adulterated ghee—Refined Palm Oil, Palm Kernel Oil, Palmolein, MG-90, Monoglycerides, Myvacet Soft 400 and Acetic Acid Ester—none of which are animal fats of any kind, let alone fats of particularly polarising animals, like cows.


 


On 17 September 2026, almost exactly two years later, the enforcement directorate reproduced the same findings. Seven adulterants were listed in an ED press release announcing the arrest of a food promoter allegedly involved in multi-crore transactions behind the procurement of the adulterated ghee—Refined Palm Oil, Palm Kernel Oil, Palmolein, MG-90, Monoglycerides, Myvacet Soft 400 and Acetic Acid Ester—none of which are animal fats of any kind, let alone fats of particularly polarising animals, like cows.


In the light of both revelations, the dozens of mainstream media outlets across the country who expounded the now debunked claims without any evidence of their legitimacy back when the controversy had first surfaced, fanning communal sentiments within the country’s dominant caste-Hindu population, triggering a rise in hate speech, and cementing the popularity of the then newly elected NDA government in the state, have remained conspicuously silent.


“Unfortunately, we cannot use any news content against the AP government. I cannot say more than that,” he said.


Major newspaper outlets with the largest circulation rates in India; channels with the highest viewership statistics, and websites at the top of Search Engine Optimisation and provenance score rankings—The Times Group, The Express Group, Firstpost, The Hindu, Dainik Bhaskar, NDTV, and many more—all solicit their newsdesk items from this agency. This is possibly why the only visible headlines currently in the public domain that acknowledge this debunking, are the opposition party’s own social media posts, and an article by The News Minute, an independent alternate online news portal focusing on the South.


 


A noteworthy aspect of the entire controversy was that the allegations, from the outset, were being made in retrospect. Though the Telugu Desam Party had already come to power by the time the FIR was registered, with Naidu having replaced YSRCP’s Jagan Mohan Reddy (who was then targeted for his Christian identity) during the Legislative Assembly elections in May 2024, the complainant made it clear that his accusations were about procurements made during the preceding government’s tenure.

was heard
