author: Yohannes Woldemariam
title: Imperial Nostalgia: History, Sovereignty, and the Unfinished Work of Decolonization in the Horn of Africa
content:
History in the Horn of Africa is rarely allowed to remain history. An ancient civilization becomes evidence of modern sovereignty. A medieval dynasty becomes proof of national continuity. Territory incorporated during one political era is later remembered as though it had always belonged to the state that governed it.


This habit has become especially visible as the Red Sea has returned to Ethiopian political discourse. Ethiopia is landlocked and has obvious economic reasons to seek dependable maritime trade. But there is a fundamental difference between negotiating the use of a port and claiming that a neighboring country possesses territory that properly belongs to Ethiopia. That distinction disappears when Assab is described as a “lost Ethiopian port.”


Ethiopia did not lose a sovereign port in 1993. Eritrea recovered sovereignty over territory that had been incorporated into Ethiopia after the violation and eventual termination of an internationally established federal arrangement. To describe this as Ethiopia “losing the sea” begins the story at the moment of Ethiopian possession and ignores how that possession came about.


This is what I mean by imperial nostalgia.


Imperial nostalgia is not merely admiration for emperors or attachment to an earlier age. It is a way of remembering political space. Territory once incorporated into an empire is remembered not simply as territory once governed, but as territory that naturally belonged there. Incorporation becomes ownership, ownership becomes entitlement, and independence can then be remembered as national loss.


Christopher Clapham’s notion of an Ethiopian “manifest destiny” is useful at the margins of this argument, although I invoke him cautiously and not to validate Ethiopian historical claims. The phrase captures a mentality in which expansion can stop looking like expansion when incorporation is presented as the fulfillment of history. Manifest destiny looks forward. Imperial nostalgia looks backward and imagines that a geography produced through expansion was the natural order all along.


The deeper problem is the projection of modern states backward into political worlds that did not organize themselves according to contemporary borders. Aksum is an obvious example. Its political and commercial world crossed territories that are now divided between Eritrea and Ethiopia and formed part of a much larger Red Sea system.

UNESCO’s account of Aksum

 describes an ancient civilization. It does not describe a modern territorial state possessing a contemporary claim to the Red Sea.


Calling Aksum simply “ancient Ethiopia” imports the political geography of today into antiquity. Calling it “ancient Eritrea” would make the same mistake. Civilizations, languages, religions, trading networks, and archaeological landscapes regularly cross the boundaries of modern states. Shared history does not create shared sovereignty.


I explored this problem more fully in

There Is No Timeless Eritrea or Ethiopia

. The point is not to diminish the history of either country. It is to stop asking ancient civilizations to perform the work of modern territorial law. Aksum should be studied as Aksum rather than recruited into a contemporary argument over Assab.


Richard Reid examined this problem directly in

The Trans-Mereb Experience: Perceptions of the Historical Relationship between Eritrea and Ethiopia

. Reid is useful because he is skeptical of efforts on either side to recruit antiquity into modern nationalism. The same history can be arranged to prove a supposedly eternal Ethiopia or, in the opposite direction, an Eritrea with no meaningful historical relationship to communities south of the Mereb. Neither approach is good history.


Even the word Ethiopia should make us cautious. The Greek term

Aithiopia

 did not refer neatly to the bounded territorial state called Ethiopia today. Recognizing this does not make modern Ethiopia less legitimate. It simply acknowledges that political names, communities, and territorial states change over time.


Eritrea should be approached in exactly the same way. Fred Halliday, writing in 1971 while the Eritrean war was still underway, acknowledged in

“The Fighting in Eritrea”

 that Eritrea in its modern territorial form had been defined under European colonialism. That fact does not weaken Eritrean sovereignty. It places Eritrea within the history of modern Africa.


Most African states inherited territorial forms created or …

author: Paul Tiyambe Zeleza
title: The Historiographical Legacy of B.A. Ogot and His Generation
content:
Good evening, colleagues, and the Governor of Kisumu County, Professor Anyang Nyong’o! It is truly a pleasure for me to join you in this commemoration of the towering historian, scholar, and public intellectual, Bethwell Alan Ogot. I believe I speak on behalf of all of us in extending our deep gratitude to the Council for the Development of Social Science Research in Africa (CODESRIA) and the Department of History at Kenyatta University for organizing this important conference. Personally, my appreciation extends to that rarity of experiences, the opportunity to meet several of my former students at Kenyatta University between 1984 and 1989 who have become distinguished academics and administrators. It’s a befitting tribute to our intellectual father, grandfather, quickly becoming a great-grandfather, who was raised and spent his last years and is buried in nearby Yala, that this conference is being held in his home city of Kisumu, under the transformative leadership of one of Kenya’s leading scholars and public intellectuals, Governor Peter Anyang Nyong’o.


Introduction


Let me begin by noting that I last visited Kisumu in January 2019 to join Professor Ogot as he celebrated his 90th birthday. I first visited this city nearly forty years earlier, in 1980, when I was doing research for my doctoral dissertation on Kenyan economic and labor history, and spent time at this venue, the Tom Mboya Labor College. Professor Ogot had a lot to do with my interest in Kenyan history. My engagement with him goes back to 1976 when he served as external examiner at the University of Malawi.


Years later, he would proudly tell audiences at events where both of us were present that I owed my degree with distinction to him! In our classes on East African history, we had read Ogot’s books, and it was an indescribable honor and privilege to meet him in person. I was deeply touched and humbled when he asked to meet the student who had received the distinction, and he prevailed upon the department to bring me to the cottage along Lake Malawi, where the department took him to show their gratitude for bestowing the department with the distinction of his presence. .


That was the beginning of a lifelong mentoring and intellectual relationship that changed the trajectory of my personal and professional life, on which I will say more later.


When Professor Ogot passed away in January 2025, there was an avalanche of tributes in the popular and academic media celebrating his life and immense scholarly contributions. It is befitting that we are gathered here to remember and celebrate him as a towering historian and intellectual polymath.


Ogot belongs to an exceptional generation of the pioneering architects of the African academy in its multifaceted epistemic and institutional dimensions. These were extraordinary individuals, inspired by the fierce historical and humanistic urgency and imperatives of African nationalism: decolonization, nation-building, regional integration, development, and democracy. They were driven by the audacity, passion, and commitment to remaking the production, dissemination, and consumption of knowledge in, and for, Africa and the world.


They were scholar-activists who transformed existing disciplines and founded new ones, who built interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary paradigms, perspectives and practices, who believed in the power of education as a public good and engine of development, who relished their role as rigorous academics and public intellectuals, who jealously guarded academic freedom and the intelligentsia as the conscience of their new nation-states.


Their lives were large, complex, and multilayered. The trajectory of Ogot’s career is quite emblematic of his peers, born between the third and fourth decades of the twentieth century in the immediate aftermath of the formation of the colonial conquest state, whose ideologues deluded themselves would last for centuries, if not millennia, only to collapse spectacularly as Ogot and his peers matured into adulthood. I would like to explore, rather briefly given the limitations of time, five aspects of Professor Ogot’s remarkable life and legacy: Ogot the man, the historian, the institution builder, the public figure, and the mentor. Let me add that today we’ve heard much about many of these themes. My excuse for revisiting them is that I came a long way, and I have to justify my ticket!


Ogot the Man


Biographical reflections and commemorations …

author: Kodao Productions
title: How the Al-Aqsa Flood Shattered the Two-State Solution
content:
By

Prof.


Sarah Raymundo


Marking three years since Operation Al-Aqsa Flood requires confronting how October 7 shattered the foundational ideological facade of modern imperialist diplomacy: the two-state solution.


Far from being a mere military escalation, the Flood operated as a decisive historical rupture that definitively broke the illusion that occupation could be perpetually managed through endless diplomatic process. It shattered the false premise that a people under genocidal  foreign domination could be pacified by paper accords built on the systematic erasure of history.


Where imperial diplomacy attempts to reduce occupation to a manageable border dispute, the underlying reality has been laid bare: the Palestinian question is fundamentally a struggle for national liberation against settler-colonialism, driven by the historic necessity of an oppressed nation to achieve emancipation by all means necessary, including armed resistance.


Even comprador regimes thoroughly integrated into the US-Israeli orbit are occasionally forced to acknowledge the weight of global outrage. The Philippine state—despite its active complicity in Israeli settler-colonialism through agricultural, economic, and military-cultural exchanges—joined the historic walkout at the UN General Assembly during Netanyahu’s address.


This integration runs deep: under Washington’s direction, the Philippines is being incorporated into Pax Silica, a US-led technology and critical minerals framework that serves as direct war infrastructure. The semiconductors and supply corridors produced under this arrangement function to power the Zionist military apparatus and its broader campaign across the Arab-Iran region.


Yet, while the UN walkout presented a momentary divergence, the Philippine diplomatic apparatus swiftly reverted to form, clarifying its position by reaffirming adherence to the very two-state dogma that October 7 shattered.


Far from offering a pathway to liberation, the two-state doctrine represents one of the most persistent, insidious ideological constructs of modern imperialism. It operates precisely to allow international actors to project a humanitarian stance while ensuring the structural preservation of settler-colonial dominance. Dialectically, this framework functions not as a resolution to national oppression, but as a management technology designed to institutionalize it across three critical dimensions:


First, an examination of the primary diplomatic texts reveals a foundational deception. The phrase “Palestinian state” is entirely absent from the Oslo Accords; from its inception, the framework was engineered to reduce national liberation to a series of fragmented, demilitarized bantustans under administrative proxy control.


Second, rather than reflecting an indigenous aspiration of the Palestinian national liberation movement, the two-state model emerged as a liberal Zionist construct later adopted and weaponized globally by US imperialism—particularly under the Bush administration—to neutralize regional resistance and manage imperial stability.


Third, the material reality of the occupation exposes the structural utility of the framework: while Washington maintained the diplomatic illusion of negotiations, the Israeli ruling class proceeded with complete clarity that no sovereign Palestinian state would ever be permitted.


Imperialism utilized the rhetoric of the “peace process” as an ideological shield, securing the necessary time and political cover to expand illegal settlements, fragment territory, and entrench apartheid.


The Al-Aqsa Flood permanently shattered this paradigm. Historically, Palestinian revolutionaries and regional anti-imperialists have understood that the Palestinian condition cannot be resolved through diplomatic management between unequal entities. It is an ongoing anti-colonial war against foreign occupation and imperialist hegemony.


A framework engineered by imperial powers to preserve a colonial garrison state can never produce genuine self-determination. True liberation requires the complete dismantling of the apartheid state of Israel, an end to foreign occupation, and the realization of Palestinian national sovereignty from the river to the sea. #

How the Al-Aqsa Flood Shattered the Two-State Solution

 appeared first on

Kodao Productions

title: +++ Die Demo ohne Inhalt meldet sich zu Wort +++
content:
Gegen Ihre Repression


Am Sonntag, 11.10.2026, geht es wieder auf die Strasse. Und es hängt ein dunkler Schatten über dem Tag. Das war zu erwarten und wir möchten uns dazu nun positionieren. Klar ist, wir werden auf die Strasse gehen, denn die Berner Shitshow des letzten Jahres lassen wir so nicht stehen.


Zunächst eine erneute Einordung der aktuellen Lage


Die Schweiz ist eine Mörderin. Zum einen bietet sie ein ruhiges Hinterland für andere Mörder*innen wie UBS, Palantir, Glencore, Syngenta, die Weltbank oder Valcambi. Andererseits bringt sie als Teil des US-imperialen Blocks seit hunderten von Jahren unsere Geschwister auf der ganzen Welt um. Auch wenn gerade alle Augen dem seltsam faszinierenden Spektal der Trump-Administration zuschauen, fallen weiterhin echte Bomben, werden weiterhin echte Menschen verdrängt, sterben weiterhin echte Kinder. Kurz: die Lage hat sich nicht verbessert, sie ist nur nicht mehr so interessant für die bürgerliche Presse. Für uns heisst das nur, dass alle bereits bestehenden Analysen zu Krieg und Genozid weiterhin anzuwenden sind. Sie zu wiederholen, sparen wir uns an dieser Stelle. Wer es noch nicht kapiert hat, wird für den Moment wohl selbst dahinter kommen müssen (gäu Alec).


Zur Demo


Wir wissen, viele Menschen sind verunsichert und trauen sich aufgrund der Repression nicht mehr, an diesem Tag ihre Wut auf die Strassen zu tragen. Schöne neue Demokratie. Genau diese Menschen wollen wir mit diesem Communiqué ansprechen.


Wir nehmen an, ihr wollt euch grundsätzlich auch nicht von der Repression unterkriegen lassen. Aber das von Medien, Politik und Bullen kreirte Klima macht einfach keine Lust die "Demokratie" zu leben. Wir verstehen das und haben eine Antwort: Eine kreative Anti-Kessel-Demo. Ein Konzept, um am 11. Oktober auf die Strasse zu gehen und trotz Repression ein Ereignis zu schaffen, das uns im Widerstand gegen unseren mörderischen Staat und im Kampf für eine andere Welt zusammenbringt und unsere Banden stärkt. Um nichts über die aktuellen Entwicklungen zur Anti-Kessel-Demo zu verpassen und am Tag selbst optimal vorbereitet zu sein, ist es wichtig, dass du dem Demoticker beitrittst. Die Links dazu findest du unten im Beitrag.


Zur Frage der Bewilligung


Wir leisten Widerstand gegen den Schweizer Staat und lassen unser Handeln darum nicht von ihm bewilligen. Was wäre das auch für eine witzlose Logik.


Für die Repression ist die Bewilligung immer der erste Angriffspunkt. Und angegriffen wird, wenn es der Polizei beliebt. Oder was war das bitte am Smash WEF dieses Jahr? Einer bereits aufgelösten Demo in den Rücken prügeln?


Zum prophezeiten "Aufstand"


Die Herrschenden dominieren die Medien - wir sagen, sie kontrollieren den Diskurs - indem sie selektiv berichten und unsere Inhalte verschweigen. Diese Kontrolle des Diskurses erlaubt es dem Staat der Öffentlichkeit zu vermitteln, unser Widerstand sei nicht legitim, verwirrt, sinnfrei oder sonst irgendwie falsch. Und unser Aufruf vorallem eine Ansage zur totalen Eskalation. Das wurde einwandfrei klar aus den bereits veröffentlichten Beiträgen, siehe NZZ, BZ, Blick. Die Demo ist zur Projektionsfläche für alle möglichen Ängste und Unzufriedenheiten der Bürgerlichen geworden. Das ist bei linken Demonstrationen nicht ungewöhnlich, doch gerade der 11. Oktober 2025 wird immerwieder als Referenzpunkt verwendet, um die Verschärfung staatlicher Repression und Überwachung zu rechfertigen. Um verfassungswidrige Repression gegen uns zu legitimieren und unsere Inhalte unsichtbar zu machen. Der Staatsapparat will uns verunmöglichen, das "Recht" auf Protest auszuleben und zeigt damit im Endeffekt, was Rechte für diese "rechtsbasierte Ordnung" bedeuten - nichts.

Anti-Imperialism and National Liberation

“Each generation must out of relative obscurity discover its mission, fulfill it, or betray it … As for we who have decided to break the back of colonialism, our historic mission is to sanction all revolts, all desperate actions”

Anti-Zionism has entered the phase of sabotage. Lobbying governments to sanction Israel has been replaced with breaking drones and dismantling factories; boycotts traded for slashed truck airlines and arson; rallies and peace marches superseded with red paint and shattered office windows. It is a medium of tactics signaling a shift in the repertoire of collective action undertaken against Zionist Imperialism. This form of resistance did not emerge out of Al Aqsa Flood – but it too signals a new terrain upon which Palestine will be fought. It deserves an uncompromising theory of struggle.

The time has arrived for us to create something new. The mainstream Palestine Solidarity Movement has demonstrated its inability to effectively counter the growing international Zio-fascist alliance. author: Rodrigo Acuña
title: Cubans See Hope in Reforms But Worry Over How the US May Thwart Them
content:
Residents of Havana discuss the obstacles facing the revival of the Cuban economy amid the US fuel blockade.

Residents of Havana discuss the obstacles facing the revival of the Cuban economy amid the US fuel blockade.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Last month, Cuban Prime Minister Manuel Marrero Cruz declared that 158 new economic and social measures, out of an original package of 176 approved in July by the Cuba’s National Assembly, were being implemented and backed by 197 legal decrees. The measures include allowing private business to import medicines and other goods, loosening restrictions on private tourism, and authorising privately owned banks — under Central Bank supervision — on a regulatory basis equivalent to state banks. Adding to these measures, the National Assembly for the first time permitted foreign capital to invest directly in Cuban private businesses instead of having to operate exclusively through state-controlled structures. Private companies also will no longer be restricted to a maximum of 100 employees.

According to Daniel Torralbas, a London-based Cuban economist, the National Assembly’s new measures are “the most profound economic reform programme … since the 1959 revolution.” Headed by Fidel Castro, the government in Havana between the mid and late 1960s nationalized a vast array of U.S.-owned businesses that controlled major shares in key industries such as public utilities, mining, railways and infrastructure, and land and agriculture.

Mauricio Alonso, a 68-year-old former nuclear engineer who lives in Havana and now runs an Airbnb rental, is embracing the government’s new economic measures.

“On a personal level this is going to benefit me,” says Alonso, “because it’s going to allow, for example, me — since I’m self-employed — to partner with foreigners, to team up, to be part of a larger organization, and to carry out actions with my lodging business, and so on.” Working with travel agencies, in Alonso’s view, will now be made easier with the lifting of restrictions. “If I qualify, if I get accredited as such,” says Alonso, “I can carry out the work of a tour guide without any kind of problem.”

During the 1980s, Alonso worked at the Central Electronuclear de Juraguá, near the city of Cienfuegos, which was being built with the aid of the Soviet Union to become Cuba’s first nuclear power station. Alonso says that, “when the Soviet Union collapsed in late 1991, work on the plant came to a halt in 1992.” Although Alonso continued working in the nuclear sector until 1995, he “realized that the project couldn’t go on — due in part to [the] intense pressure from the U.S. government.” At that point, he decided to “switch to the private sector and start renting out rooms” after inheriting a large apartment from his mother.

Had Cuba’s nuclear power station become operational, it is doubtful the island would be facing its current energy crisis.

Despite a small recovery between 2021 and 2022, after Cuba’s GDP in 2020 contracted by 10.9 percent as COVID-19 effectively shut down international tourism, the island’s economic crisis has been worsened by the Trump administration’s fuel embargo. When U.S. President Donald Trump began to take action against Venezuela’s oil shipments to Cuba in 2025, which approximated 26,500 barrels per day, Cubans saw a serious reduction of fuel on the island. On January 29, the Trump administration formalized the oil sanctions on Cuba by signing Executive Order 14380, which did not simply add another sanction on the island, but instead, created a mechanism to penalize third countries that supply oil to Cuba. Should a country provide crude oil or petroleum products, then the United States government can impose further tariffs on that country’s goods entering the U.S.

For Amalia Díaz Pérez, a 21-years old recent graduate in philosophy from the University of Havana, the Trump administration’s oil embargo disrupted her final year of study. Speaking to Truthout, she said:

The total blockade of fuel imports — with only one ship arriving in nine months — caused public transportation to disappear and reduced daily electricity availability to a minimum. Consequently, my study conditions and most of my daily recreational activities were affected. Compounding this situation, household chores became increasingly difficult due to the strain of the nationwide fuel shortage placed on water and …

title: Flávio Bolsonaro y Lula van a segunda vuelta en Brasil
content:
Con casi el 100% de las mesas escrutadas, Flávio Bolsonaro se impone con el 47,05% de los votos y suma en total 56.082.216 votos. Este resultado no le alcanza para ganar la presidencias, por lo que se disputará una segunda vuelta con el actual presidente Lula Da Silva que consiguió 45,14% de los votos, que equivalen a 53.799.870. Las elecciones se dan en un contexto de extrema polarización, incertidumbre e injerencia del imperialismo yanqui. El resultado de las elecciones brasileñas tiene un especial peso en la balanza de las fuerzas políticas en Latino América. Tanto por el tamaño de la economía de Brasil como por la polarización entre el actual presidente Lula y el hijo de Bolsonaro subordinado al alineamiento del continente a Trump, el Escudo de las Américas y su doctrina de seguridad Donroe.

Por La Izquierda Diario.


Distintos analistas sostienen que el voto indeciso fue el que sorprendió en esta primera vuelta al volcarse a favor de Flavio Bolsonaro, que quedó dos puntos arriba de Lula. Este resultado refleja lo que las encuestas captaron días antes, una mejora de Bolsonaro quien capitalizó el voto útil de otras fuerzas conservadoras.


La presión del imperialismo parece haber surtido efecto como en la Argentina en las elecciones intermedias de 2027. Allí con el respaldo de dinero y la amenaza de retirar el apoyo y hundir las finanzas del Estado, de la mano del Secretario del Tesoro yanqui Scott Bessent. En Brasil, la amenaza se materializó con el cierre de consulados y la embajada por una supuesta cuestión de seguridad que la Policía Federal investigó y descartó. Además, está el antecedente de Venezuela y todas las acciones de presión con aranceles, y otras presiones diplomáticas sobre el gobierno de Lula.


Por otro lado, en todos estos años de gobierno petista no se cambió la estructura de la nación dependiente del imperialismo, así como tampoco se resolvieron las diferencias sociales, el racismo ni la concentración de tierras en manos de los latifundistas. Los salarios bajos y las familias endeudadas demuestran eso. No es solo el grave tema de las apuestas on line, son los ingresos de las familias, cada vez peores.

Después del triunfo en primera vuelta, el candidato opositor Flávio Bolsonaro habló desde su bunker en Brasilia y aseguró que «Brasil quiere un cambio», sin hacer mención a la fallida presidencia de su padre.

Pensando en el próximo round, le dijo a sus seguidores que en la segunda vuelta «mostraremos la verdadera foto de Brasil.» También afirmó que su campaña se centrará en convencer a todos los que se ausentaron de las urnas de la importancia de ir a votar.

author: Céli Pinto
title: The Most Important Election in Brazilian History
content:
We usually say that in general elections, we’re choosing a president, governors and lawmakers for the next four years. That much seems obvious. But in this election, with the first round on October 4 and the runoff on October 25, we’re not just choosing who governs. We’re choosing the country’s future for decades to come.

This isn’t a choice between candidate A and candidate B. It’s a choice between a sharp lurch toward colonized totalitarianism and the survival of democracy. Every voter needs to have this clearly in mind. We are responsible for this country’s future. Future generations will blame us, and rightly so, if we fail and Brazil is handed over to colonizer vultures.

Voters, whether or not they are politically active, whether they are young, middle-aged or elderly, have plenty of issues with the current government. It’s true the government could have done more, particularly if it didn’t have a Congress dedicated almost exclusively to serving its own interests. Even so, the government accomplished a great deal. It did this not despite Congress, but because Congress exists. That made it possible to negotiate with lawmakers and to pressure them through the press and social media.

We can only keep doing that if we also fight to change how Congress does politics. Everyone who wants to speak must be free to speak. Everyone must be free to fight politically. Institutions must be able to investigate, and to be investigated in turn. That means guaranteeing elections that are completely free and fair. None of this is possible unless we secure the survival of democracy, problems and all.

Voters, activists, young, middle-aged and elderly people all have good reason to be frustrated with the Supreme Court. There is a glaring indecency in the conduct of this group of mostly older men, all of them white. As for the court’s only woman, who is conservative, there hasn’t been a single incident involving her conduct as a public official.

But we live in a democracy. The only reason we weren’t overrun by the attempt to sabotage the 2022 election, and later by the attempt to pardon the military officers and their allies behind a heavily armed coup, is that the Superior Electoral Court and the Supreme Court exist. And the only reason we even know what’s happening now is that we live in a democracy, where everything can come to light.

The Trump administration is deepening its imperialist policy to alarming levels, even for those of us who have always understood the United States’ colonial ethos. This current phase of capitalism has abandoned even its weak pretense of democratic values. It now advances unbridled on the autonomy and sovereignty of countries in the Global South, especially in Latin America.

When President Lula said, in his address at the opening session of the U.N. General Assembly, that “Brazil doesn’t fit in anyone’s backyard,” he knew exactly what he was saying. Like many of us, he knows that a plot against Brazilian sovereignty is being assembled, led by the Bolsonaro family and its most obvious financial backers. Everyone involved would be pardoned if the worst were to happen, and the country would be driven into misery and excess.

This is a moment of absolute gravity. Circumstances like these have to be confronted directly, without half measures. If Lula wins the election, paradise won’t arrive overnight. Many people will keep facing frustrations. But I can assure you of this: no one will take the food out of people’s mouths, or the roof from over their heads, their universal right to public health through the Unified Public Health System (Brazil’s Sistema Único de Saúde, or SUS), or free medications, or the economic and racial quotas in education and public sector hiring.

If Lula wins, Brazil won’t magically become a country free of violence. Men won’t stop killing women in the senseless way they do today. But you can be certain that fewer poor, Black youth will die, and that police will be held accountable more often for mass killings.

The government will keep fighting organized crime, as it does now, by cutting off criminal factions’ money and arresting their leaders, including the politicians among them. There won’t be spectacular massacres like the one carried out by a police force whose state governor stands accused of colluding with the commanders responsible for the 122 deaths in October 2025 in Rio de Janeiro’s Complexo do Alemão favela.

Voting for Lula in this election isn’t voting for a …

title: Claudio Katz: “Hay que construir la izquierda para derrotar a Milei”
content:
Tras la repercusión de la Marcha de la Bronca, Claudio Katz analizó el rol de la izquierda en la coyuntura actual, donde juegan cada vez más fuerte dos variables: el retroceso de Milei y un potencial estallido económico.


Las incógnitas sobre el peronismo, la apuesta del establishment a perpetuar el esquema de ajuste, explotación laboral y saqueo del país que logró establecer durante la actual gestión, la impunidad de la Corte Suprema y la agresividad del imperialismo estadounidense en la región son datos ineludibles del escenario presente ante los cuales la izquierda deberá plantearse nuevas tácticas y compromisos, consideró Katz, si quiere llegar al gobierno y disputar el poder.


Indymedia: – ¿Cómo ves el papel de la izquierda luego de la Marcha de la Bronca?


Claudio Katz:

 – Está cumpliendo un papel muy positivo ante todo en la acción callejera. La marcha fue un éxito

 por la

 concurrencia y el impacto de un acto político, que traspasó la resistencia social y democrática a los atropellos de Milei. Contrastó frontalmente con la capitulación de la CGT que deja pasar el ajuste.


La movilización alcanzó el nivel más alto de una convocatoria de

la izquierda. Superó lo conseguido con la “Plaza del No” en los años 90 y con las grandes concentraciones que en el pasado articulaba el

PC. Exhibió un nivel de politización muy superior a las marchas piqueteras e ilustró nuevamente cómo gravita la izquierda en las coyunturas de inmovilidad del peronismo.


Esa indefinición del justicialismo se vio por ejemplo cuando ganó Alfonsín, durante el neoliberalismo de Menem o en la época de Alianza. Actualmente, vuelve a aflorar por momentos y por eso hubo cierta presencia de militantes o simpatizantes del peronismo en la marcha. Igualmente te diría que el dato más significativo fue la centralidad de Myriam

Bregman. La movilización consolidó su protagonismo y la consiguiente incidencia de la izquierda en las próximas elecciones.


Indymedia: –

Pero cuál es la proyección electoral efectiva de Myriam, porque las encuestas resaltan una imagen muy positiva sin equivalencia en la intención de voto…


Claudio Katz: – Hay infinitas especulaciones sobre esa relación y no tiene mucho sentido obsesionarse con el tema, cuando falta más de un año para la elección. El número de votos que lograría el FIT-U depende de escenarios muy

abiertos con dos variables centrales: el retroceso de Milei y un potencial estallido económico, que podría repetir lo ocurrido tantas veces en la Argentina.


Foto:

Nicolas Solo ((i))


Nadie sabe si el gobierno podrá sostener el tipo de cambio hasta el 2027. La recesión, la pobreza y el endeudamiento podrían desencadenar el mismo tipo de rebelión que sepultó a De la Rúa o la protesta masiva que derrotó a Macri. No cabe duda que la izquierda estará en la primera línea de ese eventual estallido.


Pero en cualquier caso su crecimiento dependerá de lo que suceda con el peronismo y en ese campo hay varios cursos posibles de división o cohesión y de amoldamiento conservador o resurgimiento progresista.


Por el momento se verifica una gran fractura en el justicialismo, entre corrientes de adaptación y crítica al modelo que la clase dominante apuntala con Milei. En general predomina la postura de no decir nada a la espera de lo que más conviene. Pero mientras tanto, un fascista como Cúneo participa del espacio de Kicillof, que a su vez emite mensajes de adaptación tipo Alberto Fernández y elude comentarios básicos de denuncia del genocidio de Palestina. Pero lo que haría como presidente es un misterio. Conviene recordar que nadie imaginaba el giro progresista de Néstor y Cristina antes del 2001 y sería un error ignorar la recomposición que logró el peronismo al calor de la gestión kirchnerista.

author: ROAPE
title: What is the Real Marxist Tradition in Africa?
content:
John Molyneux’s classic statement of Marxist theory and practice

What is the Real Marxist Tradition

? was first published in 1984. The short book provided an incredibly sophisticated description of Marx’s method, and his relentless and insistent focus on the core agency of the working class.


Only the working class – however it is interpreted, described or labelled in social theory – can deliver a revolutionary anti-capitalist project. There cannot be, Molyneux argued, any substitute – no enlightened project of state development, or ‘socialist’ military leadership who deliver socialism on behalf of working people. Molyneux – in restating Marx’s central tenet – emphasised the role of the working class in their self-emancipation. Marx was the original prophet of the self-emancipation by working people. Without this class, and this project, there is simply no Marxism, no socialism, and no possibility of international revolution.


For an African audience the book speaks to multiple failed projects of socialism delivered by military coups, ‘enlightened’ governments and guerrilla movements. Each of these movements at different times dressed themselves in the language of Marxism, class and anti-imperialism but systematically broke genuine efforts at working class power.


What is the Real Marxist Tradition

? speaks directly to those on the continent trying to find a way to a genuine and emancipatory theory and practice of liberation.


Molyneux’ brilliant short book has now been reissued by the UK based publisher Bookmarks, and the Ugandan publisher Editor House Facility (EHF) who focus on readers across the African continent.


The new issue of the book comes with a major new introduction by the Ghanian socialist Gyekye Tanoh. Tanoh writes about the development and transformation of the working class on the continent since Molyneux wrote the book, and the continued capacity of this class to bring about socialist and revolutionary transformation across Africa.  


Join us for the launch of the African edition of

What is the Real Marxist Tradition?

 on 22 October at 18.30 (BST) with Gyekye Tanoh, Tafadzwa Choto

, 

Martin Empson and Mark Thomas. Reserve your place 

here

.


For readers based in Africa, John Molyneux’s 

What is the Real Marxist Tradition?

 can be purchased through Editor House Facility


here

. 


Endorsements of the book:


‘John Molyneux cuts through a century of distortion to recover Marxism’s authentic, revolutionary essence. This classic work distinguishes between living theory and dead orthodoxy, showing that Marxism is not a relic of the past but a vital method for understanding and transforming the world. It is essential reading for anyone seeking to understand capitalism and how to change it. For young activists and students alike, it is a must-read as it offers a powerful weapon for today’s struggles.’ 


Tafadzwa Choto

, International Socialist Organisation, Zimbabwe


‘In this book, John Molyneux undertakes a principled exercise by applying Marxism as a “method of analysis” to Marxism itself. He thereby provides not just a description of what Marxism is, but a method for detecting what isn’t. His application of this exercise—in the form of an autopsy of the interests and classes represented by three self-proclaimed Marxist tendencies—provides a valuable model for defining Marxist politics and organizations in our own contexts while enabling us to avoid the “hybrid ideologies of the petty bourgeoisie.” This is crucial, for us in the Global South, where reality differs greatly from that of Europe, thereby demanding a Marxism of contextualized design, not rigid imitation. The method offered is therefore a vital tool in enabling Marxist projects capable of fulfilling its role in “guiding revolutions to victory.” Such is true whether in the Global South or in global contexts marked by increasing economic complications and the co-option of Marxism by bourgeois ideologies fighting for survival amid the clear failure of neoliberal models … One need not agree with all of Molyneux’s conclusions to find his method a timely and indispensable resource.’


Muzan Alneel

,Marxist researcher and writer from Sudan

What is the Real Marxist Tradition in Africa?

title: Antiimperialistische Aktionswoche 7. - 11. Oktober
content:
Aufruf zur Antiimperialistischen Aktionswoche


💥Vor fast einem Jahr sind in Bern tausende Menschen zusammengekommen, um ein Ende des Genozids in Gaza und ein freies Palästina zu fordern. Und die Schweizer Kompliz*innenschaft dabei zu konfrontieren. Der Widerstand auf den Strassen Berns war kräftig und gebündelt. Verständlich, nachdem wir in Lausanne, Genf, Basel, Zürich, Lugano, Bern und so vielen anderen Orten verschiedene Unis besetzt und bereits unzählige Demos und andere Aktionen organisiert hatten, die ungehört blieben. Während der Genozid weiterhin geläugnet wurde. Unsere Wut über den Genozid in Gaza, die Kolonisierung Palästinas und den Imperialismus liess entsprechend die Strassen beben und verschlug dem Staat die Sprache. Er hatte keine andere Wahl, als sein wahres Gesicht zu zeigen und zu versuchen unseren Widerstand gewaltsam im Keim zu ersticken. Er hatte keine andere Wahl, als am Rattenschwanz zu ziehen, der der Öffentlichkeit als Verschärfungen der Repressionsmassnahmen und der Roadmap für nationale Sicherheit präsentiert wird.


👉Ob in Lugano, Genf, Lausanne, Bern, Zürich oder Basel: Überall spüren wir die Gewalt des Schweizer Staats. Er beschützt mit Schlagstock und Gummischrott auf Ausbeutung beruhendes System. Er beschützt - indem er unseren Aufstand unterdrückt - die Interessen der Grosskonzerne, welche Rekordprofite am Krieg, am Genozid und der Vernichtung unseres Planeten und dem Leben von hundertausenden von Menschen erzielen.

title: Elecciones Brasil 2026, una batalla contra el imperialismo
content:
Las amplias elecciones que el próximo 4 de octubre tendrán lugar en Brasil, en las que se elegirán presidente, gobernadores y legisladores, son de importancia estratégica para nuestra Abya Yala y para todo el globo terráqueo. Brasil es el 5to país más extenso, está entre las 10 economías más grandes y demográficamente ocupa el séptimo lugar en el mundo.


Por otra parte, el Brasil de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, del Partido de los Trabajadores (PT), forma parte de los BRICS, quienes vienen abogando por un orden mundial más justo y equilibrado; su principal socio comercial es China, con una tendencia al crecimiento en su intercambio comercial; ha hecho fuertes críticas al ente sionista que, con la ayuda de los EE. UU., está ejecutando un genocidio contra el pueblo palestino. Todo lo anterior lo convierte en el principal objetivo del presidente Trump en el hemisferio. Ya le ha impuesto a las importaciones de EE. UU. desde Brasil, entre el 12.5 % y el 50 % de aranceles, lo que ha hecho descender las exportaciones brasileñas hacia los EE. UU. a sus niveles más bajos desde 1997, lo que ha afectado negativamente su economía, expresado esto, en el bajo crecimiento de su PIB durante 2026.


Trump y su secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio, se han estado pronunciando a favor de la candidatura de Flavio Bolsonaro y criticado ferozmente el juicio que se le siguió a Jair Bolsonaro, por el intento del golpe de Estado, llegando al extremo de tomar medidas coercitivas unilaterales contra el juez que llevó la causa.


La intromisión de los EE. UU. en los asuntos internos de otros países es bien conocida. En Nuestra América han derrocado decenas de gobiernos e instalado dictaduras militares, han desestabilizado gobiernos legítimos, han bloqueado e impuesto medidas ilegales e inhumanas contra pueblos enteros y han llegado a violar la soberanía de varios países con agresiones militares directas: México, Cuba, Haití, Nicaragua, República Dominicana, Panamá, Granada y Venezuela son ejemplo de ello. Han manipulado elecciones abiertamente, teniendo los últimos 18 meses los ejemplos de Honduras, Ecuador, Colombia y Perú, donde, de manera grotesca y descarada, han impulsado candidatos, amenazado a la población con bloquear el envío de remesas, amedrentado a los gobiernos y empresarios con elevar aranceles y han utilizado sus mecanismos de manipulación y desinformación contra amplios sectores de la población, utilizando técnicas como la Big Data, los algoritmos de las redes sociales y buscadores y la última tendencia que es el uso de la inteligencia artificial como una más de estas nefastas herramientas.


La injerencia de EE. UU. en los asuntos internos de decenas de países, ha quedado registrado en diversos libros, como los de William Blum (2005) y (2006), Guenther Roppel (2005) y Luis Suárez Salazar (2006) entre otros. En el caso brasileño ya en 1960 los militares, por presión de la embajada yanqui, exigieron y lograron la salida del presidente Quadros, quien pocos meses antes de ser destituido había otorgado la máxima condecoración, para autoridades extranjeras, al Che Guevara. En 1964 le darían un golpe de Estado al presidente Joao Goulart, poco después de anunciar la expropiación y redistribución de tierras privadas y la nacionalización de refinerías de petróleo y lograrían la destitución de la presidente Dilma Rousseffa del PT, a través de un impeachment, en 2016.


Por otra parte, el candidato con mayores posibilidades de disputar la presidencia a Lula, es el actual senador del Partido Liberal (PL), Flávio Bolsonaro. Como digno hijo de su padre, el ex presidente Jair Bolsonaro, viajó a Washington a reunirse con el secretario de Estado, para planear la campaña en contra de Lula, lo que resultó en la aplicación de aranceles del 50 % a importantes productos provenientes de Brasil, pretendiendo afectar a todo el pueblo de Brasil, con la intención de robarle apoyo al gobierno de Lula. Pocos días después de esta visita, llegó Rubio a declarar que, “Brasil no es amigo de Estados Unidos”, lo cual fue dirigido a genera malestar y angustia en las clases medias y altas del país.


Flavio Bolsonaro también visitó Tel Aviv, buscando el apoyo de Netanyahu y ofreció cambiar la embajada de Brasil a Jerusalem, en caso de ganar las elecciones. El apoyo sionista es muy importante, ya que tienen relaciones muy importantes con los grandes grupos económico-financieros que manejan la economía brasileña y mundial. author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "She Put Her Body on the Line": Maricarmen, 87, Dies; Her Eviction Sparked Spain Housing Protests
content:
The 87-year-old pensioner in Spain whose eviction from her lifelong home sparked nationwide protests has died. María del Carmen Abascal, better known as Maricarmen, died on Wednesday just hours before she was set to sign a new rental agreement. She was forcibly removed from her Madrid apartment last month on a stretcher after the private investment company that owns the building hiked her rent. After massive public outcry, the landlord had agreed to allow her back into her apartment.


Independent Spanish journalist María Carrión says that although Maricarmen’s story galvanized much of the country, evictions like hers are “a daily occurrence” in Spain.


“Rents have gone up 80% in the last 10 years, while salaries have not kept up,” Carrión says. “Young people cannot leave their homes. They cannot become independent or start families. And this is what people are trying to change from the street.”

title: Çeşme Belediye Başkan Yardımcısı 16 aydır tutukluydu: Tahliye edildiği gün yine gözaltına alındı
content:
İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyesine (İBB) yönelik yürütülen soruşturma kapsamında yaklaşık 16 aydır Silivri Cezaevi’nde iddianamesiz tutuklu bulunan Çeşme Belediye Başkan Yardımcısı Onur Gülin, hakim karşısına çıktığı ilk duruşmada tahliye edildi. Ancak Gülin, aynı gün Çeşme Belediyesine düzenlenen eş zamanlı operasyonda hakkında verilen yeni gözaltı kararı nedeniyle özgürlüğüne kavuşamadan İzmir İl Jandarma Komutanlığı’na sevk edilecek.

Onur Gülin, 20 Mayıs 2025 tarihinde eşi Yelda Gülin’in ameliyatı için bulunduğu hastaneden gözaltına alınarak tutuklanmıştı. Kasım 2025’te hazırlanan yaklaşık 4 bin sayfalık ana İBB iddianamesinde yer almayan Gülin, süreç içerisinde kısa süreli bir tahliye kararı alsa da savcılığın itirazı üzerine Silivri Cezaevi’nde kalmaya devam etti. İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı’nın ana dosyadan ayırarak 21 Temmuz 2026’da hazırladığı ek iddianamede, Gülin ve beraberindeki sanıklara İBB Basın Yayın ve Halkla İlişkiler Daire Başkanlığı ihalelerine ilişkin "ihaleye fesat karıştırma", "rüşvet" ve "kamu zararından dolandırıcılık" suçlamaları yöneltildi.

İstanbul 7. Ağır Ceza Mahkesi’nde dün görülen davanın ilk duruşmasında mahkeme heyeti, aralarında Onur Gülin’in de bulunduğu 5 sanığın tahliyesine karar verirken bir sanığın tutukluluğunun devamına hükmetti.

İzmir Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Cemil Tugay'ın AKP'ye geçtiği günün sabahında dün Çeşme Belediyesine yönelik 12 kişi hakkında "suç örgütü kurma", "rüşvet", "irtikap" ve "resmi belgede sahtecilik" suçlamalarıyla başlatılan soruşturmanın ihbarla başladığı öğrenildi.

Onur Gülin'in yarım kalan tahliye sevinci ise ilk değil. 4 Aralık’taki aylık tutukluluk incelemesinde aralarında Ekrem İmamoğlu’nun şoförlerinin de bulunduğu 21 kişilik gruptan Gülin dahil 19 kişi hakkında tahliye kararı verildi.

İzmir’den gelen ailesi ve iki küçük kızıyla cezaevi kapısında buluşmayı bekleyen Gülin, savcılığın jet hızıyla yaptığı itiraz üzerine cezaevinden çıkamadan, gece yarısı jandarma karakoluna götürülerek 9 saat içinde yeniden tutuklandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Steven Methven
title: How Labour Put Big Property Above Camden’s Local Residents
content:
A little more than a week before Thursday’s crucial byelection in the London constituency of Holborn and St Pancras, prime minister Andy Burnham laid out

a radical social and economic programme

 at Labour’s party conference in Liverpool. If the ideas were big, the shift in Labour’s direction was even bigger. Words not heard in years peppered the speech:

the working class

,

public control

, and apologies for political failures. Beginning with a curt acknowledgement that former prime minister Keir Starmer won a general election he could hardly lose, Burnham spent the rest of his speech slamming the door on Starmerism. 


Not in Holborn and St Pancras, though, Starmer’s old parliamentary seat.


Labour’s candidate in the byelection, Sagal Abdi-Wali, has been

a fixture of Camden council

 (the London borough in which the constituency falls) since the 2022 local elections. She quickly rose to prominence, appointed cabinet member for the council’s Better Homes programme in 2024, before being voted council leader in May this year.


But sources close to Camden council have described it as a stronghold of the Labour right. Characterised by purges of dissenters, cosiness to corporate interests and a lack of vision, the Labour group running the council, Novara Media was told, is ground-zero for Starmerism. 


That empty philosophy is epitomised in the council’s approach to housing, a topic – especially in the form of social housing –

at the heart of Burnham’s national plans

. While the new prime minister has promised a generational transformation in building council home capacity, Camden council has repeatedly sided with wealthy corporate developers when they’ve requested massive cuts to promised affordable and social housing allotments in new developments. Described as a “weak touch” by one source, another was more blunt: “They are fucking aroused by private developers.”


One example is the redevelopment of the O2 centre on north-west London’s Finchley Road. The three-phase plans, drawn up by Landsec, Britain’s largest commercial property developer, were originally approved by the council in 2023. Involving the demolition of an existing shopping centre, cinema and leisure centre, Landsec promised that 570 of the 1,796 new flats would be a mix of social and affordable housing. At a meeting last month, Camden council

approved an enormous reduction

: now, just 330 flats will meet those criteria, a drop from 32% to 18%. In the first phase of the construction, the slash has been even deeper, with

barely 15%

 of the total being classed as affordable. (A council spokesperson told Novara Media that the permission granted includes 20% affordable housing across the whole site, and that the development also supports the delivery of other community benefits, including funding for step-free access at West Hampstead Station.)


If the prime minister is to be believed, neoliberalism is on its way out of Burnham’s Britain. But in Camden, it appears in rosy health.


In the O2 centre case, Landsec took advantage of a Starmerite innovation. In October last year, then-housing secretary and

self-proclaimed Starmer-loyalist

 Steve Reed (since returned to the backbenches) announced a two-year window in which developers who promised a 20%, rather than the previous 35%, affordable housing quota

would have their plans fast-tracked

. This didn’t require Camden to accept Landsec’s changes. But the council rolled over anyway. 


The council’s approach to private development has also raised questions over future social housing. Approved in January, the Camley Street development near King’s Cross currently promises 401 new homes of which

almost half will be for social rents

. History suggests this too may be revised downwards before the first completions – and several longstanding businesses have already been

forced out, they say without council support

 (the council

denied this

). In the constituency’s northern-most area, the Labour stronghold of Kentish Town,

residents were perturbed

 by the permission granted for the construction of a £1bn Film Quarter. Promising 11 purpose-built sound stages, production suites and workspaces, developer Yoo Capital has also committed to

243 affordable homes

 – 50% of the sites’ planned 485 flats. Asked in a recent profile whether the developer could be trusted not to slash those figures, Abdi-Wali refused to consider that highly-plausible possibility. “I don’t want to talk like that,”

title: Das Projet-Evasions braucht Cash Money
content:
Das Projet-Evasions ist ein mehrsprachiges Netzwerk anarchistischer Freundschaften, das seit 2019 besteht. Nach sieben fröhlichen Jahren, in denen wir unsere kleinen Aktivitäten* durchgeführt haben, ist es nun an der Zeit, euch um Unterstützung zu bitten.


Mit „kleinen Aktivitäten“ meinen wir: Dinge zu tun, in denen wir Sinn, emanzipatorisches und revolutionäres Potenzial sowie anarchistische Perspektiven sehen. Mit „Dingen“ meinen wir die Erstellung zahlreicher Inhalte (Bücher, Broschüren, Artikel, Podcasts, Audio-Clips, Aufkleber, Zeitschriften, Postkarten, Spiele, Ausstellungen, Plakate), die Durchführung von

Workshops und Präsentationen,

 das erschaffen von tools gegen die Repression, sowie umfangreiche Verbreitungsarbeit. All das in vielen verschiedenen Sprachen, denn – haben wir es schon gesagt ? – sind wir ein mehrsprachiges Projekt, das sich über mehrere Sprachräume erstreckt.


Wir erstellen Inhalte, weil wir diese teilen wollen, sowie Werkzeuge, die andere Menschen nutzen können. Meistens erstellen wir unsere Inhalte selbst, manchmal arbeiten wir aber auch mit externen Personen zusammen. Wir geben alle gedruckten Versionen zum frei wählbaren Preis heraus; jede Person kann frei entscheiden, je nach ihren eigenen Möglichkeiten, was sie dafür geben kann und will. Parallel dazu sind alle

digitalen Versionen

 unserer Produktionen kostenlos auf unserer Website verfügbar.


Das Geld, das wir haben, wird größtenteils für die Druckkosten verwendet. Auch wenn wir hauptsächlich mit einer befreundeten Druckerei zusammenarbeiten, die uns unglaublich unterstützt, bleiben die Druckkosten unser größter Ausgabenposten. An zweiter Stelle stehen die Versandkosten, die jedes Jahr steigen. Bei Sendungen ins Ausland sind die Porto- und Zollgebühren oft höher als die Druckkosten der Publikation, die wir verschicken. Daneben kaufen wir auch regelmäßig Bücher und andere selbstveröffentlichte Publikationen, die wir zum freien Preis weitergeben, und in den besten Zeiten unserer Finanzlage konnten wir mehrmals inhaftierte Anarchist*innen und Projekte, die auf der Suche nach Geld waren, unterstützen sowie in seltenen Fällen einen Teil unserer Reisekosten und unserer Arbeitzeit finanzieren. An letzter Stelle unserer Ausgaben stehen die Kosten für unsere Website und ein paar logistische Kleinigkeiten.


Zum Zeitpunkt der Abfassung dieses Textes beläuft sich unser Kontostand auf genau 741 Schweizer Franken und 123 Euro, und wenn wir ihn wieder auffüllen möchten, dann deshalb, weil wir mehrere Projekte haben, die bald bereit sein werden, in den Druck zu gehen. author: Helmut Weiss
title: Wohngeld: Keine Lösung gegen Mietenwahnsinn – sondern Bestandteil des Problems
content:
Dossier


„

Das Wohngeld soll zum 1. Januar 2020 erhöht werden, zu diesem Zweck werden die Mittel für Wohngeld durch Bund und Länder aufgestockt. Im Jahr 2020 werden insgesamt 1,2 Milliarden Euro zur Verfügung stehen. Die Bundesregierung argumentiert mit den deutlich gestiegenen Wohnkosten und den Verbraucherpreisen. Die Leistungsfähigkeit des Wohngelds nehme dadurch mit der Zeit immer mehr ab. Zusätzlich würden bereits Erhöhungen der Einkommen, die ja nur die Entwicklung der Verbraucherpreise ausgleichen würden, zu einer Reduktion oder zum Verlust des Wohngeldanspruchs führen, mit der Folge, dass die Zahl der Wohngeldempfänger und die Reichweite des Wohngelds sinke. Mit dieser Argumentation setzt man weiter auf die Subjektförderung, bei der das Wohngeld durch die Mieter an die Vermieter weitergeleitet wird und damit die erhöhten Mietpreise legitimiert bzw. subventioniert werden. Man setzt nicht auf die Objektförderung, was konkret heißt, auf den Bau von Sozialwohnungen

…“ – so beginnt der

Beitrag „Wohngeld trägt nicht zur Lösung des Problems von Wohnungsnot bei – es ist Teil des Problems“ am 01. August 2019 beim Gewerkschaftsforum Dortmund


 zur Problemlösung, die gegenteilig wirkt. Siehe dazu:


Bund und Länder wollen beim Wohngeld Milliarden Euro einsparen – und die sozialen Kosten auf Kommunen und die ärmsten Menschen statt auf Vermieter umwälzen


Bund und Länder wollen beim Wohngeld Milliarden Euro einsparen – der Kahlschlag trifft eine Rekordzahl an Wohngeldhaushalten


Kahlschlag beim Wohngeld trifft vor allem Rentner*innen, Geringverdienende und Kinder


„

Zu den geplanten Kürzungen beim Wohngeld ein Statement von Anja Piel, DGB-Vorstandsmitglied: “Der Kahlschlag beim Wohngeld sucht seinesgleichen in der Geschichte unseres Sozialsystems. Die Kürzungen treffen mit voller Härte vor allem Rentner*innen, Geringverdienende und Kinder. Insgesamt trifft die Kürzung 1,3 Millionen Haushalte, alles solche, die jetzt schon kaum über die Runden kommen. 400.000 Haushalten raubt die Bundesregierung die finanzielle Hilfe für die Miete komplett, sie gehen zukünftig beim Wohngeld leer aus.

Umso unbegreiflicher, weil sich die Union gleichzeitig weigert, selbst sehr große Vermögen und sehr hohe Einkommen heranzuziehen, um Haushaltslöcher zu stopfen. Ein solcher Kahlschlag wäre der komplette Verlust eines sozialen Kompasses. Die Abgeordneten im Bundestag dürfen die Wohngeldkürzung keinesfalls durchwinken

.”

DGB-Pressemitteilung vom 6. Oktober 2026

 


1,3 Millionen Wohngeldhaushalte im Jahr 2025


„

Am Jahresende 2025 haben rund 1,3 Millionen Haushalte in Deutschland Wohngeld bezogen. Das waren 7,2 % oder rund 90 000 Haushalte mehr als ein Jahr zuvor. Wie das Statistische Bundesamt (Destatis) weiter mitteilt, bezogen damit 3,2 % aller privaten Haushalte Wohngeld (Ende 2024: 3,0 %). Die staatlichen Ausgaben für Wohngeld stiegen im gleichen Zeitraum nach Angaben des Bundesministeriums für Wohnen, Stadtentwicklung und Bauwesen von rund 4 689 Millionen Euro auf 4 992 Millionen Euro (+6,4 %). Damit erreichten sowohl die Zahl der Wohngeldhaushalte als auch die Wohngeldausgaben ihre höchsten Werte seit Beginn der Zeitreihe im Jahr 2005

…“ korrigierte

Pressemitteilung vom 25. September 2026 vom Statistischen Bundesamt


 (Destatis)


Wohngeld soll um Milliarden gekürzt werden – Referentenentwurf vorgelegt


„

Bund und Länder wollen im kommenden Jahr beim Wohngeld rund 1,5 Milliarden Euro einsparen. Auch in den Folgejahren sind weitere Kürzungen geplant: Ab 2028 sollen jährlich gut zwei Milliarden Euro eingespart werden. Das geht aus einem Referentenentwurf des Bauministeriums von Verena Hubertz (SPD) hervor. Die Ministerin hatte das Vorhaben bereits vergangene Woche angekündigt. Nun liegen die Details vor. Laut Entwurf soll das Wohngeld an drei Stellen gekürzt werden:


– die Heizkostenpauschale soll halbiert werden,


– die geplante Wohngelderhöhung zum 1. Januar 2027 soll entfallen,


– die Berechnungsformel für das Wohngeld soll geändert werden. (…)


Diese geplanten Kürzungen sind fatal. author: ACG
title: When history accelerates: Maricarmen’s eviction
content:
We publish below the statement from the Spanish group Liza on the Maricarmen mobilisation and the need for revolutionary organisation.


Context: On Saturday, September 26, thousands of people marched through the streets of Madrid to protest the eviction of 87-year-old disabled  Maricarmen Abascal from her home. Her door was broken down by local riot police, and she was evicted on a stretcher despite the resistance of a cordon of protesters. Maricarmen, who had lived in her apartment for 70 years, instantly became a symbol of the housing crisis plaguing Spain, particularly in major cities. Whose fault is it? Rampant gentrification, in which real estate developers systematically buy up buildings in city centres, taking the opportunity to “revise” rents. Maricarmen’s rent, which was around 500 euros per month, was increased by 275% to 2,750 euros! Anger swept across Spain, withtens of thousands mobilised and fifty demonstrations,, particularly in Madrid, where the demonstrations, claimed as involving as high as 500,000, culminated in an impromptu encampment at Puerta del Sol, reminiscent of the 2011 protests that sparked the Indignados movement. This time, a few nights of occupation were enough for the real estate company that had evicted Maricarmen to reverse its decision, release her from the hospital, and reinstate her in her apartment, cancelling the rent increase it had planned to impose. While applauding this outcome, the Puerta del Sol “campers” are maintaining the pressure, as numerous other evictions are taking place daily across Spain. They are demanding that the “socialist” government enact a new, more protective law to curb rising purchase and rental prices.

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez promised once more to introduce a new bill to regulate rent levels.  However, this was blocked by the conservative People’s Party (PP) and far-right Vox and the centre-right, pro-independence Together for Catalonia (JxCat). Sánchez has now called a snap election.


On the political climate and the need for revolutionary organisation


“Revolutions have their own rhythm, punctuated by accelerations and decelerations. They also have their own geometry, in which the straight line breaks at the bifurcations and sharp turns of history.” Daniel Bensaid,

Politics as a Strategic Art


There is a fundamental difference between chronological time and political time. The former unfolds in a seemingly uniform manner: days follow days, and development is linear. The latter, however, under the dialectical logic of a contradictory reality, is very different: There are historical periods in which months or even years seem to contain very few substantial transformations, while there are moments in which, in a matter of days, political reality can be radically transformed.


This means that political time cannot be understood simply as the succession of events on the calendar. It is, above all, the pace at which the relationships between social forces, institutions, organisations, and the possibilities for political action change. There are specific events that, based on the accumulation of internal contradictions, appear as turning points, making possible, in qualitative terms, what until recently was unthinkable.


A society can remain seemingly stable for years and yet be accumulating contradictions. These contradictions don’t necessarily manifest themselves immediately. They can remain separate, partially invisible, or even appear unconnected. An economic crisis, a labour dispute, a housing crisis, a particular police action, a popular mobilisation, or an institutional crisis may seem, individually, like isolated phenomena. However, they can establish connections between them: each event modifies the conditions under which the next ones occur, and each new conflict can amplify, accelerate, or transform the previous ones. It is at this point that the acceleration of political time appears, the concrete expression of latent contradictions.


It is not that an isolated event creates a revolutionary situation out of thin air. Rather, it happens that a prior accumulation of contradictions finds certain events capable of condensing them and making them politically visible. The event then acts as a catalyst for processes that were already developing in society.


“Men make their own history, but they do not make it as they please; they do not make it under self-chosen circumstances, but under circumstances directly encountered, given and …

author: Judy Mundey
title: Judy Mundey: ‘Public housing needed as housing crisis deepens’
content:
This is a slightly abridged version of a speech by Judy Mundey, housing campaigner and women's rights activist, to a meeting focused on NSW Labor’s development plan in the Bays West precinct, organised by Better Futures Coalition on September 29.

The Sydney Morning Herald, in May, referred to twin babies born to a mother who lived and gave birth to them in a tent on the banks of the Murrumbidgee River at Wagga Wagga in NSW. One died; the other had to be hospitalised.

A local councillor said the tragedy was a predictable result of systemic failures to address homelessness. He put the problem down to a lack of public housing.

The SMH editorial referred to the surge in people living in cars, tents and caravan parks, describing it as having echoes of the Depression era.

In Sydney, people are sleeping in the St James railway station tunnel, parks and other forms of less than salubrious accommodation.

Then there is the scourge of domestic violence and the desperate need for safe housing for the victim-survivors. For many women it is a choice between living with domestic violence or homelessness. The refuge system is unable to cope and thousands are on the waiting list for public housing.

Renting in the private property market also presents problems.

A recent estimate said that, nationwide, more than 1.25 million low-income households are in financial stress. Even where people can find rental accommodation, it is often less than stable.

A new report from Adelaide University said children who grow up in rental housing move every 2.3 years, on average, and that by the age of 14 a child in private rental had moved an average of six times, with some as often as 10 times.

Such frequent moves can incur or inflict other disadvantages, such as changing schools and the loss of friendship, sporting and social relationships.

We are not only in the midst of a housing crisis, we are experiencing a systemic failure to address it.

There is no shortage of promises meant to rectify the problem. Recently, NSW Labor announced some 9,400 homes would be built in the Woolahra/Edgecliff area, with towers of 32 and 34 stories. Almost all such proposals involve the private sector and that has not always gone well.

People will recall the examples of developer-built projects with serious defects, such as Opal Towers in 2018 and Mascot Towers in 2019, with some homes remaining uninhabitable.

Peoples’ lives have been ruined. They save and borrow, only to find they cannot not live in their new home but there is no financial recovery. At that time, developers were able to employ private certifiers.

The explosion of defect-riddled apartment project failures with their multi-million dollar repair bills prompted the NSW government to appoint NSW’s first Building Commissioner in 2019.

But then came the collapse of Dyldam disaster in 2020, one of NSW’s biggest apartment builders, with debts of half a billion dollars. The NSW building regulator identified serious defects in a 230 apartment development in Baulkham Hills, including defects so serious as to be labelled a threat to human life. That development is still undergoing repair work.

There are almost daily reports about the impact of these dodgy developers.

The latest dodgy developer in the spotlight is Bathla. It has collapsed, owing debts of $3.3 billion. Many buyers have been left in the lurch, losing large sums paid as deposits.

Bathla’s work was not only riddled with defects, it also engaged in unsafe work practices. It was fined $135,000 in 2018 over a serious injury on a project at Doonside and was slapped with more than 300 notices by Safe Work NSW relating to safety issues.

Thousands of partially-built properties have been left unfinished.

These collapses has inevitably had a devastating effect on those further down the supply chain — suppliers, sub contractors and employees are owed, as are those who paid deposits.

Bathla’s collapse is also a disaster for the national housing supply, as there are 14,000 apartments stalled.

The NSW target for new housing is already running well behind target.

The Chris Minns Labor government pledged to build 378,000 homes by mid 2029. This requires 22,000 homes to be delivered each year until mid 2029. There appears to be a massive disparity between the government’s promises and its actual delivery.

Notwithstanding these dodgy developer disasters, Labor seems wedded to private development.

But there is an alternative — public housing …

author: Sebastian Lotzer
title: City Of Blood [Part l]
content:
Mein Gespräch, meine Lieder


Mein Hass und mein Glück


Mein Tag, meine Nacht, mein Vor, mein Zurück


Meine Sonne und Schatten, Zweifel, die ich hab


An dir und in mir bis zum letzten Tag


Deine Straßen, wo ich fliehe, stolper und fall


Deine Wärme, die ich brauch, die ich spüre überall


Klaus Hoffmann – Berlin


„Das Gedächtnis der Menschheit für erduldete Leiden ist erstaunlich kurz. Ihre Vorstellungskraft für kommende Leiden ist fast noch geringer.“


Bertolt Brecht


2004 verkaufte der Berliner Senat in einer SPD-PDS Regierung 65.000 Wohnungen der städtischen Wohnungsgesellschaft GSW zum Schnäppchenpreis von 400 Mio Euro an private Spekulanten, der Wohnungsbestand ging 2011 schließlich an die Deutsche Wohnen über, die mittlerweile in einer Fusion mit Vonovia zum größten börsenorientierte Wohnungsunternehmen in Deutschland wurde. 2019 werden 6000 Wohnungen, also rund 10 Prozent der 2004 verkauften Wohnungen, für 920 Mio Euro vom ‘rot-rot-grünen’ Senat unter Federführung der PdL Stadtentwicklungssenatorin zurückgekauft. 2021 werden dann für knapp 2,5 Milliarden Euro an die 15.000 weitere Wohnungen mit Schwerpunkt Kreuzberg von Deutsche Wohnen/Vonovia zurückgekauft. Seitdem dürfen sich die Mieter in den Hochhäusern rund um das Kottbusser Tor über steigende Mieten und explodierende Nebenkosten freuen, die alles weit in den Schatten stellen, was die Profitmaximierungsexperten der Deutsche Wohnen zu verantworten hatten.


Sämtliche im Zuge der Kahlschlagsanierung Ende der 70er entstandenen ‘Neubausiedlungen’ rund um das Kottbusser Tor weisen einen extremen Sanierungsstau auf, ständig fallen wichtige Infrastruktur wie Fahrstühle aus, behinderte Mieter, die auf Rollstühle angewiesen sind, sitzen teilweise monatelang in ihren Wohnungen fest. Wie sich die städtische Wohnungsbaugesellschaft HOWOGE, die jetzt auch in Kreuzberg besitzt, eine “Mieterfreudliche Sanierung” vorstellt, exekutierte sie jüngst in Reinickendorf, wo 170 Mieter mit einer Vorlauffrist von nur 6 Monaten darüber informiert wurden, dass ihre Wohnanlage komplett saniert werde und sie Umsetzwohnungen verteilt über das gesamte Stadtgebiet erhalten sollen, was gegen jede Rechtsprechung auf eine ‘Wohnortnahe Umsetzung’ verstößt.


Während börsenorientierte Unternehmen wie die ‘Deutsche Wohnen’ aufgrund von medialen Meltdowns gezwungen waren, besonders skandalöse Zustände in ihren Wohnungsanlagen abzustellen, glänzt die HOWOGE seit Jahren mit der weitgehenden Verweigerung der direkten Kommunikation mit ihren Mietern und dem Aussitzen von Problemen. Bezeichnenderweise wechselte der operative Leiter des Vorstandes der HOWOGE im Frühjahr dieses Jahres zu genau dem technischen Dienstleister, der in den letzten Jahren zahlreiche Aufträge der diversen ausgegliederten HOWOGE-Tochtergesellschaften erhalten hatte. Eigentlich können die betroffenen Berliner Mieter im Nachhinein wahrscheinlich froh darüber sein, dass sich der “Sieg” des ‚Volksentscheids Deutsche Wohnen und Co enteignen’ bisher im typischen Berliner Wohnungssumpf verloren hat. Denn nun kommt ja der “Vergesellschaftungshammer” der PdL.


Verkauf dich nicht


Berlin


Jung bist du nicht


Du alterst so schnell


Buckelst zu sehr


Trägst an den Geldern der Freier so schwer


Die werden gehn


Dich sterben sehn


Berlin


Geliebte Berlin


Klaus Hoffmann


“Ein Drittel Heizöl, zwei Drittel Benzin” sangen Slime einst, in Berlin bauen die Punks jetzt Molotows mit Urin und rufen dann dazu auf, nicht zu einer laufenden Räumung zu kommen, weil das den Standort der ‘angemeldeten Mahnwache’ gefährden würde. Der ‘Wohnungskampf’ in der geschichtsträchtigen Hausbesetzer-Hochburg Berlin ist auf den Hund gekommen, während der TikTok Wahlerfolg PdL auf dem harten Boden der staatstragenden Realität aufgeschlagen ist. Erste Bauern werden geopfert, die Nahost Frage wird erneut in Neukölln entschieden und zur der Demo von DGB und anderen Verbänden gegen den Generalangriff von BlackRock Merz auf die Überreste der “sozialen Marktwirtschaft” kommen gerade mal ein paar tausend Leute, darunter die wichtigsten Repräsentanten der aus dem geschichtlichen Mausoleum auferstandenen K-Gruppen. Es scheint, als habe Disney das Playbook für seine neueste dystopische Serie direkt an den künftigen ‘rot-rot-grünen’ Senat weiterverkauft. Während draußen alles in Kleinstaaten zerfällt, die Mauern hochgezogen werden und der Klimawandel und Pandemien ihr Werk verrichten, macht Berlin weiter auf weltoffen. In Wirklichkeit aber lebt lediglich …

author: Unknown
title: On Saturday, as tens of thousands of people took to the streets of Madrid to protest against the…
content:
On Saturday, as tens of thousands of people took to the streets of Madrid to protest against the country’s deepening housing crisis, the retired schoolteacher was among a small group who had sought to take the protest one step further. “At first we were 10 tents,” she said, gesturing to the sprawling encampment set up in the central Puerta del Sol plaza behind her. “Now, we’re more than 300 tents, and it keeps growing.” Days earlier, many across Spain had watched in shock as news channels showed Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old woman with a disability, being evicted from the home where she had lived for seven decades. The shock soon gave way to anger as the octogenarian was shown being brought out of her home on a stretcher, flanked by protesters on one side and police officers on the other.

Maricarmen, 87, waits at home for police to arrive before being evicted from the home where she lived in Madrid, Spain, Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026. (Fernando Sánchez/Europa Press via AP)

Housing campaigners seized on the moment. “The whole country has seen that housing speculation has no mercy on anyone,” said Alicia del Río of the Madrid Tenants’ Union. “We’re not sad, we’re angry. And we’re not going to stop until we change things.” Abascal’s lawyers reportedly reached a deal for her to return home on Monday evening. “If this agreement we have reached is signed, it will obviously be a better and happier outcome for everyone,” her lawyer, Beatriz Duro, told reporters, saying it could “help to change the paradigm when it comes to housing in general”. At the encampment earlier on Monday, many described the days of nationwide protests and the encampment as a turning point in a movement that had long simmered as rents rose by 80% within a decade, while the cost of homes climbed by 63%. “We need stability,” said David Iglesias, 25, as he described how the ever-soaring prices had forced people to put their lives on hold to try to keep a roof over their heads. “People who want to have children should be able to do so, even if they are renting. People who dream of becoming musicians or barbers should have the chance to do so and not have to worry that they need to work, work, work to pay for housing,” he said. “It’s an endless loop that is undermining the mental health of young people.” As he spoke, a large banner flapped nearby, reading: “You can speculate on watches, jewels, cryptobros and Ferraris. But not on our fucking homes.” […] It was a nod to the informal camp slogan, launched by housing campaigners and oft-repeated by protesters in recent days: “Either the rentier economy falls, or the government does.”

[Video]: “Hundreds of protesters across Spain took part in pot banging demonstrations to demand political action over soaring rents, evictions and the shortage of affordable housing. The protests come ahead of a parliamentary vote on Friday on measures to strengthen tenant protections.”
