author: Jake Johnson
title: ICE Has Obtained Over 50 Million Voter Roll Records From DOJ Ahead of Midterms
content:
The agency’s investigative branch mulled sending undercover agents into nonprofits involved in voter registration.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Documents obtained and released on Wednesday by the advocacy group Democracy Forward show that the investigative arm of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement has gathered tens of millions of voter records ahead of the midterm elections as part of a purported effort to combat “voter fraud.”

Democracy Forward, which obtained the ICE documents through the Freedom of Information Act, said records from the agency’s Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) branch underscore how the Trump administration is “using the power of the government to try to silence eligible voters and prevent them from accessing the ballot.”

The 166-page document that ICE turned over to Democracy Forward shows that HSI has considered sending undercover agents to investigate nonprofit organizations accused of illegally registering noncitizens to vote. President Donald Trump and his allies have repeatedly and baselessly claimed that noncitizen voting is a significant problem in the US.

HSI admits in one of the newly released documents that its “review” of more than 40 nonprofits in New Jersey uncovered “no derogatory information.”

“The information revealed in the documents should concern all Americans and is further evidence of an alarming attempt by the executive branch to undermine our elections. It appears the president and his allies want to pick their voters, as opposed to the way things are supposed to function in a democracy where voters pick their leaders,” said Skye Perryman, president and CEO of Democracy Forward. “If not for the laws that protect the public’s right to know what their government is doing, the public likely would have never known about these concerning schemes. We will continue to use all legal tools to expose threats to our elections and to challenge them swiftly.”

Democracy Forward noted that the records also show that HSI has “obtained 26,235 US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS)-derived records, and 50.6 million voter roll records from the US Department of Justice, for investigating so-called voter fraud.”

“Notably, ICE listed out priority states for each set of these records, including Texas, Pennsylvania, California, New Jersey, Minnesota, Michigan, Arizona, Florida, Georgia, and Ohio,” the group said. “Alarmingly, certain state voter roll data may have been entered into Palantir’s ELITE app, which is used by ICE to identify, prioritize, and locate targets for deportation. HSI may also be investigating voting machines and seeking to prove voter fraud in ‘counties with 2020 results.’”

ICE’s efforts are part of what watchdogs and election experts have characterized as a sweeping, lawless attempt by the Trump administration to disrupt the 2026 midterms, which will determine control of the US Congress.

Hart Wood, senior oversight counsel at Democracy Forward, said the ICE documents provide “chilling new insights into the breadth and depth of the Trump-Vance administration’s efforts to pursue baseless claims of widespread election fraud and assert greater federal control over elections ahead of the 2026 midterms.”

“These records also expose the influence of election denier Heather Honey at both [the Department of Homeland Security] and ICE — including her working in partnership with activists and feeding nearly 50 million records from ‘independent sources’ into DHS voter fraud data collection,” said Wood. “They also show, for the first time, that HSI may be using undercover agents to investigate non-profits for purely political reasons.”

Συγκέντρωση ενάντια στις εκδικητικές απολύσεις στο Documento


Την Πέμπτη 8/10 αναμένεται να εκδικαστούν οι αγωγές των δύο απολυμένων εργαζομένων στο Documento, στις οποίες είχαν προσφύγει μετά τις εκδικητικές και καταχρηστικές απολύσεις τους από τον εργοδότη Κώστα Βαξεβάνη. Μάλιστα, η απόλυση του επί 8 χρόνια εργαζόμενου και πρώην συνδικαλιστικού εκπροσώπου συνοδεύτηκε από μια αήθη συκοφαντική επίθεση στο πρόσωπό του, όπου η εργοδοσία έστησε μια ολόκληρη σκευωρία με στόχο την ηθική και επαγγελματική εξόντωσή του, ώστε να αποκρύψει τον εκδικητικό χαρακτήρα της απόλυσής του λόγω της συνδικαλιστικής του δράσης. Μόλις ένα 24ωρο μετά, ακολούθησε η απόλυση και της συναδέλφου του, εργαζόμενης στο δημοσιογραφικό σάιτ «Κουτί της Πανδώρας», ιστοσελίδα του ομίλου Documento Media, επειδή «τόλμησε» να τον υπερασπιστεί απέναντι στη σκευωρία που στήθηκε εναντίον του από την εργοδοσία. Τα τελευταία αυτά περιστατικά έρχονται να προστεθούν σε μια μακρά λίστα απολύσεων στο Documento (πέντε μόλις τον τελευταίο χρόνο), που εκφράζουν την τιμωρητικότητα και την εκδικητικότητα του Βαξεβάνη. Ο ίδιος δε διστάζει να καταφύγει σε κάθε μέσο απέναντι στους εργαζόμενους που αντιστέκονται στους εργοδοτικούς εκβιασμούς και διεκδικούν καλύτερους μισθούς και αξιοπρεπείς συνθήκες εργασίας, σε εκείνους που στέκονται στο πλευρό των συναδέλφων τους αγωνιζόμενοι συλλογικά απέναντι στην εργοδοτική ασυδοσία και τρομοκρατία. Οι προσπάθειές του αυτές μείναν άκαρπες, μιας και η απόφαση που εκδόθηκε από το Μονομελές Πρωτοδικείο Αθηνών τον Σεπτέμβριο του 2025 έκρινε άκυρες τις καταγγελίες των συμβάσεων των πρώτων τριών συναδέλφων, λόγω της συνδικαλιστικής τους δράσης και της αλληλεγγύης που επέδειξαν σε απολυμένους συναδέλφους τους. Έτσι, το δικαστήριο αναγνώρισε την εκδικητικότητα της εργοδοσίας απέναντι στη συμμετοχή των εργαζομένων σε συνδικαλιστικές και συλλογικές διαδικασίες εντός του χώρου εργασίας και ξεσκεπάστηκε πλήρως το σχέδιο του εκδότη του Documento, Κώστα Βαξεβάνη, να «ξεφορτωθεί» μέσα σε σύντομο χρονικό διάστημα τους εργαζόμενους που δεν του ήταν αρεστοί – μέσω ψεμάτων, λοιδορίας και απόπειρας ηθικής και επαγγελματικής εξόντωσης – επειδή αντιστέκονταν στις αντεργατικές πρακτικές του και διεκδικούσαν καλύτερες συνθήκες εργασίας.


Το τελευταίο διάστημα καταδεικνύεται η διαρκής κλιμακούμενη επίθεση του Κράτους και των αφεντικών στην κοινωνική βάση, η οποία έχει ως προϋπόθεση το τσάκισμα κάθε κοινωνικής και ταξικής αντίστασης, όπου αυτή επιχειρείται να εκδηλωθεί, όπως καταδεικνύεται και από τις τελευταίες εργατικές αναδιαρθρώσεις οι οποίες ποινικοποιούν τις εργατικές κινητοποιήσεις, τη συνδικαλιστική δράση και την απεργία. Χαρακτηριστικό όλης της προαναφερθείσας κατάστασης είναι βέβαια και η προσπάθεια καταστολής -τόσο διοικητικά όσο και ποινικά- της οποιασδήποτε εργατικής κινητοποίησης, με απολύσεις εργαζομένων που συμμετέχουν σε απεργιακές κινητοποιήσεις ή ακόμη και αντίστοιχες πειθαρχικές διώξεις χιλιάδων απεργών εκπαιδευτικών. Ταυτόχρονα, η απελευθέρωση των απολύσεων, ο καθημερινός εκφοβισμός και η απειλή της ανεργίας, η γιγάντωση των μορφών εργασίας με μειωμένα δικαιώματα (όπως αυτή με μπλοκάκι) και η εντατικοποίηση των συνθηκών εργασίας είναι τα όπλα που έχει προσφέρει το κράτος στη φαρέτρα των αφεντικών για την περαιτέρω εκμετάλλευση των εργατών. Όλες αυτές οι «παρεκτροπές» που νομοθετούνται επίσημα τις τελευταίες δεκαετίες συνεχών αναδιαρθρώσεων, έρχονται να επισφραγίσουν την αφαίμαξη και εξάντληση της κοινωνίας, τη δολοφονία της στο βωμό του κέρδους των αφεντικών.


Μέσα σε αυτό το πλαίσιο, οι εκμεταλλευόμενοι και οι καταπιεσμένοι συνεχίζουμε να πληρώνουμε με το αίμα μας τη διατήρηση και αναπαραγωγή του βάρβαρου εκμεταλλευτικού καταπιεστικού συστήματος που καταδυναστεύει, δολοφονεί και εξαθλιώνει. Απέναντι στην εργοδοτική τρομοκρατία, τις κρατικές και καπιταλιστικές αναδιαρθρώσεις των αποκλεισμών, της υποταγής και της καταστολής, την υποτίμηση της ζωής μας, τη φτωχοποίηση και την καταπίεση, απέναντι σε κράτη και αφεντικά που καταδυναστεύουν τις ζωές μας, να εντείνουμε τους κοινωνικούς και ταξικούς αγώνες. title: Un mese all’inferno. Autistici/Inventati
content:
Abbiamo già raccontato quanto è accaduto a partire dal 26 agosto scorso al Collettivo Autistici/Inventati (vedi UN

n.24

 e

n.25

) e in questo articolo aggiorniamo agli ultimi sviluppi quella storia.


In seguito allo spegnimento dei server gestiti da A/I si è verificata una cosa facilmente prevedibile: migliaia di compagn* in Italia e in tutto il mondo hanno dovuto cercarsi un nuovo indirizzo di posta elettronica che avesse almeno qualcuna delle caratteristiche offerte da quelli che avevano usato fino al 18 settembre. I pochi server gestiti da gruppi di attivist* sono stati presi d’assalto dalle richieste e molt* hanno dovuto ripiegare su e-mail gestite da servizi commerciali che promettono una comunicazione elettronica più sicura.


Il vuoto più grande e meno colmabile è stata la chiusura della piattaforma noblogs.org che da venti anni permetteva la creazione e la gestione di siti a singole persone, collettivi, gruppi di attivisti e attiviste impegnati nella lotta per il cambiamento sociale. Un danno enorme, difficilmente calcolabile e che probabilmente non verrà riparato presto.


In uno dei suoi comunicati, il Collettivo A/I aveva scritto: “Ora mollate il pc, uscite, lottate, abbracciatevi e non perdete il sorriso. Perché noi ci fermiamo. Ma la resistenza e le idee no. Restiamo umani.”.


E il 25 settembre a Firenze e a Roma alcune centinaia di persone hanno auto-organizzato due iniziative in solidarietà e sostegno ad A/I. A Firenze quella che doveva essere una manifestazione statica si è trasformata in un corteo che dall’Ambasciata statunitense è arrivato davanti alla Prefettura.


Anche se si è trattato di iniziative non certo oceaniche il segnale è stato chiaro: l’attivismo digitale non basta ed è necessario uscire dalle “bolle” nelle quali sono confinate anche le posizioni più radicali. In questo momento si stanno organizzando altri momenti pubblici allo scopo di continuare a mantenere alta l’attenzione su questa vicenda.


Dopo lo scioglimento del Collettivo A/I, anche la collegata “Associazione AI ODV” ha iniziato la procedura per la sua chiusura, un percorso reso più complicato dalla decisione di “Banca Etica” di bloccarne il conto corrente. Il primo appuntamento è fissato per il 22 ottobre prossimo, quando a Pisa inizierà la discussione sul ricorso urgente presentato per chiedere la riattivazione del conto dell’Associazione. Come già scritto, ma è necessario sottolinearlo, il comportamento dell’Istituto bancario ha costretto chi gestiva AI ODV in una situazione paradossale. Per sciogliersi, l’Associazione deve devolvere il suo patrimonio a un altro ente senza scopo di lucro, cosa che non è possibile fare stante il blocco del conto.


Paradossi burocratici a parte, sempre restando nel campo istituzionale, le numerose interpellanze e interrogazioni presentate sia al Parlamento italiano che a quello europeo sono, per il momento, ancora in attesa e, se non sono prevedibili i tempi, è più facile prevedere che le risposte non saranno che aria fritta, visto che i problemi che il caso di A/I ha sollevato sono molto, ma molto più grandi di un piccolo collettivo. Si tratta infatti di mettere in discussione il potere di alcuni stati di gestire in modo privato la rete Internet e di avere il quasi completo monopolio di alcuni dei principali canali di funzionamento delle transazioni finanziarie mondiali. Due argomenti che saranno ritenuti in questo momento storico di secondaria importanza, tenuto conto dello scenario attuale, tra guerre in corso e immaginate, problemi di approvvigionamento energetico e crisi economiche.


Sempre in questo campo va segnalata la supplica presentata il primo ottobre da Banca Etica e firmata da altre 14 associazioni alla Commissione Europea e al Governo italiano, anche a sostegno di alcune delle interrogazioni presentate da alcuni parlamentari.


Va anche segnalato l’intervento di un solito noto (a volte ritornano) che ha proposto di “costruire un’alleanza tra “democratici e ribelli”, dove tutti stanno alla pari. Chi fa una banca e chi è accusato di essere, come capita a noi di Mediterranea, una “minaccia alla sicurezza nazionale”. O coloro che sono accusati di essere “terroristi globali” come Autistici/Inventati.” Un personaggio che non ha perso le cattive abitudini visto che ha provato a mettere il suo berretto persino sulle due iniziative citate più sopra: “E già questo percorso di lotta e iniziativa politica che comincia oggi con gli appuntamenti di Roma e Firenze, indica uno …

author: Emma Honeybun
title: Proposed bill would push RCMP to enforce First Nations law
content:
The Senate committee on national defence began the study of a proposed bill that would make RCMP officers enforce bylaws enacted by First Nation governments.


“Why we are here is to fight for the same rights that other Canadians have and we don’t,” said Sen. Mary Jane McCallum, sponsor of Bill S-223.


The

proposed law

,

An Act to Amend the Royal Canadian Mounted Police Act

, is meant to ensure that the duties of the RCMP would “include the prevention of offences against First Nation laws and the execution of warrants that may, under First Nation laws, be lawfully executed and performed by peace officers,” according to the bill.


This means that bylaws passed by First Nations governments that are regularly published in the

First Nations Gazette

 — a national government resource for announcements and updates from leadership — would be enforced by RCMP with the same urgency as a municipal or provincial law.


Bylaws are laws that are established by municipal governments or corporations and apply to only a specific jurisdiction.


According to Jennifer Ebert, assistant commissioner of operational policing services at the RCMP, First Nations can make bylaws under the Indian Act, but the legislation does not specify who is responsible for enforcing them.


“The RCMP continues to seek clarity regarding the legal barriers and authority that impact effective enforcement of First Nations laws, including band bylaws,” she told the committee.


She said band bylaws are “presumptively valid,” meaning that they are to be enforced as long as they “don’t contradict another piece of federal legislation.”


Despite this, several First Nations have spoken out about their bylaws not being enforced in the first place.


“Enforcement really does bring out a community’s voice,” Garrison Settee, grand chief of

Manitoba Keewatinowi Okimakanak (MKO),

 which represents 26 First Nations in northern Manitoba told the committee. “How can you be a recognized government without having your laws enforced? It just doesn’t make sense.”


Some First Nations are using the courts.


In February 2025, Heiltsuk Nation in B.C. sued the RCMP for what its chief claimed was a “refusal to enforce Heiltsuk bylaws, duly enacted by Indigenous band councils as federal laws under the Indian Act,”

APTN News had reported.


According to the statement of claim, “the discriminatory conduct of the RCMP” harmed Heiltsuk and undercut “the authority of Heiltsuk leadership and [eroded] Heiltsuk’s self-governance.”


It emboldened “drug dealers, other offenders, and wrongdoers to enter and stay on reserve lands and to continue objectionable activities,” the Nation said.


If passed, Bill S-223 would create a bridging form of legislation so that presumptive laws are not in question.


Lack of enforcement ‘undermines authority’: Senator


According to Sen. Mary Jane McCallum, who sponsored the bill, the lack of RCMP enforcement of bylaws under the Indian Act has been an issue since the law was amended in 2014.


Prior to the amendment, section 82 of the Act determined that new bylaws from First Nations governance would need to undergo ministerial review before being accepted and enforced.


However, this was repealed and councils were given back the authority to pass bylaws on their own terms.


This created a new issue, she said. Bylaws that “were valid at one time were no longer valid,” despite being reviewed and accepted prior to the amendment.


“They were no longer being enforced, all of the sudden,” McCallum said.


During the bill’s second reading before the Senate, she had added that, “when responding on June 1, 2023, to a question from Chief Hubert Watt of the God’s Lake First Nation [Manitoba] about the enforcement of First Nations laws … the chief federal prosecutor for Manitoba said, ‘With respect to your question, with respect to specifically the issue of the Indian Act bylaws, it’s always been the position of the federal Prosecution Service that we don’t prosecute those bylaws.’


“So, I take it that the RCMP, once they get that message from us, they take the position that if the Crown’s not going to prosecute, we’re (RCMP) not going to lay charges.’”


The senator is a member of Munsee Delaware Nation in Ontario, but lives in and represents Manitoba in the Senate.


During her previous work as a dentist, she said she saw “distinctive” and “unique” challenges faced by Indigenous communities in the middle province, specifically when it came to the …

author: Unknown
title: Scuole occupate: facciamo come in Francia!
content:
A Torino si prende esempio dalla Francia: l’aria di rivolta proveniente dal paese oltralpe ha superato i confini geografici, ridando un senso di possibilità di rivalsa studentesca anche alle nostre latitudini.


All’istituto Lagrange, come al Regina, Giulio e Gobetti le mobilitazioni studentesche francesi hanno squarciato il velo che impediva alle contraddizioni di tradursi in lotta aperta.

Da rivendicazioni di edilizia alla presa di coscienza dell’attacco complessivo alla formazione tecnica con la riforma del 4+2, il mezzo dell’occupazione si sta consolidando come mezzo adottato dalle scuole per porre una critica complessiva alla gestione capitalistica della scuola.

Attraverso i social i contenuti tutti politici legati alla rivolta francese costruiscono un immaginario di rivalsa collettiva che ipotizziamo diano le possibilità di un rilancio generalizzato di riappropriazione giovanile del proprio protagonismo.

La crisi generalizzata causata dalla crisi a sfondo bellico si propaga, seppur con delle specificità nazionali, in egual misura in tutti i paesi del continente europeo.

Le contraddizioni legate al modello sociale del neoliberismo occidentale vedono la possibilità di venire a galla e poter essere tradotte in un programma politico concreto.

Siamo i figli della crisi, e in questo contesto, le uniche possibilità di riappropriazione di decisionalità sulle proprie vite non possono che passare dalla lotta.

Da Parigi si alza un urlo di lotta: sta a noi tradurlo alle nostre latitudini in un movimento capace di mettere le nostre necessità al centro di un assalto al presente.

Nelle scuole torinesi il messaggio è chiaro: espandere la lotta e prendersi lo spazio politico per poter contare.

ci vediamo sulle barricate!

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: 51 Children Among 1,700 Homeless Deaths in 2025
content:
At least 51 children, the majority under a year old, were among 1,700 people who died while homeless in the UK last year, a social justice charity has said.


It is the highest number of child deaths recorded since the Dying Homeless Project started in 2017, which is run

 by the Museum of Homelessness

. 


Many of the overall deaths occurred in emergency accommodation, the charity said, proving that “moving people indoors does not automatically make them safe”.


Working with the

National Child Mortality Database

, the project found that 61% of the children who died were less than a year old, while only seven children were identified as homeless by councils. The Museum of Homelessness said the findings raise questions about how the deaths of children living in temporary accommodation are recorded by local authorities.


In total, the project identified 1,720 people who died while homeless in 2025 across the UK – an increase of 6.8% on the previous year. More than 10,000 deaths have been recorded since the project began almost a decade ago in 2017.


For 2025, 197 people who had died were found to be missing from local authority records, equivalent to one in 10 of the deaths.


“Local authorities are under-reporting the true scale of homeless deaths,” the charity said.


Meanwhile, 214 people died while rough sleeping or “with no fixed abode”, it added. Almost one third (30%) of deaths occurred while people were sleeping on the streets or in accommodation assigned to people who had been recently sleeping rough.


“Deaths of despair” caused by drugs, alcohol and suicide accounted for half (52%) of all homeless deaths, the charity said, adding that “recovery, harm reduction and mental health services need urgent investment”.


Deaths rose sharply in both England and Scotland, at 8% and 38% respectively, while Wales and Northern Ireland showed a downward trend.


The findings are part of a preliminary release, with the museum’s full report expected 14 October.


In July, as his first act as prime minister,

Andy Burnham promised to end rough sleeping

, with plans to get people temporarily

off the streets in time for Christmas

.  


Mairi Macrae of homeless charity Shelter

described the new figures as “unspeakable”

. And said it was time for a “national reckoning”.


She added: “With winter setting in, the government’s drive to end rough sleeping by Christmas is the right one.


“People need safe emergency accommodation, specialist support and, crucially, permanent social homes where they can truly rebuild their lives.”

author: Unknown
title: Özmen: Municipalities should support Kurdish theatre
content:
Teatra Jiyana Nû (TJN), which holds an important place in Kurdish theatre, announced that it has resumed its work after a long break. The group opened the new season with the children’s play Rovî Ji Çiyê Xeyidîye and also announced that it is preparing a new play for adults.


Founded in 1992 within the Mesopotamia Cultural Centre (MKM), Teatra Jiyana Nû has staged many significant productions in Kurdish theatre over the years. The group has performed plays including Daweya Generale Teneke, Ta: Sê Evren Dûr and Komara Dinan: Şermola. Teatra Jiyana Nû later formed a subgroup called Şanoya Helîn, where it also provided acting training.


Teatra Jiyana Nû faced numerous bans and forms of repression throughout its years of activity. Its plays were repeatedly banned, its stages were sealed, and its actors were detained and arrested. Some actors from the group later joined the Kurdish Freedom Movement. The group’s most recent play, Berû, was also banned in many cities across Turkey and Kurdistan. The group suspended its activities for a long period following this process and is now returning to the stage with the new season.


Teatra Jiyana Nû, which opened the season with the children’s play Rovî Ji Çiyê Xeyidîye, will also launch a workshop to provide theatre training in the new period.


Actor Xanim Rojbin Özmen, who continues her work with TJN, spoke to ANF about the group’s new period and the problems Kurdish theatre has faced over the years.


‘If there is Kurdish music, why shouldn’t there be Kurdish theatre?’


Rojbin Özmen said TJN set out in the 1990s with the idea, “If there is Kurdish music, why shouldn’t there be Kurdish theatre?” She described the group’s founding and the difficulties it faced: “Teatra Jiyana Nû set out in 1992, after the establishment of the Mesopotamia Cultural Centre, with the idea, ‘If there is Kurdish music, why shouldn’t there be Kurdish theatre?’ and has continued its work ever since. It also played an important role in Kurdish theatre and was essentially a pioneer, because this was the first Kurdish theatre initiative of its kind. Until then, there had been nothing like it, either in terms of a venue or theatrical productions. There may have been earlier traces of Kurdish theatre, such as traditional performances in villages that were part of our culture. But in terms of performance on stage, this was a first.


Teatra Jiyana Nû began its work in the 1990s, which, as everyone knows, were among the most difficult years for the Kurds. It faced many difficulties then and continued to encounter many challenges in the years that followed. At times, the group became dispersed because of political bans and, at other times, because of financial difficulties. Most recently, we can say that its work had largely come to a halt for around five years, particularly after the banning of the play Berû.”


‘We are the third generation of Teatra Jiyana Nû’


Rojbin Özmen said they are the third generation of the group and did not want TJN to remain merely a memory of the past. She said they had set out again to carry on this tradition: “The group was unable to come together again and, in a sense, we can say that it naturally dispersed, although not by choice. Some of our friends went to Europe and continued their work there. Others went to Kurdistan and carried on their work there. They continued their work in one way or another, but Teatra Jiyana Nû itself had largely come to a standstill.


As the new generation, we speak with our teachers from time to time, and among ourselves we say that we truly are the third generation of Teatra Jiyana Nû. We wanted to carry on this tradition and continue this research and work. We did not want Teatra Jiyana Nû to remain there merely as a nostalgic memory or to be brought to an end. That is why we are now looking for new forms for Kurdish theatre, while also exploring what we can do and create in terms of the status of Kurdish theatre and how we can grow. On this basis, we want Teatra Jiyana Nû to reclaim its place and continue its work by building on this tradition.”


‘What matters is that children grow up with their own culture’


Rojbin Özmen said they had opened the new season with a children’s play and explained why they chose to begin with children: “When we came together again to ensure the continuity of Teatra Jiyana Nû, we had many discussions. We spoke with our teachers and experienced actors who had done this work before, and during this process we …

author: Unknown
title: Sites of historical memory and peace: Sacred domes
content:
Yazidis (Êzidî) do not visit the domes only on special days, holidays and during religious rituals; they also regard these places as sites of spiritual peace and visit them in their daily lives.


Looking at when the domes were built, it becomes clear that each was constructed in some of the most beautiful, elevated and strategic locations. This is significant both for protection and for being closer to nature and the sky.


Visitors entering the courtyards of the domes encounter an atmosphere of peace, tranquillity and purity that takes them away from the weariness of the outside world. Each dome symbolizes an important event, figure or period in Yazidi history.


A philosophy of purity, light and peace


One of the most distinctive characteristics of Yazidis is their attachment to the colour white.


In the Yazidi faith, white is not merely a style of dress but a deeply sacred symbol representing purity of heart and spirit, light, peace and authenticity.


Wearing white during religious rituals, prayers, visits to the domes and religious ceremonies reflects the unity of the community and the authenticity of the faith. The colour keeps alive in their minds and spirits a direct connection with the sun and light. Although the Yazidi community has endured many Fermans (genocides), hardships and changes throughout history, this culture has preserved its authenticity for more than a thousand years. Children are taught the principles, sacred values, philosophy and rituals of the Yazidi faith within their families and community from an early age.


No matter how much time passes or how ways of life change, the new generation’s attachment to the sacred domes and the tradition of wearing white ensures that the faith is not forgotten and continues as a living heritage.

author: Unknown
title: How can we call them dead?
content:
We were together at a morale event in 2017. A young, graceful woman comrade stepped onto the stage to read a poem. She was very short and endearing. We looked at her with smiles; there was something immediately lovable about her. But her face was deeply serious, and when we saw her expression, our smiles faded too.


She began to read her poem. Its title was How Could We Call Them Dead?


She was reading it in memory of 23 of our loved ones who had been martyred in an air strike on a single day that year. She was giving voice to our pain. Those 23 lives, each one beautiful, each one courageous. With coal-black eyebrows, golden hair, proud foreheads, mischievous ways and chubby cheeks, they were warm, deeply warm comrades. All of them so young. We buried our pain in our hearts, as we had done with so many comrades over the years. Hardest of all was not being able to announce their martyrdom at the time, so that the enemy would not rejoice or take courage and so that the impact of such attacks could be contained. Neither friend nor foe was told. Saying, “Until the day comes,” we carried their pain in our hearts and continued along the path, trying not to fall behind in the marathon to liberate our country. And that endearing yet serious comrade, with features as beautiful as though they had been drawn with a pencil, was offering us something to hold on to. She was giving us the strength to carry our pain.


Only the power of meaning can enable a person to bear such pain. Abdullah Öcalan said: “The person sustained by meaning and feeling is the strongest person.” Through our own experience, we have seen how vital, life-sustaining and liberating meaning and the power of meaning can be. We are now living through days of commemorations and condolences. Condolence gatherings are being held across our country. The families of our loved ones, whose martyrdom we could not announce until the day we had been waiting for and whose memory we carried in our hearts, have now been informed. Hundreds of such announcements would plunge another country into mourning and drive a society into profound despair. In Kurdistan, however, we witnessed the opposite. We encountered an ocean of meaning.


Commemorations and condolence gatherings were held for comrades whose bodies, in many cases, we could not even lay to rest. Under bombardment, we gathered whatever fragments of them we could find, dug into the earth and hid them away, thinking: “Perhaps one day we can return them to their mother, father or siblings.” Hundreds of lives, a number that cannot simply be spoken of lightly.


We watched our mothers stand with their heads held high and with dignity. We saw the effort they made to conceal their pain and remain steadfast, their fortitude, and the way they honoured their children once again by speaking of them in the most beautiful words. Each time, we remembered that endearing comrade, small in stature but immense in mind, that great comrade who herself was later martyred by bombs many times larger than her own body.


Although we could not be together with the mothers, fathers and families of our comrades, although we could not stand beside them, we kept consoling ourselves inwardly with the line: “How could we call them dead?” We hoped that perhaps the voice within us might become a resonance, a signal, an energy and somehow reach them. Our mothers and families, indeed, tell us even more powerfully that they are immortal, that they have not died. They say it through poetry, through kilam (traditional Kurdish oral songs), through words, through their eyes and through their gaze. It seems, then, that the voices within us do reach one another. The power of meaning and feeling has spread throughout Kurdistan.


The war that unfolded across the four parts of Kurdistan between 2015 and 2025 has yet to be told. Those who emerged from that war have still not been able to heal the wounds in their hearts.


I recently came across an account of its cost. It said that the Republic of Turkey spent $1 trillion on its war with the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK) between 1984 and 2016, and another $1.2 trillion between 2016 and 2024. These figures give some sense of what kind of war the last decade was and the intensity of the attacks that were carried out.


There were great, courageous and free people who stood with nothing but their small bodies against the bombs dropped by the jets and armed drones that Turkey’s security forces so proudly boast …

title: CPT report documents overcrowding, ill-treatment and isolation in Turkish prisons
content:
The Council of Europe’s Committee for the Prevention of Torture (CPT) has published two long-withheld reports on conditions in Turkish prisons and police detention facilities. The findings are based on visits conducted in January 2021 and February 2024. The reports were not made public until October 6, 2026, after the Turkish authorities agreed to their publication. The findings range from severe overcrowding and allegations of physical ill-treatment to years of de facto isolation in high-security prisons. The CPT paid particular attention to prisoners serving aggravated life sentences, as well as women and LGBTIQ+ prisoners.


During its 2021 visit, the delegation inspected 13 police and gendarmerie facilities, including police headquarters and counterterrorism units in Ankara, Diyarbakır and Istanbul. It also visited eight prisons, including women’s prisons in Istanbul-Bakırköy and Kayseri, a juvenile prison in Istanbul-Maltepe and a high-security prison in Diyarbakır.


The special visit in February 2024


focused on four high-security prisons in Antalya, Iğdır and Van, as well as two L-type prisons in Antalya and Maltepe, Istanbul. Particular attention was paid to the detention conditions of prisoners serving aggravated life sentences, as well as the situation of women, LGBTIQ+ prisoners and people held in solitary confinement for administrative or disciplinary reasons.


338,000 people in prison


The growth of the prison population has been particularly dramatic. At the end of 2019, around 290,000 people were imprisoned in Turkey. By January 2021, the number had fallen to around 192,000, largely against the backdrop of the COVID-19 pandemic. Even then, however, the CPT found overcrowding in most of the prisons it visited.


The trend subsequently reversed. According to official figures, around 338,000 people were in prison as of June 2024. This corresponded to approximately 395 prisoners per 100,000 inhabitants, making it the highest incarceration rate among Council of Europe member states at the time. The CPT calls on the Turkish authorities to give the highest priority to reducing the prison population and addressing the structural causes of overcrowding.


Allegations of beatings and falaka


At Antalya S-Type Prison, the CPT delegation encountered several allegations of physical ill-treatment in 2024. Prisoners reported being slapped, punched, kicked and beaten with batons. The Committee considered several of these accounts credible. In two cases, prisoners also reported being beaten on the soles of their feet with batons—a method of torture known as “falaka” (bastinado). In one case, the delegation observed injuries that were consistent with the prisoner’s account of ill-treatment.


The CPT calls for prison management and staff to be unequivocally informed that physical ill-treatment and the disproportionate use of force are unlawful. Public prosecutors, it says, must also investigate cases involving the use of force by prison staff more thoroughly.


Years of de facto solitary confinement


The CPT also sharply criticizes the conditions of prisoners serving aggravated life sentences. In the high-security prisons visited, a significant proportion of them had been held in de facto solitary confinement for months or even years. Some prisoners spent at least 21 hours a day alone in their cells. In some cases, regular out-of-cell activities were limited to daily outdoor exercise, which was also taken alone.


The CPT warns that prolonged isolation can have serious consequences for mental, somatic and social health and, under certain circumstances, may amount to inhuman or degrading treatment. The Turkish authorities are therefore called upon to take urgent steps at the prisons visited to ensure that all aggravated life -sentenced prisoners (and any other prisoners held alone in their cells) are offered meaningful human contact for at least two hours every day and preferably more. More generally, the Committee emphasises once again that the very concept of the detention regime of persons sentenced to aggravated life imprisonment, as defined in the law, is fundamentally flawed and should be subject to a complete overhaul.


Women and children held in unsuitable conditions


The CPT also found significant overcrowding in the L-type prisons in Antalya and Istanbul-Maltepe. In Antalya, some areas accommodating women were in poor structural and hygienic condition. Conditions for imprisoned mothers and their …

title: RAJIN on Kurdish Women Journalists’ Day: We will continue the struggle for free press undeterred
content:
The coordination of the Free Women’s Press (RAJIN, Ragihandina Azad a Jinan) has commemorated Kurdish journalist and revolutionary Gurbetelli Ersöz on the 29th anniversary of her death. Ersöz was the first woman to serve as editor-in-chief of a newspaper in Turkey. RAJIN paid tribute to her legacy for the free press and the women’s movement and declared that it would continue her struggle amid increasing repression.


Gurbetelli Ersöz was born in 1965 in the village of Akbulut in Elazığ. After studying chemistry at Çukurova University, she completed a master’s degree and worked as a research assistant. She became politically active in 1987 and was imprisoned in 1989. Following her release in 1993, she became editor-in-chief of the newspaper Özgür Gündem.


She was detained along with numerous employees of the newspaper and severely tortured while in police custody. Following another period of imprisonment lasting around six months and amid increasing threats from paramilitary structures, she joined the guerrilla ranks in the mountains of Kurdistan in 1995. There, she also assumed responsibilities within the women’s organization YAJK. On October 8, 1997, Ersöz was caught in an ambush by the KDP and lost her life in the ensuing clash.


“Not gone, but became the path herself”


Twenty-nine years after her death, RAJIN described Ersöz as a trailblazer whose political and journalistic legacy continues to live on. “Like all those who dedicated their lives knowing that the world they dreamed of could be built not through miracles but through resistance, Gurbetelli is not gone today; she has become the path herself,” the statement said.


RAJIN also marked Kurdish Women Journalists’ Day, which is observed in memory of Gurbetelli Ersöz. The day represents all women working in the media who carry forward the legacy of those who paid a heavy price in the pursuit of truth.


Repression shifts to the digital sphere


RAJIN pointed to the detention, imprisonment and prosecution of women journalists, as well as physical threats, obstruction of reporting, verbal abuse and sexist attacks, while sayinh that repression is also increasingly extending into digital media. Accounts belonging to journalists, news portals and media outlets are being shut down or subjected to access restrictions. Digital censorship has thus become another instrument for obstructing journalistic work and preventing the publication of information deemed inconvenient, it noted.


“In the face of all measures aimed at intimidating us and preventing us from uncovering the truth, we, as women journalists working in the tradition of the free press and following in Gurbetelli’s footsteps, will not back down,” RAJIN stated.


Against sexist language in the media


The coordination also placed the struggle for a free press within the context of the women’s freedom movement. It described wars and conflicts, femicides, poverty and the destruction of nature as manifestations of a patriarchal social order. At the same time, it added, systematic efforts are being made to render women’s struggles and achievements invisible.


RAJIN therefore announced that it would continue to challenge sexist attitudes, language and journalistic practices within the media itself. “We will continue to be the memory and voice of women and all those who are oppressed, to seek the truth, bring it to light and disseminate it,” the statement said.


In addition to Gurbetelli Ersöz, the organization also commemorated Şevin Bingöl, Şilan Aras, Deniz Fırat, Nûjiyan Erhan, Dilîşan Îbiş, Dilovan Gever, Emine Demir, Gulistan Tara, Hêro Bahadîn, Cihan Bilgin and Jineology researcher Nagihan Akarsel. Their memory, it said, continues to guide the struggle of women’s media.


Abdullah Öcalan also recalled Ersöz’s legacy last year on the occasion of the first presentation of the women journalists’ award named after Gurbetelli Ersöz. “Keeping Gurbetelli’s memory alive and passing her ideas and struggle on to future generations is a responsibility we all share,” RAJIN quoted from his message at the time.


The women’s press coordination announced that it would continue to expand its organizing efforts and carry forward the struggle in the tradition of Gurbetelli Ersöz: “Drawing strength from the culture of life and tradition of struggle left to us by our fallen comrades, we will expand and strengthen our organization.”

title: DEM Party: There has been no change in Öcalan’s conditions
content:
The DEM Party calls for concrete steps to further implement the peace and democratic society process. During a meeting with parliamentary correspondents in Ankara on Wednesday, parliamentary group chairs Gülistan Kılıç Koçyiğit and Sezai Temelli made clear that there has still been no progress, particularly regarding the working and communication conditions of Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan.


At the same time, the party calls for the implementation of the framework law that has already been adopted, the commencement of work by parliamentary bodies, and further legal measures to facilitate the return of members of the Kurdish freedom movement and the release of political prisoners.


“Framework law must be implemented in practice”


For the next stage of the process, the DEM Party now sees parliament as bearing primary responsibility. Koçyiğit called on the National Assembly to present a concrete roadmap and set in motion the mechanisms for implementing the framework law that has already been adopted. The establishment of the legal basis must now be followed by practical implementation, she said, warning that further delays could have a direct impact on the process as a whole.


According to the party, the parliamentary structures for the next phase must also begin their work. Temelli referred to the anticipated commission and emphasized that what matters is not so much the number of its members as its actual function.


“

Nothing has changed in Öcalan’s conditions

”


The DEM Party continues to regard Öcalan’s situation on Imrali as a key unresolved issue. “Nothing has changed in Mr. Öcalan’s conditions,” Koçyiğit said. Remarking that the Kurdish leader is the central interlocutor in the process, she said: “For him to fulfill this role, conditions must be created that allow him to work and communicate freely.”


The fact that a new residential building has now been constructed on Imrali does not change this, she said. What matters is whether Öcalan can work and communicate freely and establish contact with different social and political circles. These conditions, she stressed, are still not in place.


Direct contact with society


Temelli likewise stated that the isolation on Imrali has not ended. Representatives of various social groups and political parties want to visit Öcalan, but the necessary conditions for such visits have not yet been established. The DEM Party therefore calls for access to the prison island to be significantly expanded.


“In addition to political delegations, journalists, academics and intellectuals should also be able to travel to Imrali. Allowing these groups to visit the island would also strengthen confidence in the process,” Koçyiğit said. Relevant applications have already been submitted to the Ministry of Justice, she added.


Koçyiğit pointed out that: “For the further development of the process, it is important that Öcalan’s thoughts reach the public not exclusively through delegations and statements subsequently issued, but that direct engagement with society also become possible.”


No return without a legal framework


Another key focus is ensuring a legal basis for the next steps. Koçyiğit made clear that members of the Kurdish freedom movement in Europe cannot be expected to return to Turkey unless the necessary legal conditions are established. “No one will return without a law,” she said.


The legal restructuring must also address the situation of political prisoners, Koçyiğit said. She called for existing obstacles to their release to be removed and for the law on the execution of sentences to be reformed on the basis of the principle of equality. The DEM Party thus links the steps already initiated toward ending the armed conflict with its demand for corresponding legal and political changes on the part of the state.


“The will of the people must not be left to the MGK”


In this context, Temelli opposed making the further course of the process dependent on decisions by the National Security Council (MGK). “We recognize no will above the will of the people, nor do we accept such a will. Therefore, the will of the people must not be left to the discretion of the MGK,” he said.


For the next phase, he said, what is needed instead is a political language of peace and functioning democratic institutions.

author: Unknown
title: Hatimoğulları: What is the National Security Council still waiting for?
content:
DEM Party co-chair Tülay Hatimoğulları has criticized delays in the peace and democratic society process and called for concrete steps. Neither have the envisaged mechanisms been fully set in motion, nor have Abdullah Öcalan’s working and communication conditions fundamentally changed, she stated.


Speaking at an extraordinary party congress in Iğdır province, Hatimoğulları pointed to growing uncertainty over the future course of the process. “What is going to happen? Why is the process not moving forward? What is the National Security Council still waiting for? What are the confirmation and determination still waiting for?” she asked.


Council for Disarmament and Strategic Coordination has not yet begun its work


At the center of her criticism was the Council for Disarmament and Strategic Coordination envisaged under the framework law. Although there is an understanding regarding Öcalan’s role within this mechanism, it has yet to be activated. “This commission is still not active and has not begun its work. What are they waiting for?” Hatimoğulları said. As a result, key structures intended to move the process into its next phase remain unable to function, she said and called for the necessary steps to be taken without further delay.


“We want to speak with Öcalan”


The politician also sees a need for action regarding Öcalan’s conditions on Imrali. Journalists, she said, are still unable to travel to the island, and Öcalan cannot hold talks with anyone outside the Imrali delegation. The DEM Party leadership is also still waiting for the opportunity to speak with him directly.


“Although this has been discussed several times, we have still not been sent to the island,” Hatimoğulları said. “We want to speak with Mr. Öcalan. For the process to continue, his working conditions and ability to hold talks must also be changed.”


“This does not require an MGK decision”


Hatimoğulları linked her criticism of the delays to demands for immediate legal and democratic steps. She called for the implementation of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) rulings and for the release of Selahattin Demirtaş, Figen Yüksekdağ and the other politicians imprisoned in the Kobanê case. She stressed that there was no need to wait for a decision by the National Security Council before taking these steps.


Hatimoğulları also reiterated the demand for the release of those imprisoned in the Gezi case and cultural philanthropist Osman Kavala. The elected mayors of municipalities placed under state-appointed trustees must also be reinstated, Hatimoğulları said, emphasizing that existing court rulings and democratic rights should not be made contingent on further decisions.


Kenan Kaya and Raşide Temiz elected co-chairs


At the party congress that followed, Kenan Kaya and Raşide Temiz were elected the new co-chairs of the DEM Party’s provincial organization in Iğdır.

title: KCDK-E and TJK-E call for Europe-wide actions for Öcalan
content:
The Congress of Democratic Societies of Kurdistan in Europe (KCDK-E) and the Kurdish Women’s Movement in Europe (TJK-E) have called for actions across Europe to mark the 28th anniversary of the international plot against Abdullah Öcalan. Demonstrations and rallies have been announced in cities including Düsseldorf, Berlin, Hamburg, Frankfurt, Bremen, Bern, London, Stockholm, Brussels, Paris and Vienna. The mobilization centers on demands for Öcalan’s physical freedom and for conditions that would enable negotiations and a democratic solution to the Kurdish question to move forward.


The process referred to as the international plot began on October 9, 1998, when Öcalan was forced to leave Syria amid intense political and military pressure on the country. This was followed by a months-long odyssey through various countries, ending on February 15, 1999, with his abduction from the Kenyan capital Nairobi to Turkey. The Kurdish leader has been held on the prison island of Imrali ever since.


Attack on the will of the Kurdish people


KCDK-E and TJK-E described the events beginning on October 9, 1998, as an international intervention directed not only against Öcalan but also against the political achievements and the Kurdish people’s will for freedom. According to the two organizations, international powers and NATO, alongside regional states, were particularly involved in the plot. “Their aim was to keep the Kurdish people without status, break their will and prevent democratic and emancipatory developments in the Middle East.”


The two umbrella organizations also criticized the role of international institutions and human rights organizations in their response to Öcalan’s prison conditions. They stated that years of silence over the isolation on Imrali are unacceptable.


Öcalan’s call is a response to the plot


KCDK-E and TJK-E explicitly placed this year’s mobilization within the context of the peace and democratic society process. With his call of February 27, 2025, Öcalan opened a path toward the equal coexistence of peoples, the organizations stated. His physical freedom is therefore not only a demand of Kurdish society, but also a prerequisite for the political process to move forward, they underlined.


“We state unequivocally: The path to a peaceful solution to the Kurdish question, the freedom of the Kurdish people and the resolution of the historical crises in the Middle East runs through the physical freedom of Abdullah Öcalan,” the statement said.


According to KCDK-E and TJK-E, the isolation on Imrali does not affect Öcalan alone: “The isolation on Imrali is a chain imposed on the rights of the Kurdish people and on the future of the peoples of Turkey and the entire Middle East.”


“Now is the time to expand the freedom campaign”


KCDK-E and TJK-E called on the Kurdish population, solidarity groups and the democratic public to participate in the announced actions. The mobilization is not intended to be limited to Europe. Activities have also been announced in Canada and Australia.


“Now is the time to expand the freedom campaign and fill the squares,” the organizations stated. The aim is to increase pressure on the international community and make the demand for Öcalan’s freedom more visible. The statement concludes with the demand: “Abdullah Öcalan must be released immediately, and the way must be opened for negotiations and a democratic solution.”

title: ISIS carries out another attack in Hawija
content:
Another attack by the terrorist group Islamic State (ISIS) has taken place within a short period of time in Hawija, southwest of Kirkuk. Late Tuesday evening, ISIS members attacked a base belonging to the 2nd Battalion of the 61st Brigade of the Hashd al-Shaabi. Troops stationed at the base returned fire. No deaths or injuries were reported.


The attack took place in the Bargliya–Danadish area, where an Iraqi Federal Police post had been attacked just one day earlier. Two police officers were killed and several others injured in that attack. Security measures in Hawija were subsequently tightened.


The Federal Police initially announced a nighttime curfew from 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. It was later clarified that the curfew applies only to the Danadish sector, which comprises five villages. Freedom of movement remained largely unaffected in other parts of Hawija.

author: Unknown
title: YRJ on October 7: Women’s journalism documents struggle and history
content:
On the occasion of Kurdish Women Journalists’ Day on October 7, the Association of Women Journalists in Rojava (YRJ) has commemorated Gurbetelli Ersöz, Dilîşan Îbiş and Dilovan Gever, as well as all those from the free press who lost their lives. “For Kurdish women, journalism is not merely a profession, but a means of documenting history, making social realities visible and carrying women’s voices to the world,” it said.


In a written statement, the YRJ paid tribute to the path forged by Kurdish women journalists through their words, writings and images. Under the most difficult conditions, it said, they documented the truth and brought women’s experiences, struggles and problems in particular into the public sphere.


Tribute to Gurbetelli Ersöz


YRJ attributed particular significance to journalist and guerrilla commander Gurbetelli Ersöz, who lost her life in 1997 during the so-called “Southern War.” The day of her death is observed as Kurdish Women Journalists’ Day. Ersöz is regarded as one of the formative figures of Kurdish women’s journalism. The YRJ recalled that today’s women’s journalism builds on the work and sacrifices of the women journalists who pioneered and continued this path under difficult conditions.


The statement also commemorated Dilîşan Îbiş and Dilovan Gever. Îbiş lost her life on October 12, 2017, and Gever on October 13, 2019. Both documented Rojava’s resistance against the terrorist organization Islamic State (ISIS) and the Turkish occupation on various war fronts.


‘Women have broken through the wall of silence’


“Through words and images, women have broken through the wall of silence, documented events and brought the truth to light,” the YRJ stated. “Women’s journalism is not limited to reporting on current events. It documents women’s struggle and resistance, makes their problems visible and carries their voices beyond social and geographical boundaries.”


“Today and in all the phases to come, women journalists will continue to follow the issues affecting women and convey them to the entire world,” the statement said. The YRJ vowed that it would continue its efforts to further develop women’s journalism, documenting social developments as well as preserving collective memory.

author: Unknown
title: Geothermal development threatens villages in the Zilan Valley
content:
In the Zilan Valley near Erciş district in the province of Van, the conflict over geothermal development in the region is intensifying. The villages of Şorik (İkizçalı), Karakilise (İşbaşı) and Çaxirbeg (Çakırbey) see their living environment threatened by the expansion of the projects. Residents report that the possible evacuation of the villages is now also being discussed and that signatures are being collected.


According to the information available so far, no official evacuation order has been issued. However, work sites and drilling areas have already been established in Karakilise and Çaxirbeg. The projects are therefore directly encroaching on residential areas, agricultural land and the livelihoods of the local population.


The conflict is not new. State-backed geothermal development in the Zilan Valley has been underway since at least 2020. Since then, drilling operations, further planning and large-scale tenders for the exploitation of geothermal resources have followed.


Project launched in 2020


At the end of November 2020, the Eastern Anatolia Development Agency (DAKA) and the Van Governor’s Office signed an agreement for a project to develop geothermal resources for agricultural use in Erciş. The project was part of the Turkish Ministry of Industry and Technology’s support program for so-called attraction centers.


With a budget of 2.6 million Turkish lira at the time, the project envisaged the exploration and development of thermal water resources as well as the planning of the necessary pipeline infrastructure. The aim was to establish a specialized greenhouse zone where geothermal energy would enable year-round vegetable production.


The use of geothermal energy for greenhouse cultivation did not remain merely a plan on paper. In June 2023, drilling operations in Çaxirbeg reached thermal water with a temperature of 65 degrees Celsius at a depth of 750 meters. Ozan Balcı, then governor of Van and state-appointed trustee of the Metropolitan Municipality, announced plans to increase the number of geothermal wells. The water was to be used to heat greenhouses.


The agricultural use of geothermal energy is therefore an implemented component of the project. At the same time, the development of the valley’s geothermal resources expanded significantly in geographical scope over the following years.


Criticism over discharge of thermal water


As drilling operations expanded, their ecological impact also came under greater scrutiny. As early as the summer of 2026, environmental groups in Van drew attention to the discharge of thermal water from the drilling areas. They warned that liquids containing heavy metals could enter irrigation systems and the Koçköprü Reservoir.


Residents also report that contaminated thermal waters from the current operations are being discharged into the valley. There are concerns about the potential impact on soil, water resources, agriculture and, consequently, the livelihoods of the villages.


However, the information available so far does not indicate which heavy metals have been detected in connection with the current operations or at what concentrations. Water contamination therefore remains one of the key issues that must be clarified as development of the area continues.


Zilan Valley is a geologically sensitive area


Interest in the region is linked to its considerable geothermal potential. At the same time, it is a complex geological system. A study published in 2022 in the Journal of the Institute of Natural Sciences of Van Yüzüncü Yıl University identifies around eleven thermal water sites along the Erciş-Zilan-Ilıca Valley. The springs are largely aligned parallel to the Zilan Fault.


The study describes the Zilan Fault as an active, northeast-to-southwest-trending left-lateral strike-slip fault. Thermal waters reach the surface along the fault structures. Active tectonics and volcanism are also the basis of the region’s geothermal potential.


In addition to the hot springs, this natural environment includes groundwater, travertine formations, river terraces and the Zilan River. The scientific study thus documents the close interconnection between the valley’s geological and hydrological structures. However, it does not examine the specific environmental impacts of the current drilling and development activities.

author: Redazione_web
title: Noi restiamo là. Pinelli: un omicidio di stato
content:
Mi piacerebbe sapere cosa dirà il 18 novembre prossimo al Politeama di Genova Mario Calabresi sul tema ‘Terrore e diritti – Anni Settanta’ in compagnia di Benedetta Tobagi, Sara Poma e Marco Damilano. Ma dato che non abito a Genova e non ho alcuna intenzione di pagare il biglietto per entrare mi dovrò accontentare dei resoconti del Secolo XIX.


Quello che so è quello che è emerso nella recente polemica sorta dalle sue dichiarazioni nei confronti di Adriano Sofri, fatte nel corso della trasmissione televisiva ‘La confessione’ condotta da Peter Gomez.


Durante la trasmissione, Calabresi aveva detto “Non ci siamo mai parlati con Adriano Sofri, ma prima della fine della sua vita sarebbe bello e prezioso verso di noi se, anziché barricarsi come ha fatto per tanto tempo dietro a mille distinguo, dicesse una parola di verità”, cioè in poche parole rendesse non solo confessione piena dell’omicidio che a suo tempo gli venne accollato, quello del padre, avvenuto a Milano il 17 maggio 1972, ma magari raccontasse un qualcosa di più utile a seppellire definitivamente la memoria di quegli anni, ridotti ad un ammasso di sangue.


Ovviamente non si è fatta attendere la replica dell’ex-leader di Lotta Continua, condannato in via definitiva a 22 anni di carcere come mandante dell’assassinio (pena interamente scontata e conclusa nel 2012). Attraverso una lettera aperta, Sofri ha respinto con decisione la sollecitazione di Calabresi, ribadendo perentoriamente la propria estraneità ai fatti: “Io dico che sono innocente, e che il tormentato itinerario giudiziario che abbiamo attraversato è stato dolosamente ingiusto.” Nel contempo Sofri afferma di avere più volte espresso direttamente a Gemma Capra, la vedova del commissario, “dispiacere per i modi dell’accanita campagna di Lotta Continua contro Luigi Calabresi, assumendomene la responsabilità piena (…). Io ero dalla parte di Pino Pinelli, e sono rimasto là.”


Non ho, confesso, simpatia per molte posizioni espresse attualmente da Sofri – e nemmeno della riduzione del suo giornale di allora a propagatore d’astio piuttosto che di stimolatore di verità, considerando che solo la virulenta campagna condotta dalle colonne di LC costrinse Calabresi a denunciarne il direttore, Pio Baldelli, e a sostenere un processo che gli si rivolse contro almeno fino all’opportunistica sospensione – ma debbo riconoscergli una coerenza di fondo, espressa in articoli, saggi, libri, riguardo la vicenda dell’assassinio del nostro compagno Giuseppe Pinelli. In effetti Adriano è “rimasto là”, così come ci siamo rimasti noi nel continuare a denunciare questo omicidio di Stato, avvenuto nella stanza al quarto piano della Questura di Milano, alla presenza di uomini dell’Ufficio politico capitanati dal commissario Luigi Calabresi e da quelli dell’Ufficio Affari Riservati diretti da Federico Umberto D’Amato nella notte tra il 15 e il 16 dicembre 1969. Il giudice D’Ambrosio con la sua ordinanza – con la quale nel 1975 derubricò la causa della morte di Pino ad un malore che lo avrebbe spinto incredibilmente al di là della balaustra della finestra – escluse la presenza del commissario da quella stanza dimenticandosi di interrogare l’unico testimone civile (cioè non appartenente a polizia, CC, ecc.) presente nel corridoio, quel Pasquale Valitutti che ha sempre negato di aver visto uscire il commissario da quella stanza. Ma non solo, un bel libro denuncia, scritto qualche anno fa, da Gabriele Fuga ed Enrico Maltini (edito da Zero in Condotta e poi riproposto, ampliato, da Colibrì) ha messo in luce un fatto di cui nessuno ha mai parlato, né dentro né fuori la Questura: la presenza di uomini dei servizi venuti appositamente da Roma per condurre le indagini nella direzione voluta, la criminalizzazione degli anarchici e, conseguentemente, l’avvio della svolta autoritaria contro il movimento di contestazione giovanile e operaia. E anche di questo nessuno, né dentro né fuori il Tribunale, se n’è mai fatto carico.


Sarebbe interessante se nell’incontro al Politeama di Genova venissero delle parole di verità ‘vera’; sul palco ci sono giornalist* di fama e di spessore, studios* del periodo, vorranno andare a fondo delle cose o rimarranno a coltivare il loro orticello di ‘buoni’ sentimenti fasulli?


Mario Calabresi ha già scelto da che parte stare (non avevo dubbi): la memoria condivisa di quegli anni deve passare dalla manipolazione, quando non dall’oblio, dei fatti, dall’abiura e dalla dissociazione, mai dal riconoscimento …

title: Trump Won’t Reimburse Taxpayers for Ads Promoting Himself Paid for by Government
content:
Trump has spent at least $10 million in taxpayer funds on TV ads ahead of the midterm elections.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

White House staffers indicated on Tuesday that President Donald Trump will not be reimbursing the government for the millions of dollars in taxpayer funds he has used to produce promotional TV ads ahead of this year’s midterm elections.

In a post on Monday, Trump indicated that he would not use taxpayer funds to produce future commercials. Despite pressure from both sides of the political aisle, Trump blamed progressives for complaining about the ads, which conclude with the tag, “Paid for by the U.S. government.”

“The Radical Left is upset with the fact that I am taking Ads, which I consider to be a positive promotion for our Great U.S.A., and paying for them with U.S.A. money,” he wrote on Truth Social. “This is a rather standard thing to do but, rather than doing that, although nothing will make them happy, I have decided to do the Patriotic Ads, among others, and pay for them myself, and with money I raised for MAGA, Inc.”

A White House aide said on Tuesday that the president’s social media post “was not referring to reimbursement.”

As of Monday, at least $10.1 million had already been spent funding the television spots. The White House has not indicated whether it will continue using the full $20 million that had originally been allocated from federal government sources.

Trump’s plan to use a super PAC to fund future ads is questionable, as it is illegal for a president to direct how a super PAC affiliated with them spends its funds.

The administration has tried to justify the ads by describing them as “public service announcements.” But the commercials largely feature Trump and his speeches from campaign events during the 2024 presidential race. Within the ad, he attacks so-called “communists” and “Marxists” — terms he has errantly used to describe Democrats in the past, making it difficult to describe the ads as non-partisan promotions of the country.

Trump is wrong in claiming that “radical leftists” are the only group of people who take issue with the ads. According to a recent Reuters/Ipsos poll, 86 percent of Americans say the ads are inappropriate, while only 9 percent say they support the use of taxpayer dollars to fund them. That includes four in five Republican-leaning voters in the poll who disagree with the ads being funded by the government.

One former Republican White House ethics lawyer said the ads could be grounds for impeachment.

“This is very dangerous. We do not allow government-sponsored propaganda in the United States,” said Richard Painter, who served during the administration of former President George W. Bush, adding that the ads are an “abuse of power” that could amount to “an impeachable offense.”

title: Abahlali baseMjondolo archive - 2005 - 2026
content:
Abahlali was formed at a meeting of 34 people held in Durban on 4 October 2005. When the movement celebrated its 21st anniversary in Durban on 4 October 2026 it had more than 200 000 members across five of South Africa's nine provinces.


In 21 years of struggle it has won large tracts of urban land, extracted significant policy concessions and resolutely opposed the xenophobia that is systemically used to divided impoverished and working class people in South Africa. It has also built strong connections with radical movements around the world and has, in recent years, moved towards building communes.


The struggle has come at a high cost. As of 4 October 2026 26 lives have been lost in the course of the struggle.


This archive runs from the movement's formation in 2005 till 4 October 2026 and includes a complete list of all the statements it has issued, memoranda delivered at marches as well as the articles and speeches by its members which are archived on the movement's website.

title: Πρεμιέρα του ντοκιμαντέρ «11 χρόνια δίκη της Χρυσής Αυγής: Οι άνθρωποί της»

Έντεκα χρόνια πέρασαν από εκείνη την 20ή Απριλίου 2015, όταν άνοιγε η αυλαία μιας από τις σημαντικότερες δίκες της σύγχρονης ελληνικής ιστορίας. Ένας μακρύς δικαστικός αγώνας που ολοκληρώθηκε με την τελεσίδικη αναγνώριση της Χρυσής Αυγής ως εγκληματικής οργάνωσης, δικαιώνοντας τα θύματα και όσους/ες επέμειναν στην αναζήτηση της αλήθειας και της δικαιοσύνης.


Το ντοκιμαντέρ «11 ΧΡΟΝΙΑ ΔΙΚΗΣ ΤΗΣ ΧΡΥΣΗΣ ΑΥΓΗΣ: ΟΙ ΑΝΘΡΩΠΟΙ ΤΗΣ», είναι η πρώτη μεγάλη παραγωγή της ΣΕΛΗΝΗ και αποτελεί έναν απολογισμό αυτής της μακράς διαδρομής μέσα από τις φωνές εκείνων που τη βίωσαν από κοντά. Πρόκειται για μια ταινία διάρκειας 95 λεπτών, της Χρύσας Λύκου, σε σκηνοθεσία του Στέλιου Ζαχαρίου, η οποία προσπαθεί να καταγράψει την εμπειρία της απώλειας και τη μετατόπιση της σε αγώνα, τις σκέψεις και τα συναισθήματα που αναπτύχθηκαν μέσα στις δικαστικές αίθουσες καθώς και τα συμπεράσματα ανθρώπων που συμμετείχαν καθοριστικά στην παρακολούθηση, την ανάδειξη και τη δικαίωση της υπόθεσης.


Συγγενείς θυμάτων, τα ίδια τα θύματα, δικηγόροι, δημοσιογράφοι και φωτορεπόρτερ, καταθέτουν τον προσωπικό τους απολογισμό μετά την τελεσίδικη απόφαση. Αναστοχάζονται την πορεία της δίκης, τις δυσκολίες, τις καθυστερήσεις, τις κοινωνικές και πολιτικές προεκτάσεις της υπόθεσης, αλλά και την τεράστια σημασία της ιστορικής καταδίκης της Χρυσής Αυγής ως εγκληματικής οργάνωσης.


Ήδη οι πρώτες ημέρες προβολής του ντοκιμαντέρ έχουν γίνει sold out.

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: Labour Council’s Palantir Investments Increased 1,200% During Gaza Genocide
content:
Labour-run Camden Council’s investment holdings in Israel-linked tech firm Palantir have increased by more than 1,200% since October 2023, new figures show.


The figures were obtained by the

Palestine Solidarity Campaign (PSC) and first reported on by Declassified UK

. 


Camden Council’s leader, Sagal Abdi-Wali, is running for Labour against Green leader Zack Polanski in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection on Thursday, hoping to win Keir Starmer’s old seat. Abdi-Wali has led the council since May this year. 


Palantir shares in the council’s local government pension fund were worth £3.65m as of December 2025, up from £276,444 in October 2023. The company has provided Israel’s defence ministry with technology amid the genocide in Gaza. 


The council has holdings in 60 companies accused of complicity in Israeli human rights abuses in Palestine, the new figures also show, and the value of these has risen from £104m to £133.5m since June 2024.


As of 31 December 2025, Camden’s pension fund had more than £2.4bn of registered investments, including more than £10m in defence companies also tied to the Israeli military, including Boeing (£1.69m), Lockheed Martin (£1.12m) and Israeli weapons manufacturer Elbit Systems (£46,837). Campaigners have repeatedly called on the council to divest.


In January 2025, more than

4,000 people signed a petition

 demanding an audit of the pension fund and possible divestment from arms companies, triggering a council debate. The matter was subsequently referred to its pension committee. 


A

council-commissioned audit later identified £15.9m of investments

 across 46 companies as having significant human rights concerns related to conflict zones.


But the council’s wider holdings in companies identified by PSC as complicit in Israel’s occupation and violations of Palestinian rights have continued to rise in value.


Abdi-Wali has not commented on Gaza or divestment, according to a review of her public statements cited by Declassified, and did not respond to requests for comment.


Camden Council’s pension fund investment policy

 says it is committed to responsible investment.


A spokesperson for the council told Declassified that it has strengthened its approach to environmental, social and human rights concerns.


“We have a duty to act with the best long-term financial interests of members but, alongside this, we also expect environmental issues, social values, and human rights to play a central role in decision-making,” he said.
