author: Andrea DiP
title: Há três anos os palestinos pagam pelo 7 de outubro
content:
Quis o destino que eu estivesse na Cisjordânia neste 07 de outubro, e que essa coluna fosse publicada no exato dia em que,

3 anos atrás, o ataque terrorista do Hamas que resultou na morte de cerca 1000 pessoas entre civis e militares, deu início a um massacre cometido pelo

Estado de Israel

 que, até agora, somente na

Faixa de Gaza, já matou mais de 75 mil e feriu mais de 170 mil palestinos. 


Eu sei que o Brasil pega fogo neste momento e é difícil falar em outra coisa ou pensar em um povo que está tão longe geograficamente. Mas talvez nós possamos aprender uma coisa ou duas sobre resistência e resiliência

 com um povo que vem sendo oprimido, colonizado e sofre tentativas reiteradas de apagamento há mais de 100 anos. 


Meus avós são sobreviventes do Holocausto. Minha avó polonesa e meu avô romeno passaram por campos de concentração e tinham números tatuados neles. Ainda jovens migraram para o Brasil, onde se conheceram e formaram família. E é também por respeito a essa história que não posso me calar diante de um genocídio étnico que acontece

live stream

 nos celulares na palma de nossas mãos. 


Nos últimos dias estive rodando pela Cisjordânia, visitando comunidades palestinas que estão sendo despejadas, torturad

as, roubadas e dizimadas por milícias israelenses formadas por colonos e por militares.

 A Cisjordânia é um território palestino que fica no Oriente Médio, situado na margem ocidental do rio Jordão, entre Israel e a Jordânia. É dividida em três zonas administrativas – zonas A, B e C –  segundo os Acordos de Oslo, assinados na década de 1990, que previam transferir gradualmente o controle do território para a Autoridade Palestina. A área teoricamente estaria sob controle total da Palestina. A área B teria um controle misto entre Israel e Palestina e a área C, cerca de 60% da Cisjordânia, está sob controle israelense total, tanto para administração civil quanto para segurança. 


Mas atualmente esses contornos estão cada vez mais borrados, com colonos israelenses tomando cada vez mais áreas.


Tudo isso ainda vai virar reportagem e indico o Pauta Pública desta sexta-feira (09/10) com o diretor geral do Centro de Assistência Jurídica e Direitos Humanos de Jerusalém (JLAC) e membro do Conselho de Comissários da Comissão Independente de Direitos Humanos da Palestina (ICHR), Issam Aruri, que traz uma verdadeira aula sobre o conflito na região. 


Mas queria contar aqui na coluna uma


das histórias que mais me marcou até agora: A de uma mulher de 67 anos, moradora de um vilarejo em Masafer Yatta

, que fica nas colinas ao sul da cidade de Hebrom, cerca de 70km ao sul de Ramallah – capital administrativa da Cisjordânia. Não vou revelar seu nome por motivos óbvios. Mas

sua vila está totalmente cercada por


assentamentos israelenses, que tentam a custo de barbárie expulsar os palestinos que estão ali há dezenas de gerações, vivendo da colheita de azeitonas e do pastoreio de ovelhas e cabras. 


Sua vila não tem água encanada nem luz. Se vê apenas pedras, areia, pequenas casas e barracões. Os cabos de energia passam por cima da comunidade, de um lado a outro, para os assentamentos israelenses, mas os palestinos não podem usar. Foi instalado um portão na estrada, que pode ser fechado pelos soldados a qualquer momento e por tempo indeterminado, impedindo os moradores de entrar ou sair, mesmo que em emergência médica.

 Essa é uma prática bastante comum na região. Até mesmo ruas dentro de comunidades são fechadas indiscriminadamente pelas forças israelenses. 


“Foi aqui que um colono israelense matou meu filho”. A senhora aponta para um ponto do centro de convivência, que já foi destruído e reconstruído várias vezes e que abriga o único banheiro disponível para a comunidade.

 As casas tinham banheiro. Mas eles foram destruídos ou absurdamente declarados como zonas militares, tornando-se inacessíveis aos moradores. Sua filha mora em uma casa há poucos metros dali e não pode usar o próprio banheiro nem construir outro sem permissão. Mais: o celeiro, que fica no quintal da casa, foi declarado “zona militar” e trancado, então a família não pode levar os animais para o pasto ou mesmo chegar perto do pequeno barracão. O exército israelense passa por lá uma vez na semana (quando muito) para alimentar as ovelhas e cabras, que estão obviamente morrendo paulatinamente. 


“Um colono entrou na comunidade e atirou na cabeça do meu filho. Meu neto, aquele ali  – aponta para um gurizinho de uns 3 anos – estava no colo …

author: Hassan Alnaser
title: How the Dagalos’ ever tightening hold on power destabilized the RSF project
content:
Daein. Amid the rain showers veiling the city in the first week of August, the fourth August of the war, four-wheel-drive vehicles pull up one after another. Out of them come men who know the villages and firgan that have sent fighters into the Rapid Support Forces, who know the families who have been giving up their sons to war since April 2023.


Abdel Rahim Dagalo sits opposite the Rizeigat tribal omdas who have come from across Darfur’s different localities. Trees ring the meeting place, shielding it from the eyes of drones. He wants one thing from them: to mobilize again.


The tribal leaders begin by talking about the soldiers wounded in battle, about fighters who came home missing limbs, a source who attended the meeting tells Mada Masr. They speak of families who lost their sons, of men who went to the front and never came back, and of communities that, for more than three years, have borne the cost of a war whose military and political decisions they have no hand in.


Then the conversation turns to the men the leadership still wants to send to fight. The omdas say they can no longer persuade their tribes to mobilize as they did in the first years of the war. The war has dragged on, and the losses have piled up. People have begun asking about the sons they sent to the front, about treatment for the wounded, asking what place these communities that gave up their men will hold in the political order being talked about.


At one point, one of the tribal leaders breaks with the language usually upheld in official gatherings. He tells Abdel Rahim that the leadership has left them and their tribes alone to deal with the consequences of the war. He asks him to go with them to the villages and speak to the women and families, to persuade them himself to send their sons.


The remark angers Abdel Rahim. He accuses the tribal leaders of colluding with the military and threatens to send them to Nyala’s Dagris prison. Several cut him off. “You don’t threaten us with prison,” one of the leaders says. The nazir and his deputy step in to contain the situation, and Abdel Rahim Dagalo leaves Daein angry.


But the problem is bigger than one angry meeting, than one rainy day in Daein.


No, that meeting in the first week of August was the culmination of a slowly building tension at the core of the RSF’s political project.


Since the start of the war, over successive battlefronts, successive planning meetings, in the administrative halls that the paramilitary group hastily erected, the RSF had circled around the same issue: how can they mount a formidable challenge to the historic government in Khartoum?


The question couldn’t be merely thought about as a military challenge. For the RSF’s leaders, it was a totalizing question that required a complete recasting of social relations and a transcending of the historical archetype of the rebel group from the state’s margins, sources inside the RSF’s leadership and former advisors who have spoken to Mada Masr over the last six months say.


To pull off such a feat has required a consistent push for greater and greater centralization of power, the sources say.


Two tracks emerged within the tangle the war’s continuation has produced. Abdel Rahim represents the military track — the belief that the answer comes with the sound of Land Cruiser engines, that military power dictates its own terms. He is the one who mobilized fighters from every corner, whose strategy succeeded in securing the RSF political influence.


The other track holds that a parallel civilian authority must be built with enough political capacity to exert negotiating pressure and impose its terms, represented by Hemedti, the younger and most trusted Dagalo brother in the RSF’s leadership. He is the godfather of the RSF project, going back to the days when they were rovers in Nyala’s plains, eating manasees in the shade of Cruisers paid for with ousted-President Omar al-Bashir’s money.


But if centralization could save the project, it could also undo it.


With every passing month, the state casts the “rebels” back into its sacred shadow. One military defection here, one political defection there. Each proving the failure of the RSF’s attempt at centralization — the kind of centralization that Hemedti once broke with the state over, when he

cast

himself as the son of the margins against the center, and is now trying to restore in the form of a project whose capital is Nyala. The other, out in the field, has …

title: When history accelerates: Maricarmen's eviction
content:
Abahlali was formed at a meeting of 34 people held in Durban on 4 October 2005. When the movement celebrated its 21st anniversary in Durban on 4 October 2026 it had more than 200 000 members across five of South Africa's nine provinces.


In 21 years of struggle it has won large tracts of urban land, extracted significant policy concessions and resolutely opposed the xenophobia that is systemically used to divided impoverished and working class people in South Africa. It has also built strong connections with radical movements around the world and has, in recent years, moved towards building communes.


The struggle has come at a high cost. As of 4 October 2026 26 lives have been lost in the course of the struggle.


This archive runs from the movement's formation in 2005 till 4 October 2026 and includes a complete list of all the statements it has issued, memoranda delivered at marches as well as the articles and speeches by its members which are archived on the movement's website.

title: Smart’ta direniş çadırı kuruldu
content:
Smart Solar Aliağa Fabrikası'nda işçiler taleplerinin karşılanmaması nedeniyle fabrika önüne direniş çadırı kurdu. İşçilerin Tes İş Sendikası'ndan DİSK Enerji-Sen'e geçiş yapmasının ardından 7 işçi işten çıkarılmış, işçiler işten atmalara karşı 4 gün üretimi durdurarak eyleme geçmişti. Patronun işçilerin taleplerini kabul ederek görüşmeler yürütüleceğini iletmesinin ardından işçiler eylemi sonlandırmıştı.

15 Eylül'de bitirilen eylemlerin ardından patron ve sendika yöneticileri toplamda üç görüşme gerçekleştirdi. İlk iki görüşmeden taleplere ilişkin somut adımların atılmaması ve yeni görüşme tarihine dair dönüş yapılmaması nedeniyle, Enerji Sen 29 Eylül Salı günü eylemlerin yeniden başlayacağını duyurmuştu. Eylem duyurusunun ardından hızla görüşme talebi ileten patron yeni görüşme için tarih vermek zorunda kaldı.

Yapılan bu son görüşmede ise; patron atılan işçiler için kıdem ve ihbar tazminatlarına ek olarak 2 brüt maaş vererek işe geri almamayı, temmuz ayından beri yatırılmayan enflasyon zammını Ocak ayından itibaren 12 taksit şeklinde yatırmayı, gelecek olan Ocak enflasyon zammını ise bir sene sonra vermeyi teklif etmişti. İşçilerin taleplerinin karşılanmadığı bu son görüşmenin ardından işçiler fabrika önünde direniş çadır kurarak her gün eylemlerine devam edeceğini ilan etti.

İşçilerin eylem kararının ardından şirket tarafından işçilere mesaj atılarak 16-24 vardiyasının iptal edildiği, servis gönderilmeyeceği iletildi. Henüz net olmayan bilgilere göre patronun fabrikada makina tamiri ve hammadde eksikliği nedeniyle 10 günlük üretim durdurma gerçekleştireceği söyleniyor. İşçiler bu durumu patronun eylemleri baltalamak için yaptığı yönünde değerlendirmeler de bulunurken eylemlerine vazgeçmeden devam edeceklerini dile getirdi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Luis Feliz Leon
title: Amazon Package Drivers Rev Up Organizing to Become Direct Employees
content:
The workers who wear Amazon vests and drive vans with the company’s logo aren’t legally employed by Amazon. But that could change in New York City, under legislation that Teamsters and Amazon workers alongside the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) are organizing to pass.


The Delivery Protection Act would require Amazon, alongside FedEx and other companies, to directly employ drivers rather than rely on third-party subcontractors. It would also establish safety, training, and labor standards for delivery drivers.


As of October 3, workers and allies had knocked on 11,446 doors across the Bronx, Manhattan, Brooklyn, and Staten Island, according to the Teamsters.


Across the country, 4,500 tiny companies act as Amazon’s delivery service partners (DSPs)—meaning these contractors are the nominal employers, even while the logistics giant retains control.


“For years, Amazon has relied on a convoluted subcontracting system that denies last-mile drivers the protections other workers get, while maintaining extraordinary control over their schedules, workloads, and uniforms,” said Julie Su, New York City’s deputy mayor for economic justice, in a statement.


Treating DSP delivery drivers as Amazon’s direct employees would make the company responsible for wage and safety protections and other legal liabilities. A similar bill is under consideration in Chicago.


LEGISLATIVE BATTLEGROUND


Tiffany Cabán, a DSA member and a city councilor representing Queens, sponsored the Delivery Protection Act. It has

majority

 support in the 51-member chamber.


Mayor Zohran Mamdani and other elected officials have thrown their support behind the legislation, saying it would help boost wages, improve working conditions, and raise standards and safety across the logistics sector.


But

multimillionaire

 Council Speaker Julie Menin isn’t on board. And Jessica Schumer, the daughter of Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, is

 leading

the lobbying fight to defeat the bill.


Amazon and other subcontractors are fighting tooth and nail. Amazon has threatened that if the bill passes, it will pull out of New York, forcing customers to pick up orders at hubs in New Jersey.


New Yorkers have been exposed to voluminous mailers and videos claiming that delivery will get slower and more expensive. Amazon has spared no expense, shelling out more than

$5 million

on lobbying, television and social media ads to defeat the bill. By proposing to make DSP operators extinct, Amazon says, the bill is "threatening the small businesses that deliver to customers.”


The Teamsters represent 330,000 warehouse and package car drivers at UPS. Amazon deliveries constitute a parallel nonunion system that not only undermines wages and working conditions across the logistics industry, but also threatens the volume that union workers deliver.


Amazon workers with support from the Teamsters and other unions have been organizing for years, but as they have hit roadblocks, they have taken the war into municipal government.


Amazon’s army of union-busters and lawyers cost the company

 $26 million

 in 2026 alone to intimidate workers and file endless court appeals in a war of attrition. The company’s signature move is to abruptly sever ties with a DSP after workers organize—as it did with a DSP that voluntarily recognized a union of drivers and dispatchers who joined the Teamsters in 2023 in Palmdale, California.


So workers are trying a different angle to constrain the behemoth through legislative fights, educating voters on regulations to level the playing field.


NO MORE ROUTES, NO JOB


“I’d just say that the threat [to workers] is bigger without the bill, because Amazon is getting away with so much,” said Latrice Johnson, a former delivery driver who worked out of a Maspeth, Queens, warehouse called DBK4.


Last year she and 149 co-workers were

laid off

 with less than a day’s notice when Amazon suddenly shut down her DSP. She recalled hearing when she came in to work, “There's no more routes, so you no longer have a job.”


A month earlier, she had received a top award for her work performance. “It was a slap in the face,” she said. The job was a lifeline for her to provide for her daughter.


The Teamsters charge that Amazon violated labor law, retaliating against the DSP drivers for organizing. In all, by cancelling DSP contracts, Amazon has terminated the jobs of nearly

500 delivery

author: Lilli Akpaleeapik
title: Ottawa gives $77M to Arctic Bay for small craft harbour
content:
The federal government has announced $77-million in funding for a multi-use small craft harbour to be built in Arctic Bay.


The harbour will include a breakwater, launch ramp, fixed wharf for larger vessels, floating wharves for small craft vessels, dredging for the harbour basin and an entrance channel, according to a Fisheries and Oceans Canada press release issued on Oct. 2.


“This harbour will create opportunities for hunters, fishers and families to be more independent. Food sovereignty and economic prosperity will follow,” said Nunavut MP Lori Idlout in the release.


Construction began in August and will continue until 2029. It’s expected to be operational for the following open water season.


Pilitak Enterprises Ltd., an Inuit-owned construction company based in Iqaluit, is the contractor.


The contract created between the company and the hamlet includes an Inuit benefits plan to support local training and employment.


According to the release, the federal government is continuing to work with northern communities to help with development and create more resources for residents of the north such as this new harbour.

content:
Notice on forthcoming ACG meeting

The Organisational Platform of the Libertarian Communists, popularly known as The Platform, was published by exiled Russian and Ukrainian anarchist communists in 1926. This short, draft, pamphlet shook the anarchist world and divided opinion with its call for a General Union of Anarchists, tactical and theoretical unity and collective responsibility. It has continued to inspire many anarchist communists across the globe. The meeting will discuss the (in)famous Platform and consider what it offers us 100 years after its publication. title: “Health insurance always denies this claim the first time but if you have the knowledge, time and…
content:
dragon-in-a-fez

:

politijohn

:

Source

honestly I think there’s an even bigger story: a 90% error rate is not the result of a technological flaw. yes, AI makes mistakes, but getting a 90% error rate on an essentially binary decision (accept claim/deny claim) out of a probabilistic system, even a poorly built one, is so monumentally unlikely there’s no justification for believing it.

I see two realistic possibilities here: either it was

explicitly directed

 to reject as many claims as possible, and told it could break rules to do so, or its training data somehow ended up massively skewed toward claims that were denied despite being valid.


“Health insurance always denies this claim the first time but if you have the knowledge, time and energy to appeal, you win most of the time”

 was a well-known thing in many patient groups long before AI came into the picture. They’ve automated it now but this has been how they work for much longer.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Three Years into Genocide, "The IDF Is Still Hunting Gazans": Palestinian Journalist Akram al-Satarri
content:
In Gaza, October 7, 2023, is viewed as the beginning of the genocide. Over the past three years, Israel killed over 74,000 people, according to the Gaza Health Ministry, but many believe that number is a vast undercount. The killing continues despite a so-called ceasefire that took effect about a year ago.


“Every single aspect of the life of the people of Gaza has changed once and forever,” since October 7, says Akram al-Satarri, a Gaza-based journalist. He points out that a large majority of structures in the Gaza Strip have been reduced to rubble and that Israel controls around 70% of Gaza. “The Israeli Air Force is still hovering all around different parts of the Gaza Strip, and the

IDF

 is still hunting Gazans, disturbing the already disturbed life, spreading death and displacement once and once again.”

title: “Για την ακύρωση της προβολής του ντοκιμαντέρ NAZA στο πλαίσο του Φεστιβάλ Κινηματογράφου Θεσσαλονίκης” – Καταγγελία του Συντονισμού Αλληλεγγύης στην Παλαιστίνη
content:
Καταγγελία του Συντονισμού Αλληλεγγύης στην Παλαιστίνη προς το Διεθνές

Φεστιβάλ Κινηματογράφου Θεσσαλονίκης, λόγω της απόφασης να αναβληθούν όλες οι

 προβολές του ντοκιμαντέρ “NAZA”, των Γιουβάλ Άμπραχαμ και Ρέιτσελ Σορ. Το φεστιβάλ ανακοίνωσε πως το προαναφερθέν ντοκιμαντέρ για τη γενοκτονία στη Γάζα δε θα προβληθεί στα πλαίσια του φεστιβάλ “κατόπιν αιτήματος των σκηνοθετών και σε ένδειξη σεβασμού προς τα θύματα της τρομοκρατικής επίθεσης της Χαμάς το 2023”.   Ο Συντονισμός αλληλεγγύης στην Παλαιστίνη καταγγέλει την απόφαση αυτή, αποκαλώντας ότι είναι μία προβοκατόρικη και φασιστικού τύπου απαγόρευση με σκοπό να επισκιάσει τα κινήματα αλληλεγγύης στη Παλαιστίνη. Παρακάτω η καταγγελία του Συντονισμού.


ΣΥΝΤΟΝΙΣΜΟΣ ΑΛΛΗΛΕΓΓΥΗΣ στην ΠΑΛΑΙΣΤΙΝΗ /Θεσσαλονίκη –

Συμμετέχει η ΠΑΛΑΙΣΤΙΝΙΑΚΗ ΚΟΙΝΟΤΗΤΑ ΘΕΣΣΑΛΟΝΙΚΗΣ


ΚΑΤΑΓΓΕΛΙΑ


ΓΙΑ ΤΗΝ ΑΚΥΡΩΣΗ ΤΗΣ ΠΡΟΒΟΛΗΣ ΤΟΥ ΝΤΟΚΙΜΑΝΤΕΡ «ΝΑΖΑ» ΣΤΟ ΠΛΑΙΣΙΟ ΤΟΥ ΦΕΣΤΙΒΑΛ ΚΙΝΗΜΑΤΟΓΡΑΦΟΥ ΘΕΣΣΑΛΟΝΙΚΗΣ


στο φόντο των

φασιστικού τύπου απαγορεύσεων

 που προωθούν οι σιωνιστές φονιάδες, οι ΗΠΑ και η Ε.Ε. γύρω από τις

7 Οκτώβρη

 με την πλήρη συνεργασία της ελληνικής κυβέρνησης


Καταγγέλλουμε την αιφνιδιαστική ακύρωση των προγραμματισμένων προβολών του ντοκιμαντέρ «NAZA» των Γιουβάλ Άμπραχαμ και Ρέιτσελ Σορ την Τετάρτη 7 Οκτωβρίου 2026 στο πλαίσιο του Φεστιβάλ Κινηματογράφου Θεσσαλονίκης. Αυτή η ενέργεια εντάσσεται στο πλαίσιο των ακυρώσεων της προβολής πανευρωπαϊκά (βλ. Ολλανδία) και της προσπάθειας της ΕΕ να σβηστούν από το χάρτη οι διαδηλώσεις αλληλεγγύης στον Παλαιστινιακό λαό στις 7 Οκτώβρη, όπως απαιτούν οι σιωνιστές δολοφόνοι του Ισραήλ και το μεγάλο αφεντικό τους οι ΗΠΑ. Σε αυτό το πλαίσιο έρχεται και η φασιστικού τύπου απαγόρευση των διαδηλώσεων στην Αθήνα με ειδικότερη αφορμή την επίσκεψη του Αμερικανού Υπουργού Εξωτερικών των ΗΠΑ Μάρκο Ρούμπιο στις 6-8 Οκτώβρη. Και αυτό, γιατί το φρικτό, γενοκτόνο καθεστώς απαρτχάιντ και εποικισμού, στηρίζουν με όλα τα μέσα – στρατιωτικά, πολιτικά, οικονομικά- οι ΗΠΑ και η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση, μαζί και η ελληνική κυβέρνηση που έχει μετατρέψει τη χώρα σε μια απέραντη ΝΑΤΟϊκή βάση κάτω από τη μπότα και της «ασπίδας του Αχιλλέα». Ένα καθεστώς που μόνο τα τελευταία τρία χρόνια έχει δολοφονήσει πάνω από 75.000 Παλαιστινίους και τραυματίσει πάνω από 175.000 σε Λωρίδα της Γάζας και Δυτική Όχθη συνολικά. Ποιους ενόχλησε μια ταινία που αναδεικνύει τα στυγνά εγκλήματα του Ισραηλινού στρατού κατοχής σε βάρος του Παλαιστινιακού λαού και φανερώνει πρώην μέλη του IDF να παραδέχονται δημόσια τη γενοκτονία; Ο ίδιος ο Νετανιάχου παρομοίασε τον αντίκτυπο του ντοκιμαντέρ ΝΑΖΑ στο εξωτερικό με «επίθεση με βαλλιστικούς πυραύλους» εναντίον του κράτους του Ισραήλ, ενώ ο υπουργός Πολιτισμού Μίκι Ζοχάρ απείλησε να αφαιρέσει την ισραηλινή ιθαγένεια από τους δύο σκηνοθέτες. Η επίσημη ανακοίνωση του φεστιβάλ που αναφέρει ότι η ακύρωση της προβολής έγινε «κατόπιν αιτήματος των σκηνοθετών» και «σε ένδειξη σεβασμού προς τα θύματα της τρομοκρατικής επίθεσης της Χαμάς το 2023», είτε προέκυψε με την ελεύθερη βούληση των σκηνοθετών, είτε μέσα από ωμό εκβιασμό, μικρή σημασία έχει πλέον σε αυτό το φόντο.


Οι λαοί όλου του κόσμου, ο δικός μας λαός, είναι με την πλευρά του δίκαιου αγώνα του λαού της Παλαιστίνης και της Παλαιστινιακής Αντίστασης για ΛΕΥΤΕΡΗ και ΑΝΕΞΑΡΤΗΤΗ πατρίδα! Το διεθνές κίνημα αλληλεγγύης είναι που έχει οδηγήσει σε πρωτοφανή ποσοστά αρνητικής στάσης απέναντι στο Ισραήλ παγκόσμια αλλά και σ’ αυτά που συνέβησαν στον ΟΗΕ. Και όση λάσπη και αν ρίξουν τα παπαγαλάκια του συστήματος, όσα μέτρα καταστολής και να πάρουν, ο λαοί, ο δικός μας λαός θα είναι με το δίκιο.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Israeli Activist Maoz Inon Lost His Parents on Oct. 7, Decries Israel's Ethnic Cleansing in Gaza
content:
Israelis and Palestinians are marking three years since October 7, 2023, when Hamas launched a surprise attack on Israel. Nearly 1,200 Israelis were killed, and around 250 were taken hostage. It was the deadliest such attack in Israel’s history, after which Israel immediately began bombing the Gaza Strip, killing at least 5,000 people by October 23, 2023. At least 74,000 Palestinians have been killed.


Israeli peace activist Maoz Inon lost both of his parents, who lived on a kibbutz just north of the Gaza border, in the Hamas attack. In the aftermath, Inon called for peace and reconciliation rather than revenge. He has spent much of the past three years working closely with Palestinian peace activist Aziz Abu Sarah.


“The Israeli government exploited the trauma, the pain, the fear of the Israelis after the October 7th massacre to change the status quo from conflict management to ethnic cleansing,” says Inon. “Those who choose ethnic cleansing, those who choose bloodshed, those who choose destruction must be sanctioned,” he adds.

author: Giovanna Vial
title: Did a Banking Scandal Put Brazil’s Bolsonaros Back in First Place?
content:
On Sunday night, Lula supporters waited nervously amid a sea of red in Laranjeiras, one of Rio de Janeiro’s most leftwing neighbourhoods. As election results rolled in, worried expressions spread across the main square, Praça São Salvador, and the chatter at tables grew lower and more urgent. 


It was not just that there would be a second round; Brazilians had been expecting that for months. It was that senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of imprisoned far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro, would now head into it as the frontrunner, around

2.22 million votes ahead

of the leftwing incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. 


While the result wasn’t unimaginable, most polls did not expect Flávio to come out on top. Neither did common sense: the far-right candidate has spent much of the last year

embroiled in the largest banking scandal in the country’s history,

 with his popularity tanking at times as a result. 


In May, one poll had Flávio falling from three to

nine points behind Lula

, immediately after it emerged that

he had sought $24m (£18m)

 from the former owner of a collapsed bank to fund a

hero biopic about his father

. (Entitled

Dark Horse,

the film, which came out in June, stars US actor Jim Caviezel.)


But as the Banco Master scandal took unexpected turns – and the right found new people to blame – the far-right candidate gradually closed the gap, eventually

inching ahead of Lula

 in some September surveys.


Now, after Sunday’s surprise result, many Brazilians are left wondering: did a scandal that should have sunk

Flávio and his party

 actually help put him in first place?


‘In this country, we choose the least bad.’


Until 2024, the mid-sized lender Banco Master grew at breakneck speed by selling high-yield debt through investment platforms. According to federal police investigators, much of that growth rested on the relationships its owner, businessman Daniel Vorcaro, cultivated with the upper echelons of Brazilian politics: federal deputies, senators, former governors and supreme court justices. 


Investigators allege Vorcaro – who has been

in pre-trial detention since March, and denies all wrongdoing

 – offered

favours, ranging from luxury trips abroad

 and lavish dinners to parties with sex workers, in exchange for information and political cover for the bank’s interests. 


In May, the Intercept Brasil published messages and audio that revealed a close personal relationship between Flávio and Vorcaro, with the presidential candidate calling the banker

“brother” in some of the many correspondences

 they exchanged. 


Flávio’s party colleague, meanwhile, was

resigned as the Rio de Janeiro governor

 in March after police opened an investigation into the state’s enormous investment into Banco Master under his leadership. In the time that Cláudio Castro was in office,

Rio’s public-sector pension fund put roughly R$1.6bn (£232m) of civil servants’ retirement savings

 into the bank.


The scandal, which has been headline news in Brazil for months now, has had an enormous impact on the election, with

7% of voters telling pollster Quaest

 that it might change their ballot. Given Brazil’s electorate is over 150 million, that’s roughly 10 million people – four times the margin that now separates the two candidates. 


But precisely how the scandal has affected votes hasn’t been straightforward or consistent over time.


Outside a polling station in Barra da Tijuca, an affluent district in Rio’s west zone, 48-year-old doctor Luciana Frávola said she would still vote for Flávio. “In this country, we choose the least bad,” she told Novara Media. “The PT’s [Lula’s Workers’ Party’s] involvement with Master was bigger than the PL’s [Flávio’s Liberal Party].” 


The evidence doesn’t support Frávola’s claim; Lula’s party has not been connected to the scandal in the way Flávio’s has. But in September a new story broke that implicated a different enemy of the Bolsonaros. For many Flávio voters, this has become the scandal’s most salient chapter.


In 2025, Brazil’s supreme court sentenced Jair Bolsonaro to 27 years in prison for plotting to overturn his 2022 election defeat. The case was overseen by Justice Alexandre de Moraes, long regarded by the Bolsonarist right as the embodiment of judicial overreach. A federal police report unsealed in September

put Moraes under suspicion

 by suggesting Vorcaro may have sought the protection of Brazil’s most powerful judge as investigators closed …

author: Unknown
title: Doza kuştina rojnameger Hakan Tosun: Cezayê muebetê li bersûcan hat birîn
content:
Danişîna li 17emîn Dadgeha Cezayê Giran a Bakirkoyê pêk hat. Malbata Tosun û parêzerên wan Hakan Bozyurt û Cemal Yucel beşdarî danişînê bûn.


Bersûc Abdurrahman Murat û Adnan Şahin ji girtîgehên ku lê girtî ne bi riya Sîstema Deng û Dîmenî (SEGBÎS) tevlî danişînê bûn.


Doza kuştina rojnameger Hakan Tosun: Ji bo du bersûcan cezayê muebetê tê xwestin


24 Adar 2026


Rojnameger û welatiyên ku dixwestin danişînê bişopînin negirtin salonê. Gelek kesan li ber deriyê adliyeyê danişîn şopandin.


“Kese sêyemîn çima li derve ye?”


Parêzerê Hakan Tosun Cemal Yucel di danîşînê de axivî û got: “Em daxwazên xwe dubare dikin. Em daxwaz dikin ku bi sûcê kuştina bi zanebûn werin cezakirin.”


Yek ji parêzerên malbata Tosun Hakan Bozyurt jî bal kişand ser ku di bûyerê de çalakiyeke organîzekirî heye û diyar kir ku kesê sêyemîn ê bi motosîkletê Yusuf Ozakdag jî divê wekî bersûk bê darizandin.


Di danîşîna ku îro saet di 10.30an de dest pê kir de dayika Hakan Tosun Fatma Tosun pirsî: “Kesê sêyemîn çima li derve ye?”


Êrîşî rojnameger Hakan Tosun kirin: Du kes hatin girtin


13 Cotmeh 2025


“Hakan bi ti awayî ranabe ser piyan”


Parêzerê Tosun, Hakan Bozyurt jî amaje bi dîmenên ku di hemû danişînan de pêşkêşî heyeta dadgehê kirine, kir û got:


“Tişta bingehîn ew e ku ji destpêka danîşînê ve me dîmenên li ser çêbûna bûyera kuştinê ya li Esenyurtê bi awayekî zelal nîşan dan. Hakan li cihekî rûniştiye û li cihê xwe ranabe û bertek nîşan nade. Min gelek caran temaşe kir. Hakan bi ti awayî ranabe ser piyan, tew destê xwe jî ranake. Tê dîtin ku bersûc bi awayekî tund bi pehînan li serê Hakan dixe. Her wiha tê dîtin ku bi porê wî digirin û lê didin.”


Bozyurt diyar kir ku şahid dibêjin “li Hakan nedane” lêbelê dîmenên kamerayan wisa nabejê. Gotinên şahidan rastiyê nîşan nadin.


“Gotinên şahidan û dîmenên kamerayan berovajî hev in”


Parêzer Bozyurt amaje bi Yusuf Ozakdag kir ku di kamerayan de bi motosîkleta xwe tê dîtin û weha got:


“Adnan Şahin ji erebeya xwe dertê û li Hakan dixe. Şahin û Murat bi erebeyê diçin. Di wê demê de Yusuf Ozakdag li ser motora xwe Hakan temaşe dike. Dîmenên kamerayan nîşan didin ku ew temaşe dike. Wesaîtê radiwestîne. Şahin jî piştre tê û lê dixe. Me di parastina xwe de ev tişt gelek caran nîşan dan. Me got ku ti pêwendiya dîmenên metrobusê bi bûyerê re nîne. Dozger jî got ku ti pêwendiya wê bûyerê û vê bûyerê bi hev re nîne. Di dîmenan de jî nîne. Em dizanin ku ev pêvajo çawa meşiya ye. Em ji daxuyaniya emniyetê hîn bû ku di vê dosyayê de ji xeynî reşkirina delîlan lêpirsîneke din hatî meşandin. Dîmenên kamerayan hatine girtin. Ji bo îro heke ev tomar hebûna me yê rastî bêtir bi cih bianiya. Em dibînin ku beyanên şahidan û dîmenên kamerayan berovajî hev in. Tevî vê yekê jî beyanên li dijî rastiyê hene. gotinên di rapora tipa edlî de li gorî lêdana Hakan û mirina wî diguncin. Hakan bi ti awayî bertek nîşan nedaye.”


Bersûcan xwestin werin tehliye kirin


Abdurrahman Murat û Adnan Şahin îfadeyên xwe yên berê dubare kirin û daxwaza tehliyeyê kirin. Parêzerên bersûcan jî daxwaza beratkirina wan kirin.


Heyeta dadgehê biryara xwe aşkere kir û bi tohmeta ku “bi zanebûn kuştine” cezayê muebetê li Abdurrahman Murat û Adnan Şahin birî.


Çi bûbû?


Hakan Tosun, êvara 10ê Cotmeha 2025an li Esenyurtê ji bo biçe mala xwe bi rê ket. Çend xulek beriya bigihîje malê, du caran rastî êrişê hat. Tosun li qiraxa rê bi awayekî li ser hişê xwe çûye hat dîtin û piştre birin nexweşxaneyê.


Lê belê ji ber ku nasnameya wî li ser nebû, qeyda wî ya nexweşxaneyê nehat kirin. Ji ber vê sedemê jî piştî 27 saetan agahî dan malbata wî.


Her weha li nexweşxaneyê xwîn rijiya ser mêjiyê wî û ew birin beşa nexweşiyên giran. Tosun sê rojan li ber xwe da, lê roja Duşema 13ê Cotmehê jiyana xwe ji dest da.


Polîsan di çarçoveya lêpirsînê de du gumanbarên 18 û 24 salî desteser kirin. Piştre ev her du kes bi sûcê “birîndarkirina bi qestî” hatin girtin.


Rojnameger Umut Taştan ê ku çûbû cihê bûyerê û bi niştecihên taxê û esnafan re axivîbû, ji liyê xizmên faîlan ve hatibû tehdîtkirin.


(CA/AY)

author: Fozzie
title: Why we should not take sides in war - Devrim Valerian
content:
From Dope Magazine #35, Autumn 2026.

The Prime Minister wears a T-shirt now. It costs 80 quid, and his jeans cost £295. The very nice Harrington jacket he’s often seen in costs £695. Looking like an ordinary bloke is expensive these days.

He’s apologised over Gaza too. He said that Labour “didn’t get it right” and “needs to do better”. It sounded like the British government was finally going to take a position on genocide. Even the climb down sounded a bit more radical than the days of Keir Starmer; “There’s increasing evidence that war crimes appear to have been committed.” But then he told us that it's not a matter for him to decide upon. Instead, it “must be for the international courts to determine, rather than politicians.”

Words matter. If the UK government declared that war crimes were being committed in Gaza, let alone a genocide, it would trigger a legal obligation to stop arms sales. The new policy then is to smile, apologise, and go on selling Israel the weapons, including components for F-35 aircraft, that it needs to continue its mass slaughter of an unarmed civilian population. Little appears to have changed at all. The sales of arms continue, and those who object to this are still arrested and charged under terrorism laws. It should come as little surprise from someone who has been a member of Labour Friends of Israel since 2015.

He also appeared alongside Volodymyr Zelensky at his first meeting with a foreign leader and assured him that the UK was 100% with Ukraine for as long as it takes. On the surface, the situation in Ukraine has similarities with that in Palestine. Russia invaded Ukraine and is committing atrocities there, just as Israel is in Palestine. The first difference is in the British response. Britain is 100% with Ukraine. In Palestine, it is selling Israel arms with which to commit genocide. That would be the equivalent of selling Russia bombs to commit massacres in Ukraine.

There must, then, be some difference between the two situations. It’s certainly not one of morality. The horrors inflicted by the Israeli army upon the civilian population have been far worse than those committed by Russia in terms of people killed. Why then is the UK 100% behind Ukraine, yet arresting people on the streets for saying that they oppose genocide in Palestine?

The answer lies not in the field of morality, but in that of geopolitics. Britain sees it as in its interests to support Israel. It also sees it as in its interests to support Ukraine. The dead have no voice in this. Nor is there anyone speaking up for any moral imperative. It’s national interests that speak loudest.

We should look at the causes of the war in Ukraine. This war is not the act of some ‘irrational actor’. Putin did not start this war because he is ‘crazy’. This war is part of a long struggle played out between America and Russia since 1945. It seemed that after 1989, Russia had been historically defeated in this struggle. Certainly, it suffered a huge defeat. The Warsaw Pact and even the Soviet Union itself were broken up. NATO and the EU expanded rapidly to incorporate many of the newly ‘independent’ states. Now, with America’s role as the single world power diminishing, Russia has seen its chance to reassert its power over Ukraine. It’s not some act of a single ‘madman’. It’s an expression of the interests of Russian capitalism. This is how imperialism works.

So in the midst of this struggle between two imperialist giants, Ukrainian workers are being asked to defend ‘their’ country, and in Britain everybody is being asked to back them. The great powers, as ever, are not clashing directly. This struggle is being carried out by a series of small wars, either between proxies or involving one of the major powers directly intervening in a country. We’ve seen all this before, in Korea, Vietnam, Afghanistan, and a host of proxy wars across the ‘third world’.

Workers in Ukraine are being rallied to this slaughter with all sorts of propaganda. Many of the slogans sound ‘left’. Both sides rally behind slogans of ‘anti-imperialism’. However, this is just a cynical ploy to rally the populace to die on behalf of one imperialism against the other. ‘Anti-fascism’ has become the rallying call of the warmongers on both sides. The West accuses Putin of being ‘worse than Hitler’, and the Russians accuse the Ukrainians of being Nazis.

Then we have patriotism. In times of war, nation-states always rely on patriotism. Russia is using it …

author: Mada Masr
title: Officials approve island residents’ demand to remain, Staying on Warraq movement says
content:
State officials have agreed to provide Warraq Island’s residents with alternative housing under a “house-for-a-house” scheme, which was one of the residents’ main demands, to allow them to remain on the land as the state advances its development plan, the Staying on Warraq

movement


announced

 on Tuesday. 


The plan is yet to be announced by any agency representing the government, however.


The movement formed in August has led negotiations with state authorities following the latest round of

clashes

 between residents and security forces. A security deployment is regularly stationed at the Nile island’s ferry and transit points to secure supply lines and construction at the state-led redevelopment project, which has for years threatened to force residents from their homes and restricted their access to goods and essential services.


The new agreement was established in a Saturday meeting between several of the island’s representatives, both members and non-members of the movement, and state officials.


Officials told the movement that residents’ demand for a “house-for-a-house” guarantee had been approved and was now a reality, with an official decision expected to be issued and announced “within a short period,” according to the movement’s statement.


The agreement was to see the Housing Ministry issue an official decision allocating a plot of land on the island for the construction of replacement homes, along with development befitting the island’s overall appearance and with full utilities, according to the movement.


Mada Masr contacted a Housing Ministry official, who neither confirmed nor denied the report, stressing only that any official position would be announced through ministry statements.


A resident who attended the meeting, who spoke to Mada Masr on condition of anonymity, said that the awaited decision represents a victory for those who have insisted on their right to remain on the island.


During the meeting, residents also called for all lawsuits related to clashes with security forces to be dropped. The officials present said they would work toward this, according to the statement.


Officials overseeing the island’s redevelopment also confirmed that the housing units currently under construction are intended for residents who wish to receive them. They will be made available to them once they are handed over by construction companies, which have pledged to complete the handover by October 15 at the latest.


The service-related demands that officials also pledged to address included reopening the post office and installing an ATM to allow residents to withdraw pensions and salaries, as well as improving access to healthcare by providing a doctor at the local clinic and continuing the weekly medical caravans. Residents also called for the removal of construction waste and the provision of two free sewage pumping trucks to service the island’s inner streets. 


Several basic services on the island have been suspended in recent years, including the post office and the health unit. People have called for the return of sewage pumping trucks as their septic tanks fill up — a problem that has resurfaced in recent weeks, as trucks sent to the island have been unable to enter its narrow lanes, according to residents.


The latest meeting came after residents resumed escalating protests over the past two months, including sit-ins, marches and demonstrations since August, over restrictions on bringing construction materials into the island, tighter security measures and deteriorating living conditions following the suspension of public services.


After the August sit-in, officials told residents that the New Warraq Island Development Authority would permit the delivery of any construction materials or supplies to the island for residents to undertake their own maintenance projects. 


The New Warraq Development Authority later

denied

 that it had permitted the delivery of construction materials to the island.

author: asn
title: Debate on the Australian United Workers Union  Election & Industrial Strategy
content:
Article from Rebel Worker Paper of Anarcho-Syndicalist Network www.rebelworker.org Vol. 44 No.2 (243) Sept. - Oct. 2026

Debate on Australian United Workers Union Election & Industrial Strategy

The United Workers Union leadership election (and why it didn't really matter)

11/9/26 Back in June, the United Workers Union (UWU) wrapped up a hotly contested election for its National Convention. The UWU is one of the biggest unions in the country, with 150,000 members in dozens of industries, including warehousing, hospitality, aged care, and early childhood education.

Two tickets pitched themselves to members. 'United for You', led by union president Jo Schofield, ended up winning with a slim majority. But they faced a serious challenge from a group calling itself 'Members First'.

Members First had a slick campaign and some of what they had to say sounded pretty good: Less focus on the Labor Party, no back room deals without delegates present, and more money for strike funds and organisers.

But despite its name, and what some on the Left claimed during the campaign, Members First was no rank-and-file movement. The ticket was the project of UWU's national secretary, Tim Kennedy, and was run with very little member involvement.

The election, then, was a factional battle between sections of the officialdom, and the parts of the Labor Party they align themselves with.

Two sides, same coin The UWU was founded as a merger between the National Union of Workers (NUW) and United Voice (UV) in 2019. The forces behind the two election tickets can be traced back to the separate unions.

United for You represented the UV wing. The ticket's campaign carried on their faction's tradition of prioritising political lobbying over industrial organising. Under their model, unionism is a kind of 'service' that members sign up for: legal advice and other perks are provided by the staff of the union in exchange for dues.

The NUW, on the other hand, placed more emphasis on traditional industrial organising, in industries like warehousing, logistics and food manufacturing. The leadership of the Members First campaign came from the NUW faction, and their election promises - more organisers, support for delegates, the occasional serious strike - reflect their own priorities.

The NUW approach, and the promises of Members First, might look pretty good at first glance. But the two strategies aren't as far apart as they seem.

The empowerment of members promised by Members First was incredibly limited, and largely focussed on 'transparency'. Even the promised strike funds were a fraction of the union's actual resources. Members weren't engaged in democratic structures as part of the campaign, and very few attended election events.

Members First wasn't an example of organisation from below-it was an advertising campaign, controlled from above.

Power to the rank-and-file? Despite the hundreds of thousands spent on campaigning by both sides, only 31% of members actually voted. Neither ticket mobilised members in a genuinely democratic or militant way, because, ultimately, both want to maintain the power of the officials and their links with the Labor Party.

Throwing money at an election isn't how you build the confidence, militancy, or participation of members. On paper, Members First may have been a marginally more militant ticket. But had they somehow managed to win, they would still be in the exact same position as their United For You opponents.

Without a real, well-organised rank-and-file movement, with power based in workplaces, the officials are left balancing between members, the bosses, and their mates in the ALP. With all the power on the bosses side, and pressure from the government to keep members in line, they have every reason to settle for bad deals.

The only people that can really put members first are the members themselves. To win democratic control over our union, we have to get organised at the level of the rank-and-file.

The UWU election was a fight for control of the National Convention, a body of 500 which then elects the day-to-day managers of the union. Rather than elect Convention delegates by industry or workplace, members are grouped together by the electorate they live in.

This system was designed to entrench the power of the Executive and prevent an alternative base of power forming among specific groups of workers on the shop floor.

Still, there are industry specific structures for parts of UWU's coverage …

author: Fozzie
title: Chapter 20: Time-Wages
content:
Harry Cleaver's study guide to chapter 20 of Marx's Capital volume one.

The Wage = "price of labor", in this chapter usually payment per hour

Nominal wages = money exchange value of labor power Real wages = the sum of the means of subistence purchased by wages

Average "price" of labor = average daily value of labor power divided by the average number of hours worked, e.g., (daily wage of 3 shillings)/12 hours = hourly price, or wage, = 3s/12 = 36d/12 = 3d = hourly wage of 3 pence. (In pre-metric English measure, 1 shilling = 12 pence, today 1s = 10d).

So, if the daily wage is fixed, e.g., 3s, then if the capitalists impose longer hours, the effective hourly wage drops:

Conversely, if the hourly wage is fixed, then a change in the number of working hours will change the workers income.

The importance of this: whether or not workers earn enough to survive, i.e., to reproduce their labor power, will depend on whether they have enough hours of work.

The implication of these two sets of observations is that unless capitalists are constrained by law, e.g., Factory Acts in Marx's time, they may manipulate hours and wages for their own benefit, to the detriment of the workers.

"Hence," Marx writes, "the perfectly rational revolt of the London building workers in 1860 against the attempt of the capitalists to impose on them this sort of wage by the hour." And hence too, the fight for the Factory acts to put a limit on such manipulations.

1) Overtime should be paid at a higher rate, because the "deterioration" of labor power accelerates during extra, exhausting hours, and therefore, the value of labor power (the cost of repairing and reproducing that labor power rises). Sometimes the capitalists recognize this and pay a bit more, although Marx suggests that the bit more they pay is not proportional to the cost of repairing the extra wear and tear on the worker.

2. If, using methods such as those described above, the capitalist succeed in lowering wages at current hours, then workers will need and either be willing to accept or even fight for longer hours.

3. The same effect is sometimes achieved by increasing the intensity of work. Higher intensity means more labor being supplied, an increased supply of labor will tend to lower wages, lower wages will lead to more overtime.

4. These kind of dynamics are circulated through "competition" wherein the success of one capitalist in this area will lead other capitalists to seek the same success as the success of the first allows the undercutting of the others through the reduction in the prices of their wares.

First, Marx is here talking about the peculiarities of one form of a form. Wages are the form of the value of labor power; time wages are the form of that form. The peculiarities that interest him at this point concern the various ways in which this particular form of wages can be and often is manipulated by capital in its efforts to impose more work. The same will be true in his next chapter on piece-wages. The same would be true if he had analyzed other forms. The same should be true if we do what he didn't do and extend his analysis to those other forms. We might note, for example, how salaries - which are paid at a fixed rate, usually so-and-so-much per year (and thus per month) leave open the amount of actual labor time required. We might also note how this means that jobs that pay salaries generally designate the tasks to be performed and that those tasks often require far more than the standard number of hours per week, e.g., 40 hrs in the US after WWII. Thus the commonplace that salaried workers wind up spending many extra hours in their offices and also take home briefcases full of work to be done in their supposed "free time." In the next chapter we will see how the analysis of piece wages throws further light on what turns out, in this case, to be a hybrid form of the wage.

The same should still be true if we turned from his focus on the explicit wage to other forms of working class income that support the reproduction of labor power, e.g., unemployment compensation, welfare payments, grades, public health services. For example, in the case of unemployment compensation, that is generally presented to the public as a kind of welfare for the temporarily unemployed, we would note how it is structured to require the work of looking for work, of making the labor market function by forcing those who want to receive compensation to actively seek out employers …

author: Fozzie
title: Chapter 19: The Transformation of the Value of Labour-Power into Wages
content:
Harry Cleaver's study guide to Marx's Capital volume 1, chapters 19.

Chapter 19: The Transformation of the Value of Labour-Power

The value of "labor" cannot be measured by labor. For "Labor is the substance, and the immanent measure of value, but it has no value itself."

The Physiocrats and the Classical economists saw that behind the market price of "labor" lay its costs of production, but conceived of its production in terms of the production of the worker.

But what is produced and what the worker sells is not "labor" but "labor power."

The worker sells labor power in exchange for a wage, but:.

--the wage-form hides the distinction between necessary labor (to reproduce labor power) and surplus labor (appropriated by the capitalist).

In corvée labor distinction between labor for self and labor for the lord is clear.

But in slave and wage labor the "form of appearance" hides the "essence":

--In slave labor all labor seems to be for the owner, hides labor for self. --In wage labor all labor seems to be for the worker, hides surplus labor for capitalist.

The wage is thus one form of appearance of the essential value of labor power that lies behind it, but the discovery of this "essence" required clear "scientific" thought of which the bourgeois economists did not prove capable.

This chapter, along with the other chapters on the wage (20-22), is the only one in volume one of Capital in which Marx examines the monetary form of the variables he has developed for his analysis. Throughout the rest of the book his analysis is couched in value terms. Later, in volume III he will take up the various money forms of surplus value, i.e., profit, interest and rent, but this is the only place in this volume where he examines the implications of the particular money forms that his value categories allow us to understand in socio-political ways.

The basic thrust of this first chapter in this section on wages is to argue that the money wage is a "form of appearance" of the value of labor power. The money wage is only one possible form, there are others. For instance, with payment in kind harvest workers are paid by a share of the harvest, or shoemakers employed by early capitalists were paid in part through tolerance of the appropriation of scraps of the leather they were given to work. Salaries are yet another form of payment for the value of labor power. The analysis presented in these chapters provide a more general methodology for analyzing other kinds of form, and therefore has an interest that goes beyond the immediate subject. In the case of wages the analysis he presented in chapter six on the buying and selling of labor power (and also on its use-value) is also true here and you should probably reread that discussion as a prelude to studying this chapter. What he adds here to what he has already said about the "essence" is an analysis of the implications of the "form."

Marx's emphasis in the first quote cited in the summary above, that "Labor is the substance, and the immanent measure of value, but it has no value itself.", is logical enough: if labor is the measure, or nummeraire, of value, then we can't speak of the value of that nummeraire in the same sense we do of what it measures. This is like mainstream economists saying that value of something is its money price and then being aware that they can't speak of the value of money, except in terms of its "value" as nummeraire or in terms of its functional roles, e.g., means of circulation. However, just as Marx, with his theory of value, showed that we can indeed understand the "value" of money in terms of a different kind of value, "labor value", so too can we understand the "value" of labor in other terms. Little by little in Capital we come to see that the "value" of labor is not merely that it is the nummeraire for measuring the value of other things, but that it plays that role in capitalism because labor is itself the fundamental social relationship that capital imposes to create and maintain its social order. Labor is the fundamental measure of value in capitalism because labor is the fundamental means of social control and social order. The value of labor, in other words, is its value to capital in the creation and maintenance of its kind of society. Every hour a person works in this society, no matter what kind of work is being done, is an hour that person's time and energy, their very life is subordinated to capital. The more hours, the more …

author: infolibre
title: Καταγγελία των εργαζομένων στην επιχείρηση ΒΙΟΛΑΝΤΑ
content:
Εργαζόμενοι στην ΒΙΟΛΑΝΤΑ απέστειλαν κείμενο – καταγγελία στο ΠΡΙΝ για τις συνθήκες εργασίας που επικρατούν το τελευταίο διάστημα στην επιχείρηση που δολοφόνησε 5 εργαζόμενες στην έκρηξη του εργοστασίου τον Ιανουάριο του 2026. Η καταγγελία κάνει αναφορές για πιεστικό κλίμα, συνθήκες εκφοβισμού, ψυχολογικής πίεσης και bullying απο την εργοδοσία της ΒΙΟΛΑΝΤΑ


Παρακάτω αναδημοσιεύουμε τη καταγγελία των εργαζομένων της ΒΙΟΛΑΝΤΑ που δέχθηκε η εφημερίδα ΠΡΙΝ:


 Καταγγελία των εργαζομένων στην επιχείρηση ΒΙΟΛΑΝΤΑ:


“Επικοινωνούμε εκ μέρους σημαντικού αριθμού εργαζομένων της ΒΙΟΛΑΝΤΑ, οι οποίοι αισθανόμαστε την ανάγκη να δημοσιοποιήσουμε μια κατάσταση που βιώνουμε καθημερινά και μας προκαλεί έντονη ανησυχία.


Σύμφωνα με τις αναφορές εργαζομένων, το τελευταίο διάστημα επικρατεί στον χώρο εργασίας ένα ιδιαίτερα πιεστικό κλίμα, με περιστατικά που οι ίδιοι βιώνουν ως ψυχολογική πίεση, εκφοβισμό και bullying.


Εργαζόμενοι αναφέρουν ότι τους ζητήθηκε να υπογράψουν έγγραφο σχετικά με τις αποδοχές και τις συνθήκες εργασίας, ενώ ορισμένοι υποστηρίζουν ότι αισθάνθηκαν πως πιέστηκαν να το υπογράψουν, καθώς τους μεταφέρθηκε ότι η άρνησή τους θα μπορούσε να έχει συνέπειες ακόμη και στην εργασιακή τους σχέση.


Παράλληλα, σύμφωνα με τις ίδιες αναφορές, εργαζόμενοι που έχουν προχωρήσει σε καταθέσεις ή έχουν εκφράσει παράπονα φέρεται να δέχονται λεκτικές πιέσεις και συμπεριφορές που τους δημιουργούν φόβο και ανασφάλεια.


Ιδιαίτερα σοβαρό είναι ότι ανάλογες συμπεριφορές bullying και ψυχολογικής πίεσης φέρεται να βιώνουν και οι επιζήσαντες, άνθρωποι που έχουν ήδη περάσει μια εξαιρετικά δύσκολη και τραυματική διαδικασία και θα έπρεπε να αισθάνονται ότι προστατεύονται και όχι ότι βρίσκονται αντιμέτωποι με νέες πιέσεις.


Ζητάμε να ακουστεί η φωνή μας και να διερευνηθούν με σοβαρότητα και ανεξαρτησία όλα όσα καταγγέλλονται.


Θέλουμε να μπορούμε να εργαζόμαστε με αξιοπρέπεια, χωρίς φόβο και χωρίς να αισθανόμαστε ότι η έκφραση μιας καταγγελίας ή η κατάθεση της αλήθειας μπορεί να έχει προσωπικές συνέπειες.


Απευθύνουμε έκκληση προς κάθε αρμόδιο φορέα, την Επιθεώρηση Εργασίας και κάθε ανεξάρτητη αρχή που μπορεί να εξετάσει την κατάσταση


Ακούστε μας. Ερευνήστε όσα καταγγέλλουμε. Προστατεύστε τους εργαζομένους και τους επιζήσαντες.”

title: Ikea macht auf Amazon – Kolleg*innen in Deutschland fürchten um Arbeitsplatz und Datenschutz und wollen den „Tarifvertrag Zukunft“
content:
Dossier


„Beschäftigte fordern Mitsprache und Zukunftssicherung“ ist das

Flugblatt von und bei ver.di Handel vom November 2020


 überschrieben: „…

Noch steht die Digitalisierung bei IKEA am Anfang. Und dennoch berichten bereits knapp 40 Prozent dass die neuen Techniken ihren Arbeitsplatz schon massiv verändert haben. Bei weiteren 37% ist das teilweise der Fall. Die Folgen: 20% der Betroffenen geben an, dass die Arbeitsbelastung zugenommen hat, 11% erleben deutlichen Zeitdruck, 10% berichten, dass sie weniger Austausch mit ihren Kolleg*innen haben, 6% geben an, die Arbeit sei eintöniger geworden. (…) Die Zukunft von IKEA muss auf einer nachhaltigen Digitalisierungsstrategie aufbauen, in der das Knowhow und die Expertise der Beschäftigten Gewicht haben. Beschäftigte, die tagtäglich den Laden am Laufen halten, müssen beteiligt werden! Gleichzeitig muss ihr unmittelbares Interesse an guter, gesunder und sicherer Arbeit respektiert und tarifvertraglich garantiert werden…

“ Siehe zur Situation und Umfrage von ver.di weitere Informationen:


IKEA wird umgebaut – Stück für Stück immer weiter weg vom „Tarifvertrag Zukunft“: „Ein neuer Zeitgeist mit Gruselfaktor!“ (ver.di Handel)


„

Was bei IKEA gerade passiert, ist alles andere als ein harmloser Spuk.

Die Bilanz der letzten 12 Monate:


– 15 betriebsbedingte Kündigungen im Einrichtungshaus Hamburg-Altona


– 63 vernichtete Arbeitsplätze in der IT in Dortmund


– 278 vernichtete Arbeitsplätze im Customer Support Center Rostock


– 127 betriebsbedingte Kündigungen


– + 32 Änderungskündigungen


– + 78 Versetzungen in der Service Organisation Wallau


Und das sind keine abstrakten Zahlen. Hinter jeder einzelnen stehen Kolleg*innen, ihre Familien, ihre Lebensplanung und oft viele Jahre Arbeit für IKEA.


Erkennst du dein IKEA noch wieder?


Ein IKEA, bei dem du dich auf deinen Arbeitsplatz verlassen kannst? Ein IKEA, in dem Erfahrung und langjährige Betriebszugehörigkeit etwas zählen? Ein IKEA, das nicht nur von seinen Werten spricht, sondern sie auch gegenüber den eigenen Beschäftigten lebt?


IKEA wird umgebaut – Stück für Stück.


Standorte und Bereiche werden verändert, Arbeitsplätze fallen weg, Kolleg*innen erhalten Änderungskündigungen oder werden versetzt. Und niemand kann sich darauf verlassen, dass der nächste Umbau nicht den eigenen Bereich betrifft. (…) Unser Ziel ist ein Tarifvertrag, der Beschäftigten beim weiteren Umbau von IKEA Schutz, Sicherheit und verbindliche Rechte gibt

…“

Nachricht vom 6.10.2026 von ver.di Handel


 und Aufruf an die Belegschaft


Neue ver.di-Kampagne für Tarifvertrag.Zukunft.IKEA: Gesundheit geht vor! Schluss mit den ständigen Überlastungen bei IKEA


„“

Wie wir das Arbeiten bei IKEA erleben, hat wenig mit dem Wohlfühlkurs aus den Werbespots des Unternehmens zu tun: Es gibt zu wenig Personal, aber immer mehr Aufgaben für die Kolleginnen und Kollegen, die oft allein auf  der Fläche sind. Führungskräfte unterstützen nicht. Mehr noch: Anzeichen von Überlastungen werden nicht ernst genommen. Und  die Personaleinsatzplanung geschieht nicht durch Menschen, sondern das macht Atoss – mit teils täglich veränderter  Arbeitszeit. Das alles ist stressig, gesundheitsgefährdend und verursacht hohe Krankenstände.


Du fragst dich, was wir gemeinsam tun können, damit es besser wird? Gemeinsam für einen Tarifvertrag streiten, der die Belastungen reduziert und folgendes regelt:

Gute, gesundheitsförderliche Arbeitsbedingungen und Führung; Schutz vor Arbeitsverdichtung; Qualitative, mitbestimmte Personalbedarfsplanung; Beteiligung der Beschäftigten an der Gestaltung technischer oder arbeitsorganisatorischer Neuerungen. Das schließt eine kontinuierliche Belastungsprüfung ein. Zeitnahe Beseitigung von arbeitsbezogener Überlastung oder Fehlbeanspruchung. Dafür streiten wir. Schließ dich uns an und sei aktiv für bessere gesündere Arbeitsbedingungen mit einem Tarifvertrag.Zukunft.IKEA. BETEILIGE DICH AN DEN KOMMENDEN AKTIONEN UND STREIKS!“


Meldung vom 28. März 2023 bei ver.di Handel

 


Streikgünde bei Ikea am Beispiel Fürth: Völlige Unterbesetzung, hoher Krankenstand, Frustration und Ausweglosigkeit

Die Angestellten sind wütend und fordern gesunde Arbeit in Zeiten der Digitalisierung. title: Tarifrunde Metall und Elektro 2026 für  5% mehr Geld, Jobsicherung und Gewinnbeteiligung für Boom-Unternehmen
content:
Dossier


„

Die Tarifbewegung in der Metall- und Elektroindustrie ist gestartet. Die Tarifkommissionen der IG Metall haben sich zusammengeschaltet, um die Lage und erste Forderungen zu diskutieren. Die Lage ist extrem differenziert: Viele Betriebe stecken in der Krise, andere wiederum machen gute Gewinne. Ab Oktober verhandelt die IG Metall wieder über höhere Entgelte für 3,8 Millionen Beschäftigte der Metall- und Elektroindustrie. Zum Auftakt zur Tarifbewegung haben die Tarifkommissionen der IG Metall am Mittwoch die Kündigung der derzeitigen Entgelttarifverträge in der Metall- und Elektroindustrie beschlossen – die Voraussetzung für Tarifverhandlungen – und die Diskussion über die wirtschaftliche Lage und mögliche Forderungen für die Tarifverhandlungen gestartet

…“

Meldung der IG Metall vom 25. Juni 2026

 

, die

Aktionsseite


 und erste Beiträge dazu:


Tarifverhandlungen in der Metall- und Elektroindustrie starten am 7. Oktober in Baden-Württemberg und Nordrhein-Westfalen mit Demonstrationen 


„

Heute startet die erste Runde der Tarifverhandlungen für die Metall- und Elektroindustrie in Baden-Württemberg und Nordrhein-Westfalen. Am Donnerstag geht es in Bayern, Niedersachsen und Sachsen-Anhalt weiter. Zehntausende Beschäftigte begleiten die Verhandlungen mit Demonstrationen.


Heute startet die erste Runde der Tarifverhandlungen für die Metall- und Elektroindustrie 2026. Die Verhandlungen führen die IG Metall-Bezirke dezentral mit den regionalen Arbeitgeberverbänden für 15 Tarifgebiete. Am Mittwoch geht es los in Baden-Württemberg und Nordrhein-Westfalen. Am Donnerstag folgen die Tarifgebiete Küste (Hamburg, Bremen, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Schleswig-Holstein, Niedersächsische Küste), Bayern, Niedersachsen, Osnabrück-Emsland-Grafschaft-Bentheim und Sachsen-Anhalt. Am Freitag verhandelt die IG Metall dann für die „Mittelgruppe“ (Saarland, Rheinland-Pfalz und Hessen). Nächste Woche folgen am Montag die Tarifgebiete Thüringen und Berlin-Brandenburg, sowie am Mittwoch Sachsen

…“

Meldung der IG Metall vom 6. Oktober 2026, aktualisiert am 7. Oktober 2026


 („Tarifverhandlungen in der Metall- und Elektroindustrie starten“)


Angeblich wollen Gewerkschafter die Lohnverhandlungen „revolutionieren“. Zur Tarifrunde 2026 in der Metall- und Elektroindustrie und einen unmöglichen (?) Spagat der IG Metall 


„

Den folgenden Ausführungen sei dieser „Disclaimer“ vorangestellt: Wenn jemand davon schreibt, dass in Deutschland etwas „revolutioniert“ werden soll, dann handelt es sich vor dem Hintergrund der bisherigen Erfahrungen entweder um traumtänzerische Rosstäuscherei oder aber um den überschießenden Beschreibungsversuch einer etwas stärkeren Veränderung des Bestehenden im Sinne seiner (punktuellen) Weiterentwicklung. Diesen Hinweis sollte man im Hinterkopf behalten, wenn in diesen gerade für viele industrielle Branchen schwierigen, für die Metall- und Elektroindustrie und darunter der so bedeutsamen Automobilindustrie besonders schwierigen Zeiten ein Beitrag mit so einer verheißungsvollen Überschrift versehen wird: 

Gewerkschafter revolutionieren Lohnverhandlungen

 

: »Die Autoindustrie baut massenhaft Stellen ab, während Rüstungsfirmen boomen. Wie soll da ein gemeinsamer Lohnabschluss für Millionen Beschäftigte klappen? Jetzt gibt es eine ungewöhnliche Idee«, so Alexander Hagelüken. (…)


Schaut man sich die bisherigen Tarifabschlüsse etwas genauer an, dann kann man zum einen erkennen, dass fast alle Gewerkschaften mit hohen Forderungen1 in die Tarifrunden eingestiegen sind (im Spektrum zwischen 5 bis 7 Prozent, teilweise in Verbindung mit Forderungen nach einer besonderen Berücksichtigung unterer Lohngruppen in Form von Mindestbeträgen der Anhebungen). Allerdings muss man zur Kenntnis nehmen, dass die bislang tatsächlich erreichten Abschlüsse hinsichtlich der Vergütungen weitaus niedriger dimensioniert sind. Zum anderen fällt die – wieder einmal – lange Laufzeit der neu verhandelten Tarifverträge ins Auge.2 Eine Laufzeit von 27 Monaten und mehr dominiert die Ergebnislandschaft.


Und was macht die IG Metall (nicht)?


Früher war sicher nicht alles besser, aber man konnte in der Vergangenheit gerade als im nicht-industriellen Bereich tätiger Lohnabhängiger regelmäßig das nicht erfüllbare Wunschgebet vortragen, dass man doch lieber von der starken IG Metall vertreten werden möchte, um von deren teilweise sehr üppigen Lohnabschlüssen profitieren zu können. title: Artist Cesim Başboğa sentenced to 10 months in prison
content:
Artist Cesim Başboğa was prosecuted over songs he performed at the Culture and Arts Festival held in Tatvan (Tetwan), Bitlis (Bedlîs), in 2025.


The songs Serhildan Jiyan e, Lê Amedê and Zana û Andok, which Başboğa performed at the festival, were cited as evidence in the case brought against him on allegations of “making propaganda for an organization.”


At the second hearing of the case, held today at the Bitlis 2nd High Criminal Court, the court sentenced Başboğa to 10 months in prison.


Başboğa said in his defence that, at a time when peace is being discussed, imposing sentences on artists who perform music in their mother tongue harms the process.

title: Karasu: Democratization is for everyone
content:
KCK Executive Council member Mustafa Karasu discussed developments in Kurdistan, Turkey, and the Middle East during a special program on

Medya Haber

.


Referring to the ongoing “Peace and Democratic Society” process, Karasu noted that the movement had taken the necessary steps, but that the Turkish state was still resisting. He said that a century-old problem such as the Kurdish issue could not be resolved through old laws, an outdated legal framework, or an old political approach.


Reminding that the existing laws had failed to resolve the issue, leading to decades of conflict, Karasu stressed that new laws guaranteeing freedom must be enacted in order to resolve the problem.


This is the first part of the interview.


Kurdish people’s leader Abdullah Öcalan sent a message to the Peace and Democratic Integration conference held in London. A notable assessment in this message was that if the republic does not become democratic, democratic integration will not be realized either. How should this be understood?


Now, we speak of democratic integration and unification. The unification of two things: the unification of the Kurdish people with the state and with the Turkish people on a democratic basis. And what is this democratic basis? It will be based on the recognition of the fundamental, democratic rights of the Kurdish people. On one hand, it is integration, and on the other, it is democratic. Without democracy, there could be no integration. In this regard, local democracy is an absolute prerequisite. All obstacles facing the Kurds – regarding their language, culture, and identity – must be removed. Democratic integration is, in fact, the democratization of the republic. Contrary to what some claim – that democratic integration can be achieved without recognizing any of the Kurds’ rights, demands, or legal claims – such a thing does not exist. We do not seek this solely for the Kurds. Rêber Apo does not seek it solely for the Kurds either. We cannot demand democracy only for ourselves. To demand democratization is to demand it for everyone. Rêber Apo has made this clear. It is for the Alevis, for women, for workers, and for the environment. It’s not as if integration is just an agreement between the Kurds and the state. All communities will benefit from this. Democratic integration is necessary for all communities. It is necessary for Alevis as well. The Alevis’ freedom of belief and their democratic rights must be recognized. That is what democratic integration is. There is no such thing as a centralized, all-controlling integration – no such integration exists. Integration does not mean accepting the policies that the Turkish state has implemented up until now. That is not what Rêber Apo means by democratic integration. It is an integration for all oppressed ethnic and religious communities. All of them will be part of this democratization.


Democratization is not tied to certain individuals or a particular group. That is not how it should be understood. The democracy and democratization we understand apply to all communities. It is the democratization of the Republic; it is a democratic Turkey. This must be understood exactly this way. Any other interpretations are pure nonsense. There’s no need for demagoguery. This is a nonviolent solution. Because a nonviolent solution is necessary for Turkey, and it is necessary for us as well. It is not a solution involving the establishment of a separate nation-state. We have abandoned that idea. But democratic integration does not mean turning oneself in to the state; it certainly does not mean giving up the Kurds’ fundamental democratic rights. No one should misunderstand this. Nor does integration mean that someone will go somewhere, become a civil servant, or serve as a state official – democracy isn’t like that, and neither is integration. Integration is a contract with society. It is a compromise reached with society. It is the recognition of society’s fundamental rights. At its core, it is the recognition of local democracy. This is true for Turkey, as well as for Rojava and all other parts of Kurdistan.


Democratic integration is not about someone going somewhere, speaking on behalf of others, becoming a civil servant, or assuming government authority – that is not democratic integration. Do the rights of society not recognize democratic foundations? Is there local democracy? That is integration. Integration must be properly understood everywhere – in …

title: Students in Afrin and Aleppo demand a solution
content:
Although the new academic year began a couple of months ago, the situation of nearly 1,000 students studying in Autonomous Administration schools, as well as the teachers working in these schools, remains uncertain.


Dozens of students attending Autonomous Administration schools held a protest in Efrîn over the continued uncertainty surrounding their situation.


The students said they were being systematically excluded as students from Efrîn and Aleppo, stating that this exclusion ranged from being deprived of education to deficiencies in language instruction.


The statement said that students and teachers had not been included in the integration of social institutions or the education system, and called for steps to be taken as soon as possible.


It was stated that a transition process would be prepared within the framework of the Autonomous Administration’s curriculum for students in the ninth and twelfth grades. However, the statement noted that no action had been taken for the nearly 1,000 students in these two grade levels.


The students demanded that their requests be addressed within two weeks, saying that otherwise they would continue taking to the streets.

title: Call for investigation into boards blocking women prisoners’ release
content:
A protest was held outside the Ministry of Justice in Ankara over the repeated blocking of the release of women prisoners held in Sincan Women’s Closed Prison. Protesters called for an investigation into the Administrative and Observation Boards responsible for postponing release decisions.


The protest, organized by the Federation of Legal Solidarity Associations for Prisoners’ and Convicts’ Families (TUHAD-FED), was attended by representatives of political parties and legal organizations, as well as many others.


At least nine women prisoners at Sincan Women’s Closed Prison are currently being prevented from being released, including women who have been imprisoned for more than 30 years.


Nedime Yaklav, who has been in prison for 34 years, has had her release postponed seven times. Hicran Binici, imprisoned for 33 years, and sisters Nuriye and Devrim Adet, who have been in prison for 32 years, have each had their releases postponed five times. Zeliha Ustabaş’s release has been blocked four times, while Fatma Aslan and Melike Göksu have each had their releases postponed three times. Emine Abiş, who has been imprisoned since 2021, has also had her release postponed three times.


Berfin Babaoğlu, secretary of the Prison Commission of the Ankara Branch of the Lawyers for Freedom Association (ÖHD), read out the statement and said the repeated postponement of women prisoners’ releases could no longer be regarded as isolated cases.


Babaoğlu said sentences imposed by courts could not be arbitrarily extended through the Administrative and Observation Boards, adding that assessing prisoners on the basis of their political identities, views and past positions amounted to “continued political punishment.”


‘Their releases are arbitrarily postponed’


Sihan Kaya, Ankara representative of TUHAD-FED, said the practice had become a serious problem, particularly for political prisoners.


Kaya said that since 2021, the Administrative and Observation Boards have postponed the release of many prisoners despite their eligibility for release. She called for an end to the practice and for prisoners whose releases have been blocked to be freed.


Kaya said at least nine women prisoners are currently facing barriers to their release, with some having had their releases postponed as many as seven times.


‘The practice has spread to other prisons’


Lawyer Fatma Sürücü, an executive of the Ankara Branch of the ÖHD, said the blocking of releases was not limited to Sincan Women’s Closed Prison but had also spread to other prisons.


Sürücü said the current practices effectively deprive prisoners of their right to release, adding that prisoners who meet the conditions for release are also not being freed.


Ministry must take action


Serhat Eren, Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) MP for Diyarbakır (Amed), said there was a “specific and systematic” practice of blocking releases at Sincan Women’s Closed Prison.


Eren said the Administrative and Observation Boards were acting in place of the judiciary by preventing releases and noted that postponement decisions exceeding one year had recently been issued.


He called on the Ministry of Justice to immediately launch an investigation into the Administrative and Observation Boards, adding that legal organizations and prisoners’ families would file criminal complaints if the ministry failed to take action.


The statement called for the release of prisoners who meet the conditions for release, an end to the Administrative and Observation Boards overriding court decisions and the repeated postponement of women prisoners’ releases, and for practices in prisons to be made transparent and subject to legal oversight.


The protest ended with the slogans “Jin, jiyan, azadî” (Woman, life, freedom), “Bijî berxwedana zindanan” (Long live the resistance in the prisons) and “Political prisoners are our honour.
