author: Christoph Morich
title: Theodor W. Adorno – Studien zum autoritären Charakter
content:
(Teil 1): Die Entwicklung der F-Skala zur Untersuchung des potentiell faschistischen Individuums


„Die Erfahrung aber und die Geschichte lehren, ist dieses, daß Völker und Regierungen niemals etwas aus der Geschichte gelernt und nach Lehren, die aus derselben zu ziehen gewesen wären, gehandelt haben.“ resümiert Hegel in seinen Vorlesungen zur Philosophie der Geschichte über das Verhältnis der gegenwärtigen Praxis zur eigenen Vergangenheit. Das gilt nicht nur für jenen Teil der Gesellschaft, der sein Glück nun wieder in der Hingabe an die deutsche Volksgemeinschaft zu suchen scheint, sondern lässt sich auch an den Reaktionen der bürgerlichen Öffentlichkeit beobachten, die einmal mehr nicht verstehen kann, warum um alles in der Welt nun schon wieder der Faschismus um die Ecke kommt. Die AFD scheint plötzlich vom Himmel gefallen zu sein und bedroht nun unsere demokratische Gesellschaft, in der doch bisher im Groben und Ganzen immer alles gut lief. Monchi, der Sänger einer Punk-Band, erinnert die deutsche Bevölkerung daran, dass wir schließlich nicht in Bangladesch leben, während Friedrich Merz darüber sinniert, wie er die Menschen emotional besser mitnehmen könnte, wenn er ihren Lebensstandard dem von Bangladesch annähert. Insgeheim haben sich längst alle politischen Akteure darauf geeinigt, dass die Geflüchteten selbst das ursächliche „Problem“ sind und die Lösung scheint nun darin zu bestehen, die rassistischen Forderungen der AFD einfach selbst umzusetzen. Zwischen Olaf Scholz‘ Ankündigung im Jahr 2023, nun endlich im großen Stil abzuschieben, bis zum Wahlslogan der AFD – „Wir werden abschieben, bis die Startbahn glüht.“ -, der ihr zum Wahlsieg verhalf, passt kaum ein Blatt Papier. „Migration steuern, bevor es die Falschen tun.“ brachte die FDP diese Politik in ihrem Europawahlkampf 2024 sehr prägnant auf den Punkt, die kaum deutlicher machen könnte, dass die qualitative Differenz zwischen Faschismus und bürgerlicher Gesellschaft relativ ist – die Faschisierung ist ein Prozess. „Der Schoß ist fruchtbar noch aus dem das kroch.“, heißt es dazu in einem Theaterstück von Bertolt Brecht. Die umfassendste Untersuchung zum sozialpsychologischen Schoß des Faschismus in der bürgerlichen Gesellschaft sind wohl die Studien zum autoritären Charakter, die als Reaktion auf den deutschen Nationalsozialismus in den USA durchgeführt wurden. Kein Weg führt an ihnen vorbei, wenn wir das sozialpsychologische Fundament unserer Gegenwart wirklich begreifen wollen.


Die Studien zum autoritären Charakter


Die Studien zum autoritären Charakter sind in ihrer Systematik ein Meisterwerk dialektischen Denkens, das einen bei der Lektüre verstehen lässt, was es bedeutet, einen Gegenstand analytisch zu erfassen, anstatt bei einer oberflächlichen Betrachtung zu verweilen. Sie heben sich in ihrer systematischen Ausarbeitung auch von den sonstigen Schriften Adornos zur Psychoanalyse ab, in denen er sonst oft recht eklektisch auf die Schriften Freuds Bezug nimmt. Das mag vor allem der Zusammenarbeit mit den drei weiteren Autoren der Studie geschuldet sein, deren Mitwirkung an der Studie in der heutigen Rezeption meist unter den Tisch fällt. Die Studien wurden unter der Leitung von Else Frenkel-Brunswik, Daniel J. Levinson, R. Nevitt Sanford und Theodor W. Adorno in einem mehrstufigen Verfahren, das Fragebögen, empirische Erhebungen, ausführliche Interviews und psychoanalytische Deutungsverfahren miteinander verknüpfte, zwischen 1944 und 1949 in Kalifornien durchgeführt. Entgegen eines sehr weit verbreiteten Vorurteils gegenüber dem Konzept des „autoritären Charakters“ geht es in den Studien ebenso wenig wie bei Reich oder Fromm darum, das Bewusstsein der Individuen zum eigentlichen Motor der Geschichte zu erklären. Von einer solchen Psychologisierung grenzen sich die Autoren in der Einleitung unmissverständlich ab: „Man scheint sich heute wohl bewusst, dass es in erster Linie von der Situation der mächtigen ökonomischen Interessengemeinschaften abhängt, ob antidemokratische Propaganda hierzulande eine beherrschende Rolle spielen wird oder nicht, ob jene, mit Vorbedacht oder nicht, sich dieses Instrumentes bedienen, um ihre Machtstellung aufrechtzuerhalten.“ (Adorno et al.) Auch heute dient die Faschisierung der herrschenden Klasse dazu, ihre Interessen gegen einen Großteil der Bevölkerung durchzusetzen. Daran lässt die mächtige ökonomische Interessensgemeinschaft des Silicon Valley, verkörpert von Wahnsinnigen wie Elon Musk und Peter Thiel, nicht …

author: Editors
title: The world since 7 October
content:
Gaza is a generational touchstone and the key dividing line of politics in the West. It has laid bare the lies of the society we live in. It has exposed the genocidal bloodlust of the political right. And it has tested official “progressive” liberal politics, which has so often shown itself to be utterly hollow or cowardly. 

Anyone can now use Google Maps’ satellite view to see for themselves the apocalypse wrought by Israel and its allies over the past three years. Gaza City, once home to around 700,000 people, is a mostly bombed-out hellscape of ruins. The same is true of Beit Hanoun, Jabalia and other major centres. 

Rafah was a city thousands of years old, first recorded in an inscription from 1303 BCE. It has now been wiped off the face of the earth. Google still displays location markers for what once existed: “Kamal Adwan School”, “Playground”, “Musab bin Amir Western Mosque”, now a pile of rubble—“temporarily closed”, according to Google.

About 80 percent of structures in the Gaza Strip have been damaged; two-thirds of those are destroyed, according to the United Nations agency for Palestinian refugees. Israel has used the so-called ceasefire since last December to systematically demolish remaining structures in the 60 percent of the Strip occupied by its forces, while killing another 1,200 Palestinians and herding around 2 million into unliveable tent cities in an ever-shrinking concentration camp.

When millions around the world poured into the streets to take a stand against this barbarism, they were viciously attacked and slandered by the institutions of our “democracy”, which have cried about “social cohesion” while turning a blind eye to the genocide and the growth of fascism they are helping to stoke.

The ruling class and the political establishment want to go after not just the Palestine movement, but the left more generally, which has naturally been at the centre of that movement. Hence the persistent effort to define antisemitism as a problem of the left rather than the far right, to ban the word “genocide”, and to criminalise opposition to the state carrying it out. 

This is not because loyalty to Israel itself is so important to the establishment, but because this loyalty test is a proxy for loyalty to Australian capitalism; a test of subservience to Australian billionaires, bosses and bureaucrats. 

Will you keep your mouth shut? Will you force that student to remove their keffiyeh? Will you cancel that author? Will you censor that article? Your answer will determine your place in Australian society. With troublemakers pilloried and purged, the apparatus can be hardened, ready to oversee the next war, the next genocide, the next round of cutbacks and layoffs, the next racist campaign against immigrants and refugees, as capitalism lurches towards its next crisis.

Despite the establishment’s intimidation and slander, and partly because of it, a seismic shift in attitudes has occurred. A July Pew Research poll found that 79 percent of Australians have a negative view of Israel, and just 4 percent have a strongly positive view. Hundreds of thousands have taken to the streets. The movement globally has been big, defiant, and defining for so many people who have thrown themselves into it. 

Yet it has not produced a widespread radicalisation or a sizable new left committed to confronting and overthrowing the capitalist system more broadly. There are many reasons for this, from the relative weakness of far-left organisations going into this period, to the weakness of the workers’ movement and spinelessness of trade union leaders.

The depth of feeling and moral commitment to the cause of Palestinian liberation is palpable, but the general political level remains low. Instead of generalising from the atrocity in Gaza to develop a critique of capitalism and imperialism, there is an obsession with the pro-Israel lobby, and there are illusions in reactionary opponents of the US and Israel such as the Iranian regime. Instead of open debate about the best strategies and tactics of resistance, recriminations focus on who is qualified to lead campaigns against the Australian government—not based on ideas or organisational skills, but on individuals’ identities. 

While our side sustained the largest anti-war movement in Australian history, the far right, rather than the left, has emerged as the most organised political force and is making all the running to push society in its desired direction: more …

author: Nick Everett
title: How the media sold the Gaza genocide
content:
When 700,000 Rohingya were forced to flee Myanmar for Bangladesh amid widespread killings, sexual violence and village burnings in late 2017, an

Age

editorial pleaded for Australian government action: 

“There is a genocide happening today in Myanmar. Our government should urgently, repeatedly and loudly call for international intervention, and lead in imposing sanctions. We should send bountiful aid to the victims, and halt economic and diplomatic relations with Myanmar unless and until the savagery is stopped. All of us, as Australians, should shun travel to Myanmar for tourism or business. And our government should, as it did with the Syrian refugee crisis a few years ago, rapidly engineer an intake of Rohingya refugees.”

The

Age

 didn’t wait for an International Court of Justice ruling before issuing its dire warning. It repeatedly used the term “genocide” to describe the Myanmar state’s atrocities despite no case of genocide having been brought before the ICJ at the time (it wasn’t until late 2019 that Gambia brought such a case and the ICJ still hasn’t ruled on it).

After three years of Israeli genocide in Gaza, no similar editorial can be found in the

Age

, nor in any of the mainstream media in Australia. That is despite Israel having killed more than 74,000 Palestinians, including over 21,280 children who,

according to

 a UN Commission of inquiry, have been targeted as “part of a deliberate strategy to destroy the future of the Palestinians in Gaza”. 

Indeed, “genocide” is a term that journalists—at the behest of their editors—routinely shun, despite the ICJ’s preliminary ruling back in January 2024 that there is a plausible case Israel is committing genocide. And when the term is used, we are reminded that Israel denies such claims, despite the UN Human Rights Council, the International Association of Genocide Scholars and numerous international human rights organisations having all concluded that Israel is indeed committing genocide in Gaza.

It is not just that the media fail to acknowledge this simple fact. For the past three years, they have been accessories to Israel’s crimes: dehumanising Palestinians, sanitising Israel’s atrocities, and silencing its critics. 

In his groundbreaking book

How to Sell a Genocide

, author Adam Johnson sets out to “prove beyond a reasonable doubt that the genocide in Gaza was enabled, facilitated, and cheered by establishment US media providing cover for months of a nihilistic campaign of starvation, bombing, arbitrary detention, shooting and sexual violence”.  

Johnson’s approach is methodical and meticulous. His research draws on more than 12,000 articles and 5,000 TV clips from nine major outlets during the first year of the genocide, including the

New York Times,

 the

Washington Post,

CNN


and


MSNBC


(now MSNOW

)

. He focuses on the liberal media because “there was a Democratic president in office when the genocide began in earnest, and support from Democrats in Congress and in the think-tank and media world was dispositive [decisive] in continuing said genocide during the given time of my study”.

Johnson argues that the “centre-left” (i.e., liberal) media engaged in “an elaborate framework of excuse-making, deflection, faux-savvy realpolitik, orientalist tropes, and glaring double standards … to justify the White House’s lockstep support for producing carnage everyone could easily witness across their social media timeline on a daily basis”.

“The primary role of [US liberal] media”, he argues, “was to rationalise, negotiate, obscure and ultimately, deny the most inconvenient of truths: a genocide carried out, defended and authorised by elite liberals and liberal institutions”.

Johnson demonstrates how the media were willing accomplices to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s efforts to portray 7 October as Israel’s “9/11 moment”, and to equate Hamas violence with that of ISIS, despite the two Islamist groups being implacable enemies. They did so by repeating and perpetuating a series of lies that emanated from Israeli media spokespeople: that Hamas beheaded 40 babies on 7 October 2023, that they targeted children and that they systematically used rape as a weapon of war.

New York Post

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Report: Trump Admin Is Deporting LGBTQ Asylum Seekers to Hostile Third Countries
content:
Officials have deported LGBTQ people to Sierra Leone, where they could face life in prison for same-sex activity.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The Trump administration has reportedly deported dozens of LGBTQ immigrants who sought or were granted asylum for their sexuality and gender to third countries where they face danger of persecution and criminalization, a new report says.

In an investigation published this week, Reuters identified 40 cases where these LGBTQ individuals were sent to countries that either criminalize same-sex relations or have been designated by the State Department as dangerous for LGBTQ people.

All of these people were granted legal protection in the U.S. for fleeing persecution for their LGBTQ status in their countries of origin, per Reuters. However, more than half of them were ineligible for asylum because of a restrictive Biden-era transit ban on asylum seekers.

Individuals tracked in the report have been deported to countries including Sierra Leone, Cameroon and Eswatini, three countries where same-sex acts are criminalized. In Sierra Leone, same sex acts carry a punishment of up to life in prison. Other countries that have signed deportation agreements with the U.S. have seen abuses against LGBTQ people like conversion therapy and “corrective rape,” the report notes.

The Trump administration has signed third country deportation agreements with at least 35 countries, and has deported over 25,000 people this way, sending them to places that they have no affiliation with. Many governments in Africa and central and South America have signed agreements to receive such deportees, often in exchange for direct funding or other financial incentives.

Reuters noted the story of one man, identified as Abdou Latifou, who fled his home country of Togo after a mob assaulted him and threatened to kill him after he kissed a man. A U.S. immigration judge decided last year that it was too unsafe for him to return home; he recalled thinking, “From this day on, I’m entering a world where I’m free to live as myself.”

But amid its mass deportation campaign, and while knowing that Latifou was gay, the Trump administration deported him to Sierra Leone, where he was held for two weeks under police surveillance before being put on a flight to Togo. Fleeing danger yet again, he went to the Ivory Coast, where he lives in fear of being recognized.

“When an individual is no longer in ICE custody then ICE will no longer be responsible for them,” Department of Homeland Security spokesperson ​Chandler Rebel told Reuters.

The report is the latest documenting the Trump administration’s deportations of people to places where they may be endangered. Other reports this week found that the Trump administration deported a former political prisoner back to the place he was imprisoned and tortured last week. Jeffrey Jarquín, who led pro-democracy protests against the Nicaraguan government, was reportedly taken directly from the deportation flight to the capital of Managua to a notorious Nicaraguan prison.

The Trump administration is facing a lawsuit from Iranian asylum seekers who say that U.S. officials secretly shared sensitive information, including LGBTQ status, about them with the Iranian government — as it’s tried to deport them into a country where they may face persecution.

Meanwhile, the Trump administration has terminated Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Haitians in the U.S., and has deported hundreds of immigrants back to Haiti, which has experienced a surge of violence and hunger.

author: Chris Walker
title: US Surpasses 4,000 Cases of Measles, Highest Numbers Seen in a Generation
content:
“Even if I got hit by a truck tonight, HHS will never go back to what it was before,” Robert F. Kennedy Jr. bragged.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Pennsylvania has surpassed 1,000 measles cases this year — nearly four times the amount of cases recorded across the entire U.S. in 2024.

The Keystone State has recorded 198 hospitalizations and five deaths as a result of the ongoing measles outbreak.

On Monday, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul (D) declared an emergency order in New York, citing the rising number of measles cases in neighboring states, including Pennsylvania, and an increase in cases in rural areas.

The move comes as the total number of measles cases across the U.S. this year has reached 4,020, according to figures collected by Johns Hopkins University. Aside from Pennsylvania, Texas and South Carolina are also at or near the 1,000-cases mark.

There haven’t been this many cases of measles in the U.S. since the early 1990s.

The current numbers mark a significant departure from the number of cases seen just a few years ago. In 2024, for example, there were only 285 cases identified across the entire U.S. That rate increased to 2,289 cases in 2025, the first year that President Donald Trump returned to office and appointed Robert F. Kennedy Jr., a noted anti-vaxxer, to lead the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).

Measles was once declared virtually eliminated in the U.S., as widespread vaccination for the virus vastly drove down case numbers. However, as anti-vax movements and right-wing disinformation gained influence over the past two decades, the rate of Americans receiving the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine decreased, likely leading to the current increase in cases. Notably, the MMR vaccine has a higher threshold than most vaccines to provide broader protection to a community.

A two-dose regimen generally provides an individual with lifetime protection from measles — and when breakthrough cases do occur, they tend to be milder and less dangerous because of the vaccine. Conversely, when unvaccinated people are infected with the virus, it can result in lifetime complications, including neurological and respiratory issues, or even death.

Despite the number of measles cases rising, Kennedy bragged about his controversial HHS tenure to an audience of MAHA (Make America Healthy Again) supporters in a speech in Washington, D.C. last week.

“Even if I got hit by a truck tonight, HHS will never go back to what it was before,” Kennedy said.

Under Kennedy’s leadership, HHS has overseen changes to the childhood vaccine schedule with little to no scientific basis, issued questionable changes to food advisory standards, and undergone major layoffs.

author: Sara Fayyazi
title: Addressing the Economic Costs of Sexual Violence: The Survivors’ Rights Restitution Act
content:
On September 15, 2026, Rep. Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), Rep. Teresa Leger Fernandez (NM-03), and Rep. Deborah Ross (NC-02) introduced the Survivors Rights Restitution Act. This legislation would establish a federal restitution program for survivors of sexual violence whose rights were violated by the federal government. The bill would include survivors of abuse by Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell while addressing the financial burden that can occur from sexual violence.

The bill focuses on the economic consequences that survivors can face long after an assault. The estimated lifetime cost of rape at $122,461 per victim, including the expenses of medical care, loss of income, housing instability and mental health support. These expenses can become an additional burden for survivors as they recover from trauma. The proposed restitution program would provide compensation for certain economic and non-economic harms and losses.

Under the legislation, an independent Office of Special Adjudicators for Survivors Restitution would be established within the US Court of Federal Claims. The office would review petitions from survivors and determine awards through what the bill describes as a streamlined, non-adversarial and trauma-informed process. The legislation would also establish a Survivors Rights Restitution Fund within the Department of the Treasury. The funds would be financed through federal forfeiture proceeds connected to trafficking and sexual exploitation offenses, voluntary contributions, and authorized appropriations.

The legislation is also intended to address the gaps in the enforcement of survivors’ existing legal rights. Under the Crime Victims’ Rights Act, survivors have certain protections when they report crimes, including the right to receive timely and accurate notice of an accused person’s release. The bill’s sponsors point to the handling of Jeffrey Epstein’s 2008 plea agreement as an example of these rights not being adequately enforced. The sponsors argue that current law does not provide a specific avenue for financial relief when victims’ rights are violated.

Although the bill is closely connected to the Epstein case, its protections would extend to other survivors of sexual violence more broadly. Rape and sexual assault victimizations occur annually, while approximately two out of three sexual assaults go unreported, the legislation argues that when survivors do come forward, there should be a helpful and easy path towards restitution.

Pressley has experience working with survivors of sexual violence and the Epstein investigation. In May 2026, Pressley and House Oversight Committee Democrats held a field hearing in Palm Beach focused on the Epstein investigation and the long-term economic and emotional harms experienced by survivors.

The legislation has received endorsements from several survivor and women’s rights organizations like World Without Exploitation, me too. International, the National Alliance to End Sexual Violence, and many others.

Financial compensation cannot erase the trauma of sexual violence. However, supporters of the legislation argue that financial restitution can help survivors address some of the costs associated with recovery while providing a mechanism for accountability when the federal government fails to protect their rights.

The Survivors’ Rights Restitution Act would create a process for survivors to seek financial restitution when their rights have been violated by the federal government. The bill addresses not only the immediate consequences of sexual violence but also some of the long-term financial burdens survivors can carry. The legislation now faces the congressional process where it will be considered before any potential action is taken.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump Blocks International Board From Conducting Oversight of Midterm Elections
content:
This is the first time in over two decades that the US has rejected OSCE participation in a federal election.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

For the first time in more than two decades, the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) will not conduct oversight of the upcoming midterm elections after the Trump administration effectively blocked them from doing so, raising yet more alarm over the administration’s rapid erosion of free and fair elections in the U.S.

President Donald Trump has declined to invite the OSCE to witness the elections, which the group has done for every federal election since 2002.

The OSCE is an international group of 57 states, largely in the global North, most of which are located in Europe. The United States is a member country. The organization is a partner group to the UN, and was established in the 1970s to address issues of human rights, conflict prevention, and election integrity.

This mandate includes conducting oversight of elections in member countries. During the 2022 midterm elections, for instance, the organization sent a group of observers to examine components of the election like its administration, voter registration, the drawing of electoral maps, election law, and media coverage.

The U.S. joins only Russia and Belarus in rejecting the OSCE’s election monitoring.

On Tuesday, Senate Foreign Relations Committee Ranking Member Jeanne Shaheen (D-New Hampshire) said that Trump’s rejection of the monitors is “unprecedented.”

“[T]he Trump Administration’s failure to continue this practice is yet another step that risks undermining public trust in America’s safe and secure election system,” she said in a statement.

Democracy Docket, a media platform founded by voting rights attorney Marc Elias, called the move the “latest ominous sign that the U.S. is backsliding on democracy” when it first reported on the development last month.

“Refusing election observers is usually something that countries in a position of weakness do, when they know that they have corrupt or unfair elections,” Dan Baer, a U.S. ambassador to the OSCE under Barack Obama, told MS NOW.

The State Department said the OSCE “should focus its limited resources on elections where it can have the greatest impact.”

The move comes as the Trump administration is seeking to deploy 1,000 monitors to poll sites this election cycle. This is a massive expansion of previous Department of Justice monitoring efforts, and comes as the Trump administration has sought to majorly disrupt the elections via sweeping restrictions to mail-in voting and threats to deploy ICE agents at polling sites.

The Trump administration has also picked ideological fights with the OSCE, of which the U.S. is a major financial contributor. Last year, the Trump administration issued an ultimatum to the group to undertake reforms or else face U.S. withdrawal from the group, Security and Human Rights Monitor reported.

In the OSCE’s ministerial meeting in Vienna last year, senior State Department official Brendan Hanrahan complained that the group’s “public facing work reads like a catalog of ideological projects that many of our societies have rejected or reversed, from opposing common sense asylum reform to misguided efforts to eliminate fossil fuels.” Hanrahan demanded that the group cut its annual budget, stop “dictating national social policy,” and engage Russia in conflict management.

We now have three full months of data since Google changed its search to feature AI results. The numbers are worse than we anticipated. Overall readership that comes to Truthout through Google is down 54 percent against last year. The number of new readers who discover Truthout via Google searches is down 49 percent, and returning users from Google are down 51 percent.

We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We anticipate a loss of roughly $500,000 in online revenue as a result of this massive traffic plunge in the next year alone.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: NTI names Navarana Beveridge its new CEO
content:
This story was updated Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026, at 5:09 p.m. ET.


Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. has named Navarana Beveridge its new chief executive officer.


The Inuit rights-holding organization in Nunavut announced the appointment Monday in a news release.


Beveridge’s hiring fills a vacancy left by Kilikvak Kabloona, who left in June,

one week after

 beneficiaries elected Gloria Uluqsi as the the organization’s new president on May 27.


“Gloria has just gotten on as NTI’s new president,” Beveridge said in an interview Tuesday. “I met her while she was campaigning and thought she was a very interesting, grounded leader, very genuine in her wanting to make a difference in the communities and working for Inuit. And that really appealed to me.”


“Navarana understands our organizations, our communities and the issues that matter to Nunavut Inuit,” Uluqsi said in the release. “She brings strong leadership experience, but just as importantly, she understands that our work must remain grounded in the people we serve.”


Beveridge said she wanted to join NTI’s leadership because she’s optimistic about Nunavut’s future.


“I think NTI is at a very exciting point in time, where there’s a lot of opportunities and possibilities to do good things,” the she said.


Beveridge was born and raised in Greenland and spent 17 years working at the Qikiqtani Inuit Association, most recently as their senior director of strategic planning. In 2021, the Kingdom of Denmark appointed her as its

honorary consul

 in Nunavut.


She speaks four languages — Inuktitut, English, Kalaallisut and Danish. Throughout her career, she helped negotiate the Mary River iron mine’s Inuit Impact Benefit Agreement and also oversaw the creation of the Qikiqtani Inuit Association’s research and training centre in Pond Inlet, which had its grand opening at the end of September.


Uluqsi said in a news release on Monday that the new CEO “brings strong leadership experience, but just as importantly, she understands that our work must remain grounded in the people we serve.”


Beveridge is expected to officially begin on Oct. 13.


Correction:

This article has been updated to correct information about Kabloona’s departure from NTI.

author: Keri Blakinger
title: What Happened During Christa Pike’s Scheduled Execution Isn’t an Anomaly
content:
The factors show how easily another failed execution could occur, even as others are planned soon in Texas and Florida.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Over the course of two hours, witnesses watched and listened as Christa Pike cried, whimpered and snored through Tennessee’s attempt to execute her. By the end of it, executioners had given her two doses of the state’s lethal injection drugs. Her arms were swollen and blistered, and one had turned purple, her attorneys said. And she was still alive, marking what legal experts say is the first time a prisoner in the U.S. has survived one dose — let alone two — of lethal injection drugs.

Even if the outcome was unprecedented, what went wrong was not. Pike’s was the third Tennessee execution in 14 months to go awry. But as a reporter who has covered death row for nearly a decade and witnessed several executions, I know the state is not alone. The factors behind the breakdowns in Tennessee have popped up again and again across the country — and show how easily another botched execution could occur, even as soon as the ones planned Wednesday in Texas and next week in Florida.

Here’s what we know about Tennessee’s attempt to execute Pike: The procedure started more than nine hours late, delayed by last-minute legal fights. Then, inside the death house, executioners struggled to find a vein, jabbing Pike with at least seven needles, according to her lawyers, one of whom watched in dismay. As the caustic barbiturate finally started flowing into the IV lines, Pike did not fall into sedation quickly. Instead, witnesses said, she sang with her spiritual adviser. Then she said her arm felt like it was about to burst open. “Does this happen like that?” she asked.

Like Pike, many aging death row prisoners have medical problems that can complicate efforts to kill them, potentially turning what are supposed to be relatively quick deaths into agonizing, drawn-out procedures. Even when prisoners are healthy, several states have faced questions about the competence of their execution teams, as both the American Medical Association and American Nurses Association have strongly opposed their members taking part in death penalty procedures. And death penalty states across the country shroud their executions in such secrecy that it is often difficult or impossible to confirm the age, source or sterility of the drugs.

“The types of failures that went into this botch happen all the time,” said Robert Dunham, director of the Death Penalty Policy Project. “There is nothing in the execution process that states are incapable of getting wrong.”

The Tennessee Department of Correction declined to comment, though hours after the attempted execution the agency said in a statement that it had “followed every step” of the state’s established protocol, which “has been consistently effective.” On Saturday, the head of the agency resigned. Meanwhile, Gov. Bill Lee said in a statement that he had ordered “a comprehensive, third-party review to determine exactly what occurred” and that the execution previously scheduled for December would no longer take place this year. His office didn’t respond to a request for comment.

On Friday, Pike’s lawyers filed a motion asking a court to order the agency to preserve any evidence related to the state’s failed effort to kill their client. In a statement, they said the filing “details the serious complications that occurred during the execution attempt, many of which Christa and her attorneys had warned the State and the courts about months earlier.” Pike remains critically ill in the hospital, they said, where she is on a ventilator, intubated and unconscious.

By the time the Tennessee Department of Correction strapped her to the gurney last week, Pike had been on death row for 30 years. She had been sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, a fellow Job Corps student in Knoxville. Pike was 18 at the time and, like many people on death row, had a history of mental illness and childhood sexual abuse.

Now 50 years old, Pike has faced an array of health problems, which her legal team had repeatedly warned could lead to a bungled execution. content:

ΚΑΛΕΣΜΑ ΣΕ ΚΙΝΗΤΟΠΟΙΗΣΗ/CALL TO DEMO [GR/ENG]


Κινητοποίηση στο Υπουργείο Μετανάστευσης και Ασύλου την Τετάρτη 07/10 09:00 (Λεωφόρος Θηβών 196-198)


Tην Τετάρτη 7 Οκτώβρη ο Soner Inanç πολιτικός αγωνιστής για τα εργατικά δικαιώματα και τις δημοκρατικές ελευθερίες στην Τουρκία κλείνει 42 ημέρες απεργίας σε απεργίας πείνας ενώ είνα διαδοχικά από τα τέλη Ιούλη σε κράτηση στο ΑΤ Λαυρίου, έπειτα στη Θεσσαλονίκη και από τις 9 Σεπτέμβρη στο ΠΡΟΚΕΚΑ Παρανεστίου Δράμας. Τα αιτήματα της απεργίας πείνας είναι η απελευθέρωση του και η απόδοση καθεστώτος ασύλου.


Σε ενδεχόμενη απόρριψη του αιτήματος ασύλου του ο Soner Inanç κινδυνεύει με άμεση απέλαση και φυλάκιση στην Τουρκία. Ο ίδιος αναγκάστηκε να εγκαταλείψει την Τουρκία καθώς έχει στοχοποιηθεί για την πολιτική δράση του από το τουρκικό κράτος και ήδη έχει φυλακιστεί στο παρελθόν για τη συμμετοχή του στο κίνημα του Gezi Park.


Στις 5 Οκτωβρίου εκδόθηκε η απόφαση του Διοικητικού Πρωτοδικείου Καβάλας επί των αντιρρήσεων κατά της κράτησης του. Η απόφαση απορρίπτει τις αντιρρήσεις του Soner, βασιζόμενη σε μία σειρά από ψευδείς παραδοχές και νομικές υπερβάσεις μετά από πρωτοφανή, πολιτικού χαρακτήρα, παρέμβαση του ΠΡΟΚΕΚΑ Δράμας μέσα από τον ψευδή ισχυρισμό πως ο Soner Inanç ξεκίνησε απεργίας στις 18/09 (!!). Για όλους εμάς, αυτή παρέμβαση καταδεικνύει την πολιτική στοχοποίηση του όπως και όλων των πολιτικών προσφύγων από την Τουρκία μέσα από τις όχι-και-τόσο-κρυφές συμφωνίες μεταξύ Ελλάδας και Τουρκίας. Ταυτόχρονα, η “λογική” των απορριπτικών ως τώρα αποφάσεων της υπηρεσίας ασύλου καταδεικνύει τις συνέπειες των μεγάλων αλλαγών που έχουν επέλθει στο καθεστώς ασύλου τα τελευταία έτη καθώς έχουμε να κάνουμε με την καταστρατήγηση της έννοιας του πολιτικού ασύλου. Γι’αυτό και ο αγώνας του Soner είναι και αγώνας για το πολιτικό άσυλο γενικότερα και χρειάζεται τη στήριξη όλων μας.


Καταγγέλουμε το ΠΡΟΚΕΚΑ Δράμας, τη δίοικηση και το ιατρικό προσωπικό του για την σκοπίμως ελλειπέστατη πρόσβασή του σε υπηρεσίες υγείας και την υποβολή του Soner σε εξευτελιστική μεταχείριση, προσπαθώντας να τον «πείσουν» (δηλαδή, να τον πιέσουν) να σταματήσει την απεργία ή ελέγχοντας αν «όντως δεν τρώει». Μετά από πολλές εβδομάδες στέρησης βιταμινών, αναγκαίων για την μη ύπαρξη μόνιμων επιπτώσεων, το αίτημα αυτό άρχισε να καλύπτεται όπως όφειλε εξαρχής μετά από συνεχή πολιτική κινητοποίηση και δημοσιογραφική κάλυψη για τον κίνδυνο τον οποίο διατρέχει αν δεν του χορηγηθούν. Το ΠΡΟΚΕΚΑ Παρανεστίου οφείλειως απεργός πείνας ο Soner Inanç να παρακολουθείται από ανεξάρτητη ιατρική επιτροπή για να διασφαλιστεί η απρόσκοπτη άσκηση της ως πολιτική δράση με συγκεκριμένα αιτήματα: τη συνέχιση της διαδικασίας απόδοση ασύλου, την μη απέλαση του στην Τουρκία και την απελευθέρωσή του. Ο Soner δηλώνει αποφασισμένος να συνεχίσει στον αγώνα του, αφού κρατείται άδικα, περιμένοντας νέα απόφαση για το άσυλό του.


Την Τετάρτη 7 Οκτώβρη εξετάζεται και πάλι προσφυγή επί του αιτήματος ασύλου του, απόφαση για την οποία χρειάζεται να εκδοθεί το συντομότερο δυνατό καθώς η απεργία πείνας του Soner βρίσκεται σε εξαιρετική επικίνδυνο στάδιο. O Soner Inanç δε ζητάει τίποτα περισσότερο και τίποτα λιγότερο από μια ανεπηρέαστη απόφαση, η οποία θα αναγνωρίσει την ουσία του ζητήματος: ο Soner Inanç διώκεται πολιτικά και ως εκ τούτου ποινικά από το τουρκικό κράτος και τους κατασταλτικούς μηχανισμούς του. Η πολιτική στοχοποίηση στο ελληνικό κράτος είναι μια δεύτερη δίωξη, η οποία καταστρατηγεί κάθε έννοια ασύλου.


Στηρίζουμε σε όλα τα επίπεδα την άμεση απελευθέρωση και απόδοση πολιτικού ασύλου στον Soner Inanç. Σε αυτήν την κατεύθυνση καλούμε σε:

author: Brian Dolinar
title: Activists Target What They Call a Major “Spy Center” for ICE in Rural Vermont
content:
As ICE widens its surveillance dragnet, activists plan a week of action to disrupt a major data network.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

After setting up robust rapid-response groups to resist Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) abductions and stopping the buying up of warehouses to detain thousands of immigrants, activists are now focusing on other ways they can disrupt the Trump administration’s plans for mass deportations. On the East Coast, some are targeting the parking spots that ICE uses for staging arrests. In Buffalo, New York, people are fighting to evict ICE from an office building where they coordinate operations and detain people. In Vermont, activists are planning a week of action to shut down a major ICE surveillance center hidden away in an office park.

Vermont has a reputation as a progressive state that is home to the democratic socialist Sen. Bernie Sanders and the birthplace of Ben & Jerry’s ice cream, whose founders are known for their political activism. The second-least populous state in the country, the federal government is also taking advantage of Vermont’s remoteness to conduct surveillance on immigrants.

The National Criminal Analysis and Targeting Center is housed at the White Cap Business Park in Williston, a rural town in Vermont with a population of about 10,000. Activists say it is one of two such centers, with the other one located in Laguna Niguel, California, based in conservative Orange County.

The Law Enforcement Support Center is also located nearby, on Williston’s Harvest Lane, where ICE operates a hotline for anyone across the country who wants to call in to report “suspicious activity.” The hotline center boasts that it is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week to process 55,000 hotline tips annually.

The capability to process mass amounts of data is dizzying. Both facilities are part of a “Targeting Operations Division” that processes 1.55 million biometric and biographic queries annually. ICE claims to have access to 340,000 records. The agency communicates with more than 13,000 law enforcement agencies throughout the country, many of them through an expanding network of 287(g) agreements that incentivize collaboration between ICE and local police. In 2021, the division analyzed records of some 7.7 million people for the “identification and removal of criminal noncitizens in the United States.”

Since 9/11, there has been a proliferation of these kinds of fusion centers and real-time crime centers, which amass large amounts of information for police surveillance systems. Automated license plate readers, like those sold to police by Flock Safety, have received the greatest amount of public scrutiny, but there are other tools like facial recognition technology, drones, ShotSpotter, and social media monitoring software.

Activists in Vermont are putting a spotlight on the ICE office to expose what they call a major “spy center” carrying out an unprecedented level of state violence.

The full scope of the government’s growing surveillance operations is not yet known, but details about last summer’s escalation of ICE violence are emerging.

During so-called “Operation Midway Blitz” in Chicago, Marimar Martinez, a 30-year-old citizen and school teacher, was shot five times by Border Patrol agent Charles Exum. She later testified before members of Congress about the horrifying incident. Martinez’s lawyers just announced she is filing a civil lawsuit in federal court.

On October 4, 2025, while driving to church, Martinez spotted federal agents patrolling her neighborhood. She started to follow them, honking her horn and shouting “la migra” out of her window. The agents rammed into her car with their truck. Exum then got out and opened fire on Martinez’s car as she drove off. She was taken to a hospital and treated for her wounds. The next day, she was charged with assault of federal agents and labelled a “domestic terrorist” in a Homeland Security statement.

The charges against her were later dropped, but new information has come out that federal agents tapped the network of Flock automated license plate reader cameras maintained by local police in an attempt to locate Martinez. author: Aline Melo
title: Plataformas mantêm anúncios e recomendações políticas irregulares no dia da votação
content:
Investigamos o que importa para os brasileiros além do que passa na campanha eleitoral. Leia mais reportagens como essa clicando

aqui

.


Em meio às acusações sobre a interferência das Big Techs na integridade eleitoral brasileira,

plataformas digitais continuaram veiculando anúncios políticos irregulares e recomendando conteúdos de candidatos durante o período de resguardo do primeiro turno das

eleições de 2026.


O período de resguardo para a circulação paga ou impulsionada de propaganda eleitoral na internet compreende as 48 horas anteriores e as 24 horas posteriores à votação, conforme previsto no

art. 29, § 11, da Resolução TSE nº 23.610/2019.

 A norma também define, nos artigos 28 e 29, as formas de propaganda eleitoral na internet e as regras para o impulsionamento de conteúdo. 


O monitoramento identificou 568 anúncios irregulares na Meta, 18 anúncios ativos no Kwai e um no Google Ads, além de ao menos seis campanhas fraudulentas que imitavam o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

 O levantamento também encontrou recomendações orgânicas de conteúdos publicados por contas oficiais de candidatos no TikTok e no YouTube durante o dia da votação. Os dados são do Observatório das Big Techs, realizado pelo NetLab UFRJ, laboratório de pesquisa sobre internet e redes sociais vinculado à Escola de Comunicação da Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ). 


O monitoramento foi dividido em duas frentes: o Observatório da Publicidade Política, voltado aos anúncios pagos, e o Observatório da Recomendação Algorítmica, que analisou os conteúdos sugeridos organicamente por TikTok, YouTube e Instagram.


Anúncios de TSE falso dizem que eleitor poderia votar pela internet


Na frente de publicidade política, foram identificados os 568 anúncios veiculados irregularmente na Meta relacionados a 15 candidatos, além de 18 anúncios ativos no Kwai e um anúncio ativo no Google Ads durante o período de resguardo. No Kwai, os pesquisadores também encontraram 45 anúncios de 10 páginas de candidaturas cuja data-limite de circulação havia sido alterada para permitir que continuassem ativos no dia da votação.


Entre os casos identificados na Meta estão ao menos seis campanhas fraudulentas que se passavam pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) ou pela Justiça Eleitoral.

 Segundo o NetLab, os anúncios eram veiculados tanto por perfis que imitavam contas oficiais, utilizando a marca da Corte e nomes como “TSE Informa”, quanto por contas aparentemente pertencentes a usuários comuns.


As campanhas promoviam a falsa ideia de que o TSE teria criado uma modalidade oficial de “voto digital”, que permitiria ao eleitor votar remotamente, de casa ou pelo celular.

 Para dar credibilidade à fraude, os anúncios exploravam situações que poderiam dificultar o comparecimento presencial às urnas, como fortes chuvas, problemas de saúde e dificuldades de locomoção.


Ao clicar nas peças, o usuário era direcionado para sites externos que solicitavam o CPF para supostamente iniciar a votação. Uma das mensagens identificadas no monitoramento dizia: “Você não precisa de fila para votar. O TSE criou o voto digital para que você participe desta eleição pelo celular, com total segurança e praticidade”. O NetLab aponta que esse tipo de conteúdo poderia induzir eleitores a acreditar que não precisariam comparecer presencialmente às suas seções eleitorais, além de criar riscos relacionados à coleta de dados pessoais.


O monitoramento também identificou anúncios da loja Vinho B II Mito, que promoviam produtos como vinhos, facas e bonés utilizando imagens de figuras políticas e manifestações explícitas de apoio a candidaturas.


O boletim aponta problemas de transparência nas próprias ferramentas utilizadas para fiscalizar a publicidade. Na Meta, os pesquisadores encontraram inconsistências entre os anúncios classificados como “inativos” e aqueles que permaneciam disponíveis como ativos na biblioteca da plataforma. No Kwai, foram identificados rótulos como “em pausa”, sem documentação clara sobre o significado desses status, além de divergências entre os dados exibidos na plataforma e os dados que poderiam ser exportados para análise.


TikTok “para você” recomenda conteúdos políticos no dia de votação


Na segunda frente, o Observatório da Recomendação Algorítmica analisou como as plataformas recomendaram conteúdos políticos e de candidatos no dia da votação. Segundo o NetLab, a Resolução TSE nº 23.732/2024 estabelece regras sobre sistemas de recomendação …

author: Randi Beers
title: Baffinland seeks court approval for sale of assets
content:
Baffinland Iron Mines Corp. is seeking court approval to solicit bids on its shares and assets, which may include its Mary River Mine.


The company operates the mine on north Baffin Island and touts its ore as some of the highest-grade in the world. It began operations in 2014.


Baffinland

sought creditor protection

 in May and a

judge approved

 a $660-million loan from Export Development Canada in June so the mine could remain operational through this year’s shipping season.


The company

owes

 more than $1.2 billion it says it cannot repay to lenders that include private equity firms, the federal and Nunavut governments, and Inuit organizations and businesses.


The $660-million “debtor-in-possession” loan, said Export Development Canada lawyers Oct. 2 in a court filing, was “expressly tied” to Baffinland pursuing a sale of its assets.


The company’s debtors, lawyers and executives are hammering out details for what this proposed sale and investment solicitation process would look like.


At question is who has final say over a potential deal to sell the company or its assets. Export Development Canada and the company’s lenders want a neutral, court-appointed officer and court monitor to have final say, while Baffinland is pushing for a committee of shareholder representatives.


Meanwhile, Baffinland continues to operate while working through the creditor protection process, said company spokesperson Peter Akman Tuesday in an emailed statement.


“The court has not approved a sale of Mary River mine,” he said, adding a sale and investment solicitation process will explore “several” options, including refinancing.


A judge is scheduled to hear the proposed sale process on Oct. 9.

author: Esperanza
title: Dúo Kosa presenta Quién es quién: investigación escénica de terror y danza contemporánea
content:
El colectivo de investigación y creación en artes escénicas, Dúo Kosa, presentará su obra de danza contemporánea “Quién es quién” los días 8, 9 y 10 de octubre a las 20:00 horas en Teatro Trashumantes, Temuco. Una exploración por las posibilidades del horror como lenguaje corporal, a partir de intersecciones entre coreografía, terror y niñez.


Desde 2021, Dúo Kosa desarrolla una práctica de danza contemporánea centrada en la investigación coreográfica y en la creación de imágenes corporales que emergen desde lo inestable, lo desplazado y lo ambiguo. “Nuestro trabajo entiende la composición como un campo de experimentación situado y abierto a la anomalía, donde la escena se convierte en un espacio de estudio y de urgencia poética”, comenta Alex Sanzana, artista escénica de Temuco.


En

Quién es quién

, esa búsqueda se encuentra con una pregunta: ¿cómo se coreografía el terror? El proyecto comenzó desde una aproximación audiovisual y fotográfica, a partir de la imagen de dos cuerpos unidos por camisas cosidas, formando una especie de cuerpo transversal y alargado. “Aquella imagen, al mismo tiempo tenebrosa, viscosa y tierna, fue desplazando la investigación hacia la práctica coreográfica y abrió la pregunta que sostiene actualmente la obra”, recuerda Pipi Villadangos, artista escénico de Buenos Aires, integrante de Dúo Kosa.


Aunque el terror ha sido ampliamente explorado por el cine y la literatura, su presencia en la danza aparece aquí como una oportunidad para tensionar los imaginarios del horror en lugar de reproducir sus clichés. En

Quién es quién

, el miedo no se construye únicamente desde aquello que se representa, sino desde aquello que ocurre en el cuerpo: una textura, una vibración, un ritmo dislocado, un gesto suspendido o una oscilación permanente entre ternura y amenaza.


La niñez ocupa un lugar central en esta investigación. Duo Kosa recurre al llamado “tiempo niño”, entendido como ese estado de imaginación absorbente en que el juego puede suspender la lógica cotidiana, para aproximarse al miedo desde una dimensión sensorial y afectiva. Así, la escena se sitúa en un territorio ambiguo entre lo real y lo fantasmático: un cuerpo que juega mientras imagina que algo acecha detrás de la puerta.


La obra se estructura en cuatro cuadros y presenta una ficción campesina protagonizada por tres figuras ambiguas: dos niños que juegan en el bosque y un espantapájaros que parece marcar el camino hacia una trampa. Entre presencias invisibles, mutaciones entre lo humano y lo animal y ensoñaciones lúgubres, la escena construye un paisaje donde la imaginación infantil convive con lo inquietante. Juegos, embestidas, sospechas, alegrías y misterios atraviesan una danza en la que fuerzas extrañas parecen transformar permanentemente el territorio.


Quién es quién

 es también el resultado de un proceso de investigación sostenido en el tiempo. La obra comenzó con un laboratorio en Espacio Kom de Temuco en 2023, y continuó con una residencia de investigación en Teatro Puerto de La Serena, durante el 2024. En 2026, el proceso llegó nuevamente a Temuco para una residencia técnica y una apertura de proceso en Teatro Trashumantes.


De esta manera, la presentación en Teatro Trashumantes da continuidad a un proceso que ha transitado por distintos espacios de investigación y creación, consolidando una propuesta que utiliza la danza para explorar aquello que resulta difícil de nombrar: el miedo, la imaginación, la amenaza y esa zona incierta donde lo tierno puede volverse inquietante.


Sinopsis:

 La danza, la comedia y el terror se encuentran en este montaje para desatar anomalías en las líneas discursivas, a partir de una serie de acontecimientos atemporales que van llevando a los personajes por juegos, embestidas, sospechas, alegrías y misterios. Tal como sucedería en un cuento de fantasía, fuerzas externas o extrañas provocan texturas y escalofríos en el baile de dos niños que juegan compenetrados mientras un monstruo acecha tras los árboles.


Las entradas se compran mediante la web

Portal Disc

 y tienen un valor mínimo de 4500 pesos. Clasificación para mayores de 14 años. Pueden entrar menores de edad con un adulto acompañante.


Mientras que el

 domingo 11 de octubre, Quién es quién se presentará sin costo en el Centro Cultural de Lautaro,

 en el marco de la 6º edición del Festival de Danza Contemporánea Magma. 


Funciones:

 8, 9 y 10 de octubre, 20:00 horas.

Lugar:

 Teatro Trashumantes, Temuco.

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Condemned for Invoking Nuclear Attacks on US Cities to Defend Iran War
content:
Trump’s attempt to defend the war comes as polling shows that the conflict is deeply unpopular among US voters.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

President Donald Trump ambiguously suggested during a political rally on Monday that Iran could “take out” San Diego or Los Angeles.

The president’s remarks seemed to be an attempt to justify his ongoing war on Iran, which is deeply unpopular among American voters.

Addressing a crowd of supporters in Nebraska, Trump claimed that the economic impacts of the war were worth it to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

“Remember, with the war, it’s just artificial. It’s a little bit high,” Trump said regarding price increases in retail goods and gas. “It’s a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, keeping our country safe.”

“They could take out a city,” Trump added, stopping mid-sentence before continuing. “Let them take out Los Angeles. Let him take out San Diego.”

“This is a very small price to pay and [the war is] going to be over with very soon,” Trump said.

Trump has repeatedly claimed that the war is necessary to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon — despite the fact that the country’s leaders had already agreed not to pursue a nuclear weapons program before the U.S. launched the war in late February.

Trump on Iran: Let 'em take out Los Angeles and San Diego, it's a small price to pay

Several California lawmakers condemned the remarks by Trump, including Sen. Alex Padilla (D), who called for Trump’s removal from office.

“25th Amendment NOW,” Padilla wrote on X, referring to the amendment of the U.S. Constitution that allows the cabinet to determine if a president is no longer fit to serve.

Several critics interpreted Trump’s comments as an endorsement of hypothetical attacks on those two cities. Indeed, Trump did not correct himself when members of his audience cheered on the idea.

Meanwhile, the White House’s social media Rapid Response team issued a belligerent response to observers who came to that conclusion.

“No, he didn’t, you buffoons,” the response team wrote on X. “He was saying the U.S. is fighting to STOP Iran from having the ability to take out LA and San Diego with a nuclear weapon — which they would if they had the chance.”

Trump’s comments on Monday echo a statement he made in late September.

“If you want to see turmoil and travesty, let them take out a city with a nuclear weapon…let them hit us with a nuclear weapon,” Trump said at a press conference.

Iran is nowhere near being able to build a nuclear weapon, and wasn’t nearing those capabilities before the war began, when Washington and Tehran were engaging in indirect negotiations to avoid the conflict. Iran has reaffirmed at multiple points during the war that it has no intention of pursuing nuclear weapons.

It’s unclear if Trump is purposefully misleading the public or woefully ignorant of the situation at hand. His past remarks on issues relating to nuclear proliferation, however, suggest the latter option is a real possibility.

In 2015, during a Republican debate in the lead-up to the 2016 presidential race, Trump was clearly confused over a question about the nuclear triad — the U.S.’s capabilities to launch a nuclear attack or response by land, air, or sea. Reports from 2019 also indicate that Trump frequently asked White House aides whether launching a nuclear bomb directly into a hurricane could work to break it up before it made landfall. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration has warned that such a move would not only fail, but result in dangerous amounts of nuclear fallout.

The U.S.-Israeli war on Iran continues to be deeply unpopular among American voters. Recent polling demonstrates that more than 6 in 10 voters want the war to end as soon as possible.

Despite this sentiment, Trump said last week that the war should be a boost for Republicans in the midterms, blaming the media for supposedly putting a negative spin on the issue — again, mischaracterizing Iran’s nuclear capabilities to make his case.

“When you say, ‘Is it OK for Iran to have a nuclear weapon?’ I would say 100 percent of the people say no, including worldwide. So, when you say it that way, it would help” Republicans running on the issue, Trump said on Friday. “If you don’t say that, it could hurt.”

author: Caio de Freitas
title: Pela 1ª vez desde redemocratização, Brasil terá 10 militares no Congresso e nos governos
content:
Investigamos o que importa para os brasileiros além do que passa na campanha eleitoral. Leia mais reportagens como essa clicando

aqui

.


Dois governadores, dois senadores, quatro deputados federais e 23 suplentes no Congresso Nacional. Esse é o saldo das eleições para uma categoria muito próxima da direita e do bolsonarismo: os militares das Forças Armadas. Com raízes no Exército Brasileiro, um oficial de alta patente e dois de baixa patente são os responsáveis por fazerem dos resultados do último domingo (4) um marco histórico na militarização da política no país.


Nome forte do bolsonarismo na Câmara dos Deputados, o tenente-coronel da reserva do Exército Luciano Zucco (PL) teve 58% dos votos válidos para se tornar o primeiro militar das Forças Armadas eleito governador do Rio Grande do Sul desde os anos 1950 – quando o também tenente-coronel do Exército

Ernesto Dornelles

 foi eleito.


Um amigo de Zucco dos tempos de Academia Militar das Agulhas Negras (Aman), também se reelegeu governador no 1º turno – o capitão da reserva Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), com mais de 62% dos votos válidos em São Paulo. Isso torna esta a primeira

vez que

dois governadores ex-Forças Armadas

 são eleitos desde a redemocratização.


Zucco vai governar o Rio Grande do Sul ao mesmo tempo em que o colega de Aman Tarcísio de Freitas estará à frente de São Paulo


No Senado, a partir de janeiro de 2027 dois militares se juntarão ao general da reserva do Exército Hamilton Mourão (Republicanos-RS), um dos

fiadores do início da carreira política de Zucco

, em 2018, e ao tenente-coronel aviador da reserva da Aeronáutica Marcos Pontes (PL-SP): o capitão da reserva Renan Contar (PL-MS) e o 3º sargento reformado do Exército Antônio Nicoletti (PL-RR). Desde a Constituição de 1988, o Congresso Nacional nunca teve quatro senadores oriundos das Forças Armadas.


Mais de 856 mil eleitores votaram no capitão Contar para senador em Mato Grosso do Sul, na eleição seguinte àquela em que ele quase se elegeu governador com

apoio direto

 do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL). Antes, em 2018, o ex-capitão do Exército já tinha se tornado o deputado estadual mais bem votado da história de Mato Grosso do Sul, com 78 mil votos – marco não superado em 2026.


Atualmente deputado federal, o 3º sargento do Exército Antônio Nicoletti se elegeu senador por Roraima com apoio direto do candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ). Ele deixou a caserna para fazer carreira na Polícia Rodoviária Federal (PRF), mas enfatiza até hoje nas redes sociais a sua origem como “militar do Exército”. No governo Bolsonaro, Antônio Nicoletti foi inclusive homenageado pelo Exército com a honraria da Medalha do Pacificador, como mostra o

boletim

 da Força de julho de 2021.


Antônio Nicoletti foi eleito por Roraima e será um dos quatro militares a ocuparem cadeiras no Senado


Para o professor de Relações Internacionais da Universidade de Brasília (UnB) Juliano Cortinhas, o avanço de candidaturas militares destoa da aproximação das Forças Armadas com a candidatura (e o próprio mandato) do ex-capitão do Exército Jair Bolsonaro.


“Vejo que as Forças Armadas se afastaram da família Bolsonaro durante o atual governo, e, nesta corrida eleitoral, o Flávio não contou com eles, nem se aproximou. Então acho que vemos um movimento de indivíduos, mais do que propriamente da instituição militar, diferentemente do que ocorreu em 2018”, avalia Cortinhas, que coordena o Grupo de Estudos e Pesquisas em Segurança Internacional da UnB.


“Acho que o resultado do 1º turno das eleições sugere uma nova tendência, com cada vez mais militares candidatando-se a cargos eletivos daqui pra frente. Mas isso é um problema porque, em geral, militares são despreparados politicamente, seja por sua formação ideológica, seja pelo fato de não serem forjados para a política – e, na minha opinião, eles não devem ser preparados para tal, sob o risco de não cumprirem sua função”, afirma.


Já para o co-autor do estudo

Fardados Partidos

, que reflete sobre as relações históricas entre as Forças Armadas e a política no Brasil, pesquisador e doutor em antropologia social pela Universidade Federal de São Carlos (UFSCar) Guilherme Lemos, o resultado das urnas mostra falhas do atual governo e de seus antecessores em separar os quartéis da política partidária.

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Cambridge Bay helps keep Northwest Passage expedition moving
content:
A handful of bolts and a little help from Cambridge Bay residents kept a Polish sailing crew from being stranded in the Canadian Arctic.


Captains Alicja Latoń and Andrzej Górajek, who work for the Polish cruise and expedition company Natango, arrived in Cambridge Bay on Sept. 12 with a damaged propulsion system and were stuck for about a week.


Alicja Latoń, left, and Andrzej Górajek, right, crew members of the Polish sailing yacht Ocean A, stand ashore in Erebus Bay on Sept. 21, during the yacht’s eastbound return through the Canadian Northwest Passage. (Photo by Andrzej Górajek)


“It became the place that determined whether the entire second half of the expedition would be possible at all,” Górajek said in an email to Nunatsiaq News.


The pair is attempting to complete a trip that began July 29 with seven crew members. Their goal is to sail the Canadian section of the Northwest Passage in a single navigation season, from Upernavik, Greenland, to Tuktoyaktuk and back to Maniitsoq, Greenland.


“We wanted to find out whether a small sailing yacht could make the passage in both directions without wintering in between,” said Górajek, who is completing the return trip with Latoń.


The crew is calling the expedition, on the 75-foot Ocean A yacht, the “first known and documented” voyage rather than the first-ever, because historical records may be incomplete.


In Cambridge Bay, the crew determined a bearing needed to be replaced. It hired Qillaq Innovations, which offers technical and mechanical services, to help with some parts of the repair in its workshop.


The crew also needed high-strength bolts that were not available locally.


After contacting other vessels docked in the community, they were directed to the Canadian Coast Guard ship Louis S. St-Laurent, which supplied the bolts.


A supplier in Yellowknife located a bearing and shipped it to Cambridge Bay, while Canadian North gave the package priority to get it there on Sept. 17, she said.


Ocean A left two days later.


Latoń said residents offered rides to the workshop, the airport and elsewhere while the crew searched for parts. Others came by in the evenings to check on the crew or have tea with them.


“I think that if circumstances had somehow forced us to spend the winter in Cambridge Bay, we certainly would not have lacked company,” Latoń said.


According to VesselFinder, an online marine tracking service, the yacht is expected to reach Greenland on Oct. 10.

author: Camila Borges
title: Regra de 1968, ano do AI-5, embasa exonerações de professoras na rede estadual paulista
content:
Em janeiro deste ano, Veruschka de Sales Azevedo passou pouco mais de uma hora contando à

Agência Pública

 como perdera o cargo de professora na rede estadual de ensino de São Paulo. Ela chorou algumas vezes durante o encontro que foi finalizado com certa esperança: “O meu retorno será triunfante”, disse. Enquanto aguardava o desfecho do seu caso, ela organizava um livro com relatos de professores também investigados por meio de Processos Administrativos Disciplinares (PAD) na Secretaria de Educação de São Paulo (SEDUC). “A gente precisa registrar isso em tudo quanto é lugar.”

Doutora em história, Veruschka tinha 24 anos de magistério, cerca de vinte deles na mesma escola de Guarulhos onde estudara antes de ser exonerada em maio de 2024 num PAD que se iniciou em 2017.

 Entre a abertura do processo e a exoneração, passaram-se sete anos e seis meses.


Em março deste ano, num artigo no

Le Monde Diplomatique

, Veruschka escreveu que o trauma da exoneração lhe causara uma doença crônica. Ela viria a falecer em julho, seis meses após a entrevista para a reportagem.

 A família não divulgou a causa da morte, mas a filha, Rayssa Sales, não tem dúvida sobre a origem da doença: “Antes, a imunidade da minha mãe era perfeita, mas, depois da exoneração, ela começou a ficar doente.”


As acusações contra a professora na SEDUC apontam falta de comprometimento com os estudantes, tumulto em reuniões pedagógicas, incitação de alunos contra a direção e excesso de atenção a temas raciais e de empoderamento feminino nas aulas.

 


Três dias antes da demissão de Veruschka, também a professora Fabiana de Abreu, que ensinava história na mesma escola, fora exonerada. Em agosto de 2025, chegaria a vez de Maitée Nogueira, professora de sociologia em São Sebastião, no Litoral Norte paulista. As três contestaram as acusações em entrevista à

Pública

.

Os processos se apoiam em um estatuto anterior à Constituição de 1988: o dos servidores civis do estado, de 1968, ano do AI-5.

 Para Salomão Ximenes, professor da Faculdade de Educação da USP e pesquisador do Observatório Nacional da Violência contra Educadores (Onve),

os estatutos escritos durante o período ditatorial têm sido “ressignificados com o objetivo de dar mote a processos administrativos de perseguição a educadores”. 


Ele fala em

“lawfare educacional”: o uso de instrumentos jurídicos e burocráticos para conter a mobilização de professores, a luta sindical e os avanços no currículo.

 Além de São Paulo, outros estados regulamentam o magistério por meio de normativas elaboradas durante o regime de exceção como Rio Grande do Sul, Pernambuco, Paraná, Rio de Janeiro, Minas Gerais, Acre e Ceará, conforme Ximenes identifica no artigo “

Os anos que não acabaram; o uso de estatutos jurídicos da ditadura militar na perseguição a educadores(as) no Brasil

”, que publicou na metade deste ano com a jurista Ligia Ziggiotti de Oliveira.


Veruschka de Sales Azevedo e Fabiana de Abreu (centro), professoras exoneradas via PAD


Sarau criado por Veruschka incomodava a direção


Veruschka nasceu em Sanharó, no interior de Pernambuco, e chegou a Guarulhos ainda criança, com seis irmãos. A mãe era empregada doméstica; o pai, caminhoneiro. Ela estudou na Escola Estadual Professora Maria Aparecida Rodrigues, no bairro Pimentas, em Guarulhos, e cursou história na Unesp. Concursada em 2000, deu aulas na cidade de Sertãozinho até pedir, em 2004, transferência para a escola onde estudara. “Lá, havia professores que incentivaram os alunos a buscar a universidade pública”, disse a filha Rayssa. “Daí ela veio com o sonho de fazer o mesmo que fizeram por ela.” Ficou lá mesmo depois do doutorado, concluído em 2016 na PUC-SP.


Nas aulas, discutia desigualdades, feminismo, direitos humanos e identidade negra, e aplicava a Lei 10.639, de 2003, que tornou obrigatório o ensino de história e cultura afro-brasileira. Militava na Associação Nacional de História (Anpuh), no sindicato e na Marcha Antirracista do Bairro dos Pimentas. Na escola, conduzia o Sarau Resistência: ao longo do ano, os alunos pesquisavam personalidades negras e as homenageavam com apresentações.

 “No sarau do Milton Nascimento, fizemos o Milton de açúcar, porque ele é uma pessoa doce”, lembrou o ex-aluno Thiago Gomes, hoje estudante de filosofia na USP. “Eu via alunos racistas mudarem de opinião depois do sarau.” No cursinho popular da UNEafro Brasil que Veruschka coordenou na Unifesp, Thiago ouvia dela que era “um menino de ouro”. author: Clara Saliba
title: Por que a proibição das Bets é tão importante
content:
Na sexta-feira, dia 25 de setembro, às vésperas do primeiro turno das eleições, o presidente Lula assinou a

Medida Provisória (MP) 1394

, que proíbe a atuação das bets no país. A MP é uma vitória, ainda que venha tarde.


É apenas o começo de uma batalha jurídica e regulatória que irá se desenrolar no próximo mandato eleitoral, com papel central tanto do presidente eleito quanto dos demais parlamentares.

 Afinal, deputados e senadores compõem as comissões mistas que analisam as medidas provisórias, e, para virar lei, uma MP também precisa ser aprovada pela Câmara e pelo Senado. 


Aqui, quero enaltecer o papel fundamental que

a cobertura jornalística da

Agência


Pública

 teve nessa decisão, e que minha colega Natália Viana detalha

em sua coluna da semana passada

.  


Que o vício em apostas – a ludopatia – tem um impacto grande na saúde da população, já está estabelecido, tanto em termos psicológicos quanto financeiros. Não são poucos os casos de pessoas que perdem bens materiais, se endividam e quebram relações familiares por causa das apostas.


O marido de uma amiga não tem celular desde o ano passado: foi a condição para que seguissem o relacionamento, depois de ele perder tudo o que tinham guardado e até vender o carro para seguir jogando. 


Rafael Borges Amaral, de 26 anos, perdeu a vida na batalha contra a ludopatia. A carta escrita por sua mãe, Vânia de Souza Borges, não foi ouvida pela CPI das Bets,

mas alcançou o Brasil

 e ajudou a levantar a bandeira de muitas outras famílias pela proibição das apostas online.


A saúde das pessoas é muito mais importante do que qualquer impacto econômico.

Antes de pensar no PIB ou na arrecadação tributária, é a vida que precisa ser colocada em primeiro plano

. 


Então, mesmo se proibir as bets fosse ruim para a economia, seria a decisão acertada.


Mas este não é o caso. Para a economia do país, acabar com esses jogos é bastante benéfico.


Isso porque a renda que é absorvida pelas bets não retorna em mesmo volume para a economia do país. Ela é tirada de circulação, em grande parte apropriada pelas casas de aposta, muitas das quais nem no Brasil estão.


Então, além da renda que sai do bolso das famílias e prejudica suas contas diárias, a economia do país como um todo é afetada. 


Isso porque, quando alguém vai ao mercado e gasta dinheiro comprando um produto ou contratando um serviço, esse valor retorna em maior escala para a economia. É o que chamamos de efeito multiplicador. 


Por exemplo, se eu compro R$ 100 no mercadinho, estes R$ 100 viram a renda do comerciante. Ele, por sua vez, vai gastá-la, o que gera renda para outra pessoa, que também vai gastar, e assim por diante. No final, R$100 viram muito mais em atividade econômica. A roda da economia gira.  


Mas, se eu perco estes mesmos R$ 100 num cassino online, este dinheiro não comprou nada, não gerou demanda nenhuma. E a maior parte dele não vai retornar em prêmios, vai ser retida na casa de apostas.


Um

estudo

 conduzido pelo professor Guilherme Klein para o Centro de Estudos de Macroeconomia das Desigualdades da Universidade de São Paulo (Made/USP) dimensionou o impacto das bets nesse movimento. 


A conta é a seguinte.

O Centro Celso Furtado estimou que, em 2025, houve uma transferência bruta de R$ 62,5 bilhões para as plataformas de apostas.

 Ou seja, somando tudo o que foi apostado e redistribuído em prêmios, as bets ficaram com mais de 60 bilhões para si. 


Com esse número, o professor estimou alguns cenários diferentes, com hipóteses mais ou menos otimistas sobre o papel econômico do setor de apostas, e chegou numa perda total para a economia brasileira de algo entre R$ 90,9 bi e R$ 141 bilhões de reais – ou de 0,7 a 1,1% do PIB do nosso país.


De um terço a metade do crescimento da economia brasileira em 2025. Até cinco vezes mais do que o impacto estimado para o tarifaço americano. 


A própria

Confederação Nacional do Comércio de Bens, Serviços e Turismo (CNC)

 estimou que o varejo sozinho deixou de faturar cerca de R$ 103 bilhões em 2024, devido ao direcionamento de recursos das pessoas para as bets.


Mesmo quando consideramos o ganho de arrecadação que a regulamentação das apostas trouxe, regular sai mais caro para o país do que proibir.

 No Estudo do Made, o efeito final é de uma redução entre R$ 14,6 bilhões e R$ 35,6 bilhões na arrecadação de impostos.


Isso sem nem considerar a elevação dos gastos em saúde pública para tratamento do vício em apostas. Conforme o …
